अँधेरा.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit अन्धकार (andhakāra, 'darkness'), via Prakrit अंधआर (andhaāra).

अंक.etymology: Learned borrowing (tatsama) from Sanskrit अङ्क (aṅka, 'hook, mark, sign, numerical figure'), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂enk- ('to bend, hook').

rootFamily.gloss: number (room number, phone number, shoe size)

अंडा.etymology: Inherited (tadbhava) from Sanskrit अण्ड (aṇḍa, 'egg'), via Prakrit अंड (aṇḍa).

अंदर.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian अंदर / اندر (andar, 'inside, within'), cognate with Sanskrit अन्तर (antara) and Latin inter.

अंदरूनी.etymology: Derived in Hindi from the adverb and postposition अंदर (andar, 'inside') with the Persian-origin adjectival suffix -ई (-ī) and an epenthetic -ऊन- element modeled on Persianate adjectives like بیرونی (bīrūnī, 'outer'). The base अंदर itself comes from Classical Persian اندر (andar, 'within, inside'), which continues Old Persian *antar and Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hantár, cognate with Sanskrit अन्तर् (antár, 'between, inside'). The resulting hybrid formation became standard across Hindustani for spatial and figurative 'internal' senses.

अंदाज़.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian انداز (andāz, 'measure, manner, style'), verbal stem of انداختن (andāxtan, 'to cast, project').

अक्षर.etymology: Learned Sanskrit borrowing (tatsama) अक्षर (akṣara, 'imperishable; syllable, letter'), from अ- ('not') + क्षर ('perishing').

अखरोट.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit अक्षोट (akṣoṭa, 'walnut tree or nut'), attested in classical medical and botanical treatises such as the Suśrutasaṃhitā. Through Prakrit *akkhoṭa / *akkhōḍa, the cluster -kṣ- simplified to -kh- and the intervocalic retroflex stop yielded Hindi -oṭ, giving अखरोट (akhroṭ). The Sanskrit word itself is likely an early borrowing from a Himalayan or Central Asian substrate language along mountain trade routes where Juglans regia grew.

अगर.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian اگر (agar, 'if'), from Middle Persian agar.

अगला.etymology: Formed from आगे (āge, 'ahead, in front') + adjectival suffix -ला (-lā), from Sanskrit अग्र.

rootFamily.gloss: ahead; forward; further on; in front (के आगे)

अच्छा.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit अच्छ (accha, 'clear, pure, transparent, sound'), via Prakrit अच्छ (accha).

अजनबी.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic أَجْنَبِيّ (ʾajnabiyy, 'foreigner, stranger'), via Classical Persian اجنبی.

अजीब.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic عَجِيب (ʿajīb, 'wondrous, strange, astonishing'), via Classical Persian عجیب.

अटकना.etymology: Inherited from Middle Indo-Aryan अट्टक्कइ ('is obstructed, stops').

rootFamily.gloss: to open; to unlock; to unwrap
to stop; to wait; to stay overnight (at an inn)

अटारी.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit अट्टालिका (aṭṭālikā, 'watchtower, upper-storey room'), via Prakrit अट्टालिआ (aṭṭāliā).

rootFamily.gloss: floor / storey of a building; destination

अट्ठाईस.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit अष्टाविंशति (aṣṭāviṃśati, 'twenty-eight'), an additive compound of अष्टा (aṣṭā, 'eight') and विंशति (viṃśati, 'twenty'). In Middle Indo-Aryan (Prakrit अट्टावीस / अठ्ठाईस), the labial v- between vowels elided and the nasalized vowel simplified, while the retroflex cluster -ṣṭ- assimilated to geminate -ṭṭh-. Modern Hindi preserves this geminate stop in अट्ठाईस (aṭṭhāīs).

अतिरिक्त.etymology: Learned Sanskrit borrowing (tatsama) अतिरिक्त (atirikta, 'surpassing, left over, additional'), from अति- + रिक्त.

अनजान.etymology: Formed in Indo-Aryan from privative prefix अन- ('un-, not') + जान ('known', from जाना / जानना).

अनजाने.etymology: Oblique adverbial form of अनजाना ('unknown, unwitting'), from अन- + जानना.

अनर्थ.etymology: Learned borrowing from Sanskrit अनर्थ (anartha, 'misfortune, harm, nonsense'), from अन्- ('non-, bad') + अर्थ ('purpose, benefit').

अनुबंध.etymology: Learned Sanskrit borrowing (tatsama) अनुबन्ध (anubandha, 'binding together, agreement'), from अनु- + बन्ध.

अनोखा.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit अनवेक्षित / अचक्षुष or Prakrit अणोक्ख (aṇokkha, 'unseen before, extraordinary').

अपना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit आत्मनः (ātmanaḥ, 'of oneself'), via Prakrit अप्पण (appaṇa, 'one's own').

अफ़सोस.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian افسوس (afsōs, 'regret, sorrow, alas'), from Middle Persian apsōs.

अब.etymology: Inherited from Prakrit अब्ब / एव्वं ('now, thus'), related to Sanskrit एवम्.

rootFamily.gloss: right now; just now; still / yet
then; at that time; तब तक 'until then'
when (in a statement or time clause, never a question!)

अभी.etymology: Formed from अब ('now') + emphatic particle ही ('right, very').

rootFamily.gloss: just then; at that very moment; that explains why

अभी-अभी.etymology: Formed by full reduplication of the Hindi adverb अभी (abhī, 'right now'), which itself fuses अब (ab, 'now') with the emphatic particle ही (hī). The base अब derives from Middle Indo-Aryan *ebba / Apabhraṃśa अम्ब, ultimately tracing back to Sanskrit एवम् (evam, 'thus') or अद्य (adya, 'today') influenced by pronominal temporal adverbs. Reduplication in Hindi adverbs intensifies immediacy, narrowing 'now' to 'just a second ago'.

rootFamily.gloss: right now; just now; still / yet

अभ्यास.etymology: A learned tatsama borrowing from Sanskrit अभ्यास (abhyāsa, 'repetition, practice, exercise'), formed from the prefix अभि- (abhi-, 'toward, repeatedly') and आस् (ās-, 'to sit, stay' or 'to throw/apply oneself'). Originally denoting repeated mental or physical application in Vedic study and archery, the noun entered classical philosophy (such as Yoga) and later became the everyday standard Hindi term for musical, academic, and athletic practice.

अरे.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit अरे (are, vocative interjection of surprise or calling attention).

rootFamily.gloss: oh dear!; goodness! (mild dismay or sympathy)
oh! (expressive vocative particle, especially in बाप रे!)

अलग.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit अलग्न (alagna, 'not attached, unjoined'), composed of the privative prefix अ- (a-, 'not') and लग्न (lagna, 'attached, clinging', past participle of लग्). Through Prakrit अलग्ग (alagga), the final geminate simplified in New Indo-Aryan to yield Hindi अलग (alag). Its semantic shift from 'unattached' to 'separate, distinct, extra' is shared across northern Indo-Aryan languages.

अलमारी.etymology: Borrowed from Portuguese armário ('cupboard, chest, wardrobe'), with dissimilation of r to l, ultimately from Latin armārium.

अलविदा.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic الْوَدَاع (al-wadāʿ, 'the farewell, leave-taking'), via Classical Persian الوداع.

rootFamily.gloss: to be found; to get/receive (with को); to meet (with से)

अलार्म.etymology: Borrowed from English alarm, ultimately from Italian all'arme ('to arms!').

असल.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic أَصْل (ʾaṣl, 'root, origin, reality'), via Classical Persian اصل.

rootFamily.gloss: truth (सच में? 'Really?'; सच कहूँ तो 'To tell the truth')

असली.etymology: Formed from असल (asal, 'origin, reality') + adjectival suffix -ई (-ī); Persian اصلی (aṣlī).

rootFamily.gloss: truth (सच में? 'Really?'; सच कहूँ तो 'To tell the truth')

अस्सी.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit अशीति (aśīti, 'eighty'), via Prakrit असीइ (asīi).

आँख.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit अक्षि (akṣi, 'eye'), via Prakrit अक्खि (akkhi), from PIE *h₃ekʷ- ('to see').

rootFamily.gloss: to look; to see; to check; (after -कर) to try out

आँगन.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit अङ्गण (aṅgaṇa, 'courtyard, open yard'), via Prakrit अंगण (aṅgaṇa).

आँच.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit अर्चि (arci, 'ray of light, flame'), related to the root अर्च् (arc-, 'to shine, praise'). In Prakrit, the cluster -rc- became geminate -cc- with nasalization of the preceding vowel in some dialects (अच्चि / *अंचि), which simplified with compensatory lengthening of the vowel in Hindi to yield आँच (ānch). It retains the concrete culinary sense of stove heat and flame.

आकृति.etymology: A learned tatsama borrowing from Sanskrit आकृति (ākṛti, 'form, shape, figure, appearance'), derived from the prefix आ- (ā-, 'toward') and कृति (kṛti, 'making, creation', from कृ 'to do, make'). In Sanskrit aesthetic and mathematical prose it referred both to geometric shape and human bodily form. Hindi adopted the word cleanly for artistic figures, outlines, and shapes.

आख़िर.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic آخِر (ʾāḵir, 'last, end'), via Classical Persian آخر (āxir, 'finally, after all').

आख़िरी.etymology: Derived from Arabic loanword आख़िर (ākhir, 'end, last') + Indo-Persian adjectival suffix -ई (-ī).

आगमन.etymology: A tatsama borrowing from Sanskrit आगमन (āgamana, 'coming, arrival, approach'), formed from the directional prefix आ- (ā-, 'hither, toward') and गमन (gamana, 'going', from गम् 'to go'). Because आ- reverses the motion of गम् ('to go'), the compound literally means 'coming hither'. Hindi uses it in polite, formal, and scheduled contexts such as train or guest arrivals.

आगे.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit अग्रे (agre, 'in front, ahead, first'), via Prakrit अग्गे (agge).

rootFamily.gloss: near (के पास); in one's possession ('to have')

आज.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit अद्य (adya, 'today, now'), via Prakrit अज्ज (ajja).

rootFamily.gloss: yesterday; tomorrow (tense of the verb tells which!)

आजकल.etymology: A copulative Hindi compound of आज (āj, 'today') and कल (kal, 'yesterday/tomorrow'), literally 'today and tomorrow'. आज descends from Sanskrit अद्य (adya, 'today') via Prakrit अज्ज (ajja), while कल descends from Sanskrit कल्यम् (kalyam, 'at dawn, tomorrow') via Prakrit कल्ल (kalla). Together the pair generalizes from immediate adjacent days to the broad present era, 'nowadays'.

rootFamily.gloss: yesterday; tomorrow (tense of the verb tells which!)
right now; just now; still / yet

आटा.etymology: Inherited from Middle Indo-Aryan *अट्ट (*aṭṭa, 'meal, flour'), via Prakrit अट्ट (aṭṭa).

आठ.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit अष्ट (aṣṭa, 'eight'), via Prakrit अट्ठ (aṭṭha), from PIE *oḱtṓw.

rootFamily.gloss: half past; plus a half (with numbers 3 and above)

आत्मीय.etymology: A tatsama borrowing from Sanskrit आत्मीय (ātmīya, 'belonging to oneself, intimate, dear'), derived from आत्मन् (ātman, 'self, soul') with the possessive suffix -ईय (-īya). Literally meaning 'like one's own soul', the adjective came to express deep familial or friendly warmth in Hindi literature and hospitality. It remains invariable across masculine and feminine nouns.

rootFamily.gloss: one's own (my, your, his, her, our, their)

आदत.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian عادت (ʿādat, 'habit, custom') from Arabic عَادَة (ʿāda, 'habit, practice'), derived from the triliteral root ع-و-د (ʿ-w-d, 'to return, repeat'). Because a habit is an action to which one repeatedly returns, the noun acquired the sense of settled custom or personal quirk. In Hindi it is treated as a consonant-final feminine noun.

आदमी.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian آدمی (ādamī, 'human being, descendant of Adam, man'), from Arabic آدَم (ʾādam).

आदर.etymology: Learned borrowing from Sanskrit आदर (ādara, 'regard, respect, honour'), from आ- + दर् ('to heed, respect').

आधा.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit अर्ध (ardha, 'half, part'), via Prakrit अद्ध (addha).

आधुनिक.etymology: Learned Sanskrit borrowing आधुनिक (ādhunika, 'belonging to the present, modern'), from अधुना ('now').

rootFamily.gloss: old (of things, places, memories, or friendships)

आनंद.etymology: Learned Sanskrit borrowing आनन्द (ānanda, 'bliss, delight, happiness').

rootFamily.gloss: peace of mind; cosy calm; tranquillity

आना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit आ-या (ā-yā, 'to come near, approach') / आगम्य, via Prakrit एइ / आवइ (āvaï).

rootFamily.gloss: to go; (as light verb) marks transition or completion

आप.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit आत्मन् (ātman, 'self, one's own person'), via Prakrit अप्पा (appā), grammaticalised as an honorific second-person pronoun.

आपस.etymology: Inherited from Middle Indo-Aryan reflexive stem अप्प- (appa-, from Sanskrit आत्मन् ātman, 'self').

आमने-सामने.etymology: Echo/compound adverb formed with सामने (sāmne, 'in front', from Sanskrit सम्मुख).

rootFamily.gloss: with; together with (के साथ); together (एक साथ)

आराम.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian آرام (ārām, 'rest, repose, quiet'), from Middle Persian ārām.

rootFamily.gloss: peace of mind; cosy calm; tranquillity

आवाज़.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian آواز (āwāz, 'voice, sound, call'), from Middle Persian āwāz.

rootFamily.gloss: to speak; to say; to talk

आसपास.etymology: Compound of आस (from Sanskrit आशा 'quarter, direction, nearness') + पास ('beside, near').

rootFamily.gloss: near (के पास); in one's possession ('to have')

आसमान.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian آسمان (āsmān, 'sky, heaven'), from Old Persian asman-.

आसान.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian آسان (āsān, 'easy, convenient'), from Middle Persian āsān.

आस्तीन.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian آستین (āstīn, 'sleeve'), related to Middle Persian āstēn and Old Iranian *ā-stāna- ('covering for the arm/hand', from *dasta- 'hand' or *stā-). Entering Hindustani through courtly tailoring and everyday garment vocabulary, it replaced older Indo-Aryan terms for shirt-sleeves in urban speech. The final consonant preserves its feminine grammatical gender in Hindi.

rootFamily.gloss: cloth; piece of fabric; clothes (in plural कपड़े)

इंजन.etymology: Borrowed from English engine, ultimately from Latin ingenium ('clever device').

इंतज़ार.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic اِنْتِظَار (intiẓār, 'waiting, expectation'), via Classical Persian انتظار.

rootFamily.gloss: to stop; to wait; to stay overnight (at an inn)

इंसान.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic إِنْسَان (ʾinsān, 'human being'), via Classical Persian انسان.

इज़्ज़त.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian عزت (izzat) from Arabic عِزَّة (ʿizza, 'honour, glory, self-respect').

इतना.etymology: Inherited from Prakrit एत्तिअ / इत्तण (ittaṇa, 'this much'), from Sanskrit इयत् (iyat).

rootFamily.gloss: how much; how many; what a!
a little; some; a few (in plural)

इधर-उधर.etymology: A paired spatial adverb combining Hindi इधर (idhar, 'hither, this way') and उधर (udhar, 'thither, that way'). Both components trace back to Old Indo-Aryan pronominal stems (इ- 'this' and उ- 'that') with directional suffixes related to Sanskrit -त्र (-tra) or Apabhraṃśa *-ddhar. Paired together with a hyphen, they express scattered or back-and-forth movement.

इमारत.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic عِمَارَة (ʿimāra, 'building, edifice'), via Classical Persian عمارت.

इलाक़ा.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian علاقه (alāqa) from Arabic عَلَاقَة (ʿalāqa, 'connection, attachment; district').

इशारा.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic إِشَارَة (ʾišāra, 'sign, gesture, pointing'), via Classical Persian اشاره.

इसलिए.etymology: Compound of oblique demonstrative इस ('this') + postposition लिए ('for'), literally 'for this reason'.

इसीलिए.etymology: Compound of emphatic proximal oblique इसी (isī, 'this very') + लिए ('for').

इस्तेमाल.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian استعمال (isti'māl) from Arabic اِسْتِعْمَال (istiʿmāl, 'using, employment'), from root ع-م-ل ('to work').

ईंट.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit इष्टका (iṣṭakā, 'brick'), via Prakrit इट्ठआ (iṭṭhaā).

ईमानदारी.etymology: From ईमानदार ('honest', Arabic إِيمَان īmān 'faith, trust' + Persian -दार '-holder') + abstract suffix -ई.

rootFamily.gloss: truth (सच में? 'Really?'; सच कहूँ तो 'To tell the truth')

उँगली.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit अङ्गुली (aṅgulī, 'finger, toe'), diminutive of अङ्गुल (aṅgula, 'finger, digit'), related to अङ्ग (aṅga, 'limb'). Through Prakrit अङ्गुली / उङ्गुली (with rounding of the initial vowel before the labial/velar nasal and syncope of the medial vowel), the word developed into Hindi उँगली (unglī). The nasalization of the initial vowel preserves the historical nasal cluster -ṅg-.

उगाना.etymology: Causative in -आना from उगना ('to rise, sprout'), inherited from Sanskrit उद्गमति (udgamati, 'rises, shoots up') via Prakrit उग्गमइ.

rootFamily.gloss: small leaf; herb leaf; tea leaf

उछलना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit उच्छलति (ucchalati, 'springs up, rebounds'), composed of the upward prefix उद्- (ud-, 'up, out') and शल् (śal-, 'to leap, move quickly') or चल् (cal-, 'to move'). Through Prakrit उच्छलइ (ucchalaï), the palatal geminate -cch- became aspirated -chh- in Hindi, giving the stem उछल- (uchhal-) and infinitive उछलना (uchhalnā).

rootFamily.gloss: to lift; to pick up; to wake up

उजला.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit उज्ज्वल (ujjvala, 'blazing, bright, luminous'), via Prakrit उज्जल (ujjala).

उठना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit उत्था- / उत्तिष्ठति (uttiṣṭhati, 'stands up'), via Prakrit उट्ठइ.

rootFamily.gloss: to lift; to pick up; to wake up

उठाना.etymology: Causative in -आना from उठना ('to rise, stand up'), inherited from Sanskrit उत्तिष्ठति / उत्थान (utthāna) via Prakrit उट्ठइ.

उड़ना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit उड्डयते (uḍḍayate, 'flies up'), formed from उद्- (ud-, 'upward') and डयते (ḍayate, 'flies', root डी 'to fly'). In Prakrit उड्डइ (uḍḍaï), the geminate retroflex stop -ḍḍ- simplified into the retroflex flap -ṛ- in Hindi, yielding the stem उड़- (uṛ-) and infinitive उड़ना (uṛnā). It applies equally to birds, aeroplanes, and wind-blown paper.

उड़ाना.etymology: Transitive and causative stem formed from Hindi उड़ना (uṛnā, 'to fly') by adding the causative suffix -आ (-ā-), reflecting the Sanskrit causative उड्डाययति (uḍḍāyayati, 'causes to fly up') via Prakrit उड्डावेइ (uḍḍāveï). While उड़ना describes self-propelled or passive flight, उड़ाना denotes an external agent such as wind or a person sending something into the air.

उतरना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit अवतरति (avatarati, 'descends, alights, crosses down'), via Prakrit ओतरइ / उत्तरइ.

उतारना.etymology: Transitive/causative inherited from Sanskrit अवतारयति (avatārayati, 'causes to descend, takes off').

rootFamily.gloss: to come down; to get off (a train); to descend

उत्तरी.etymology: Formed in Hindi from उत्तर (uttar, 'north') with the relational adjectival suffix -ई (-ī). The noun उत्तर is a tatsama borrowing from Sanskrit उत्तर (uttara, 'upper, higher, northern'), comparative of उद् (ud, 'up'), because traditional Indian geography oriented maps or mental space toward the east or north toward the Himalayas. Thus 'higher' came to mean 'northern'.

उत्सव.etymology: A tatsama borrowing from Sanskrit उत्सव (utsava, 'festival, jubilation, enterprise'), derived from उद्- (ud-, 'up, out') and सव (sava, 'impulse, pressing, generation', from सु 'to press, impel'). Originally referring to a solemn Soma-pressing or joyous undertaking in Vedic ritual, it broadened in classical Sanskrit to mean any public feast or festival. In modern Hindi it is the standard word for civic and cultural festivals.

उत्सुकता.etymology: Learned Sanskrit borrowing उत्सुकता (utsukatā, 'eagerness, curiosity'), from उत्सुक ('eager') + -ता ('-ness').

उदास.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit उदासीन / उदास (udāsa, 'sitting apart, detached, dejected').

उनतीस.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit एकोनत्रिंशत् (ekonatriṃśat, 'one less than thirty'), via Prakrit एगूणतीसा -> उनतीस.

उन्नीस.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit ऊनविंशति (ūnaviṃśati, 'one less than twenty'), via Prakrit उणवीस.

उम्र.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian عمر (ʿumr, 'life, age') from Arabic عُمْر (ʿumr, 'lifetime, span of life, age'), derived from the root ع-م-ر (ʿ-m-r, 'to live long, inhabit, prosper'). While Arabic and Persian treat it as a general abstract noun for lifespan, Hindustani adapted it as a feminine noun meaning both biological age and one's whole life. It is ubiquitous in everyday conversation.

उम्रदराज़.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian عمردراز (ʿumr-darāz, literally 'long of life'), from Arabic عُمْر ('life, age') + Persian دراز ('long').

rootFamily.gloss: old (of things, places, memories, or friendships)

उलझना.etymology: Inherited from Middle Indo-Aryan *ullajjha- / Prakrit *ulajjhaï, likely a back-formation or metathesized derivative connected to Sanskrit उद्- (ud-, 'out') and रज्जू (rajju, 'rope') or लज्ज् / रझ् ('to cling, entangle'), or Sanskrit अवलग् + य. In New Indo-Aryan the stem उलझ- (ulajh-) paired antonymically with सुलझ- (sulajh-, 'to be untangled'), where उ- and सु- function like opposing prefixes.

उलटा.etymology: Inherited from Middle Indo-Aryan *ulluṭṭa / Prakrit उल्लट्ट (ullaṭṭa, 'turned over, reversed'), connected to Sanskrit अवलुण्ठित (avaluṇṭhita) or उल्लुण्ठित (ulluṇṭhita, 'rolled over, inverted', from लुण्ठ् 'to roll'). Loss of the nasal and simplification of the cluster left a retroflex -ṭ-, giving the verbal base उलट- (ulaṭ-, 'to overturn') and the participial adjective उलटा (ulṭā). It contrasts directly with सीधा (sīdhā, 'straight, right-side up').

उस्ताद.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian استاد (ustād, 'master, teacher, skilled artisan'), continuing Middle Persian ōstād / awestād and Old Iranian *ava-stāta- ('established, proficient, well-versed', from the root *stā- 'to stand'). In South Asian cultural life the title became deeply rooted in classical music, craft guilds, and mentorship traditions. Hindi treats it as an invariable masculine noun.

ऊँचा.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit उच्च (ucca, 'high, lofty, loud'), derived from the prefix उद्- (ud-, 'up'). In Prakrit उच्च (ucca), spontaneous nasalization (common before geminates in Indo-Aryan) yielded *उंच (*uñca), which subsequently underwent compensatory vowel lengthening when the nasalized cluster simplified, producing Hindi ऊँचा (ūnchā). It covers physical height as well as high musical pitch or loud volume.

rootFamily.gloss: upstairs; above; on top of (के ऊपर)

ऊनी.etymology: Derived from ऊन ('wool', inherited from Sanskrit ऊर्णा ūrṇā, from PIE *h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂ 'wool') + suffix -ई.

ऊपर.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit उपरि (upari, 'above, over, upward'), via Prakrit उप्परि (uppari).

ऊपरी.etymology: Derived in Hindi from the adverb and postposition ऊपर (ūpar, 'above, on top') by adding the relational adjectival suffix -ई (-ī). The base ऊपर descends from Sanskrit उपरि (upari, 'above, upon') via Prakrit उवरि / उप्परि, cognate with Greek ὑπέρ (hypér) and English 'over'. Unlike ऊँचा ('tall/high'), ऊपरी specifically indicates relative upper position or surface layer.

rootFamily.gloss: upstairs; above; on top of (के ऊपर)

एक.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit एक (eka, 'one, single, alone'), via Prakrit एक्क (ekka), from PIE *óynos / *óykos.

rootFamily.gloss: one each; one by one; every single

एक-एक.etymology: Productive Indo-Aryan distributive reduplication of एक (ek, 'one'), itself inherited via Prakrit इक्क / एक्क (ikka / ekka) from Sanskrit एक (eka, 'one, single, alone', from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Háykas).

history.meaning: one each, one by one, every single

एक-एक.notes: Followed by a singular noun (एक-एक कमरा, 'every single room / one room each'), and pairs with करके in एक-एक करके ('one by one').

एकदम.etymology: Compound of एक ('one') + Persian दम (dam, 'breath, moment'), literally 'in a single breath'.

rootFamily.gloss: completely; absolutely; (with नहीं) not at all

एक्सप्रेस.etymology: Borrowed from English 'express' (short for 'express train' or 'express service'), which entered Indian English and Hindi through the nineteenth-century expansion of the Indian railway network. The English word itself derives from Old French expres and Latin expressus ('distinct, clear, dispatched for a special purpose', past participle of exprimere). In Hindi it functions invariantly both attributively before ट्रेन and elliptically as a train designation.

rootFamily.gloss: fast; heavy (rain); strong/sharp (salt, spice, sun, sound)

एप्रन.etymology: Borrowed from English 'apron' into modern urban Hindi through commercial bakeries, cafés, and home-economics vocabulary. English 'apron' itself originated in Middle English as 'a napron' (from Old French naperon, diminutive of nape 'tablecloth', ultimately Latin mappa), which lost its initial n- by metanalysis ('a napron' became 'an apron'). In Hindi it is a masculine consonant-final noun.

rootFamily.gloss: cloth; piece of fabric; clothes (in plural कपड़े)

ऐतिहासिक.etymology: A learned tatsama borrowing from Sanskrit ऐतिहासिक (aitihāsika, 'historical, traditional'), formed by vriddhi vowel strengthening (इ -> ऐ) from इतिहास (itihāsa, 'history, traditional account') with the suffix -इक (-ika). The base इतिहास literally means 'thus indeed it was' (इति + ह + आस). Hindi uses ऐतिहासिक across both scholarly historiography and heritage conservation.

rootFamily.gloss: old (of things, places, memories, or friendships)

ऐसा.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit ईदृश (īdṛśa, 'of this kind, such'), via Prakrit एरिस / अइस (aïsa).

rootFamily.gloss: what kind of; how (in quality or state)

ऑपरेटर.etymology: Borrowed from English 'operator' during the era of telegraphy, manual telephone switchboards, and railway communications in India. The English noun comes from Late Latin operātor ('worker, doer'), derived from Latin operārī ('to work, operate') and opus ('work'). In Hindi it remains an invariable masculine agent noun.

ओर.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit अवर (avara, 'lower, hinder, nearer') or अपर (apara, 'other, further'), via Prakrit ओर (ora, 'side, edge, direction'). Contraction of the sequence -ava- to -o- in Middle Indo-Aryan yielded ओर, parallel to Marathi ओढ / ओर. In modern Hindi it functions both as a feminine noun meaning 'side/end' and as the core of the compound postposition की ओर ('toward').

ओवन.etymology: Borrowed from English oven, from Old English ofen.

ओह.etymology: An expressive vocal interjection shared widely across Indo-European and South Asian languages, reinforced in modern Hindi dialogue by both native exclamation patterns (अहो / ओहो) and English conversational 'oh'. In Sanskrit, parallel exclamations such as ओ (o) and अहो (aho) marked sudden realization or emotion. In contemporary spoken Hindi, ओह expresses surprise, sudden alarm, or warm gratitude.

rootFamily.gloss: oh!; hey!; wait a moment! (surprise or sudden realisation)

औज़ार.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian اوزار (awzār, 'tools') from Arabic أَوْزَار (ʾawzār) / Middle Persian abzār ('instrument, tool').

औपचारिक.etymology: Learned Sanskrit borrowing औपचारिक (aupacārika, 'ceremonial, formal'), from उपचार.

और.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit अपर (apara, 'other, another, further'), via Prakrit अवर (avara) -> और.

rootFamily.gloss: with; together with (के साथ); together (एक साथ)

कंधा.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit स्कन्ध (skandha, 'shoulder, trunk of a tree'), via Prakrit कंध (kandha).

कंप्यूटर.etymology: Borrowed from English computer, from Latin computāre ('to reckon together').

कंबल.etymology: Inherited/borrowed from Sanskrit कम्बल (kambala, 'woollen blanket or cloth').

कटना.etymology: Intransitive/passive-sense stem derived in Indo-Aryan from Sanskrit कृत् (kṛt-, 'to cut') via the passive or Prakrit stem कट्ट- (kaṭṭa-, from Sanskrit कर्तित kartita / कृत्यते kṛtyate). While the lengthened-vowel stem काटना (kāṭnā) became the active transitive verb 'to cut', the short-vowel stem कटना (kaṭnā) expresses 'to get cut, be sliced'. This short/long vowel alternation is a classic Indo-Aryan transitivity pair.

कटोरा.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit कटोर (kaṭora, 'cup, bowl, vessel') or कटोरी (kaṭorī), attested in late Sanskrit and Prakrit कडोर (kaḍora), possibly from a Dravidian or Munda substrate word for a hollowed cup or shell (compare Sanskrit कठोर 'hard' or कपाल 'cup'). Maintaining the -ओर- stem and masculine -आ ending, it became standard Hindi कटोरा (kaṭorā) for a deep medium or large bowl.

कड़वा.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit कटुक (kaṭuka, 'sharp, pungent, bitter'), via Prakrit कडुअ (kaḍua).

rootFamily.gloss: sweet; pleasant (of voice, music, or scent)

कड़ी.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit कटि / कटक ('link, ring, ridge-piece') via Prakrit कडिआ (kaḍiā).

कतरा.etymology: Derived from the Hindi verbal root कतरना (katarnā, 'to clip, shear, slice finely'), which descends from Sanskrit कर्तति / कर्तयति (kartati / kartayati, 'cuts, clips', from कृत्) via Prakrit कत्तरइ (kattaraï). The agentive/resultative noun कतरा (katrā) denotes a small clipped piece, flake, or sliver, especially in culinary contexts like sliced almonds or pistachios. It is distinct in both spelling and origin from Arabic-derived क़तरा ('drop').

कतार.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian قطار (qatār, 'row, string of camels, line') from Arabic قِطَار (qiṭār, 'string, file, train of camels'), related to the root ق-ط-ر (q-ṭ-r, 'to tie in a file, drip in sequence'). From camel caravans moving in single file along desert routes, the word broadened in Persian and Hindustani to any orderly row of seats, objects, or waiting people. In Hindi it is a feminine consonant-final noun.

कप.etymology: Borrowed from English cup, ultimately from Late Latin cuppa.

कपड़ा.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit कर्पट (karpaṭa, 'patched garment, piece of cloth'), via Prakrit कप्पड (kappaḍa).

कबीर.etymology: From Arabic كَبِير (kabīr, 'great, noble'), famous across India through the poet-saint Kabir of Varanasi.

कब्ज़ा.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic قَبْضَة (qabḍa, 'grip, handle, hinge'), via Classical Persian قبضه.

कभी.etymology: Formed from कब ('when?', from Sanskrit कदा) + emphatic particle ही.

rootFamily.gloss: when (in a statement or time clause, never a question!)

कभी-कभी.etymology: Attenuative reduplication of कभी (kabhī, 'ever, at some time'), which evolved in Early Hindi by fusing कब (kab, 'when', < Prakrit कब्ब < Sanskrit कदा kadā) with the emphatic particle ही (hī, producing aspirated -भ-).

morphemes.meaning: ever, at some time (< कब + ही)

कभी-कभी.notes: Repeating an indefinite time word in Hindi turns 'at some time' (कभी) into 'from time to time, occasionally' (कभी-कभी).

कम.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian کم (kam, 'little, few, less'), from Old Persian kamna-.

rootFamily.gloss: a little; some; a few (in plural)

कमरा.etymology: Borrowed from Portuguese câmara ('room, chamber'), ultimately from Latin camera and Ancient Greek καμάρα (kamára, 'vaulted chamber').

कमाल.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian کمال (kamāl) from Arabic كَمَال (kamāl, 'perfection, excellence').

कमी.etymology: Formed in Persian/Hindi from कम (Persian کم kam, 'little, few') + abstract feminine suffix -ई (-ī).

rootFamily.gloss: less; little; fewer; कम से कम 'at least'

कमीज़.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic قَمِيص (qamīṣ) / Portuguese camisa, ultimately from Late Latin camisia ('shirt').

rootFamily.gloss: cloth; piece of fabric; clothes (in plural कपड़े)

कम्पास.etymology: Borrowed from English 'compass' during the colonial-era introduction of modern cartography, surveying, and school geometry in India. English 'compass' derives from Old French compas ('circle, pair of dividers, measure') and Vulgar Latin *compassāre ('to pace out, measure with steps', from com- + passus 'step'). In Hindi it is an invariable masculine noun covering both directional and drafting instruments.

करना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit करोति / कृ (karoti, 'does, makes'), via Prakrit करइ (karaï), from PIE *kʷer- ('to make, form').

rootFamily.gloss: to be; to become; to happen
to make; to prepare; to build

कराना.etymology: Causative of करना, formed within Indo-Aryan with causative suffix -आ- (-ā-).

कल.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit कल्यम् (kalyam, 'at daybreak, tomorrow/yesterday'), via Prakrit कल्ल (kalla).

कला.etymology: A tatsama borrowing from Sanskrit कला (kalā, 'small part, sixteenth part of the moon, skill, art'). In classical Indian texts such as the Kāmasūtra and Purāṇas, the 'sixty-four arts' (चतुःषष्टि कलाः) encompassed music, painting, architecture, and culinary craft. Hindi retained the word as a feminine noun for every form of creative skill and fine art.

कलाकृति.etymology: A modern Sanskritized compound (tatpuruṣa) formed from कला (kalā, 'art') and कृति (kṛti, 'work, creation, deed', from Sanskrit कृ 'to do, make'). Literally 'a creation of art', it corresponds directly to the English phrase 'work of art' or 'artwork'. It behaves as a feminine -इ noun in Hindi.

कसना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit कषति / कर्षति (karṣati, 'draws tight, pulls'), via Prakrit कस्सइ (kassaï).

कहना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit कथयति (kathayati, 'tells, relates, speaks'), via Prakrit कहेइ (kaheï).

rootFamily.gloss: to speak; to say; to talk

कहाँ.etymology: Inherited from Prakrit कहँ (kahã, 'where?'), from Sanskrit कुत्र / कस्मिन्.

कहानी.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit कथानिका (kathānikā, 'little tale'), from कथा (kathā, 'story'), via Prakrit कहाणी (kahāṇī).

कहीं.etymology: Formed from कहाँ ('where') + emphatic suffix -ईं (from ही).

rootFamily.gloss: right here; in this very place
someone; anyone; any (before singular count noun)

क़द.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic قَدّ (qadd, 'stature, size, figure'), via Classical Persian قد.

क़दम.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic قَدَم (qadam, 'foot, step, pace'), via Classical Persian قدم.

rootFamily.gloss: to walk; to go; to move; to come along

क़लम.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian قلم (qalam, 'reed pen, stylus') from Arabic قَلَم (qalam, 'pen'), which itself was borrowed in antiquity from Ancient Greek κάλαμος (kálamos, 'reed, reed pen', ultimately cognate with Sanskrit कलम 'rice/reed'). As reed pens were the primary instrument of calligraphy and administrative correspondence across South Asia, the word entered everyday Hindi alongside स्याही ('ink').

क़ानून.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic قَانُون (qānūn, 'canon, law, code'), ultimately from Ancient Greek κανών (kanṓn, 'measuring rod, rule').

क़ानूनी.etymology: Formed from क़ानून (qānūn, 'law') + adjectival suffix -ई; Persian قانونی (qānūnī).

क़िस्मत.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian قسمت (qismat, 'portion, lot, destiny') from Arabic قِسْمَة (qisma, 'division, allotted share, fate'), derived from the root ق-س-م (q-s-m, 'to divide, apportion'). From the concept of one's allotted share in life, the noun evolved to mean 'destiny' or 'luck', and even entered English in the nineteenth century as 'kismet'. In Hindi it is a feminine noun.

क़ीमत.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian قیمت (qīmat) from Arabic قِيمَة (qīma, 'value, worth, price').

क़ीमती.etymology: Derived from क़ीमत ('price, value', from Arabic قِيمَة qīma) + adjectival suffix -ई.

rootFamily.gloss: old (of things, places, memories, or friendships)

का.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit कृत (kṛta, 'done by, belonging to'), via Prakrit कर / कअ -> का/के/की.

rootFamily.gloss: near (के पास); in one's possession ('to have')
one's own (my, your, his, her, our, their)

काँच.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit काच (kāca, 'glass, crystal, quartz'), via Prakrit काच / *कंच (*kañca), which acquired spontaneous nasalization and compensatory lengthening in Hindi to become काँच (kānch). The Sanskrit word already denoted both clear rock crystal and manufactured glass beads or vessels in ancient texts. In modern Hindi it specifically names glass as a substance, distinct from शीशा ('mirror/pane').

काँपना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit कम्पते (kampate, 'trembles, shakes'), via Prakrit कंपइ (kampaï).

काउंटर.etymology: Borrowed from English counter, from Anglo-Norman countour ('counting desk').

काग़ज़.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian کاغذ (kāġaz, 'paper'), ultimately borrowed via Sogdian from Central Asian paper-trade terminology.

rootFamily.gloss: slip of paper; short written note; chit

काग़ज़ी.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian کاغذی (kāġazī, 'made of paper, documentary').

काटना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit कर्तयति (kartayati, 'cuts, slices'), via Prakrit कट्टइ (kaṭṭaï).

कान.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit कर्ण (karṇa, 'ear'), tracing back to Proto-Indo-Iranian *karnás ('ear'). Through Prakrit कण्ण (kaṇṇa), the retroflex nasal geminate -ṇṇ- simplified with compensatory lengthening of the preceding vowel, yielding Hindi कान (kān). It is one of the most basic anatomical nouns in Indo-Aryan.

काफ़ी.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian کافی (kāfī, 'sufficient, adequate') from Arabic كَافٍ / كَافِي (kāfin / kāfī, active participle of كَفَى kafā, 'to suffice, be enough'). Originally meaning 'sufficient', it widened in colloquial Hindustani to function as an adverbial intensifier meaning 'quite, considerably, fairly'. Note the nuqta on फ़, distinguishing it from English loanword कॉफ़ी ('coffee').

काम.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit कर्मन् (karman, 'deed, action, work'), via Prakrit कम्म (kamma) with compensatory vowel lengthening.

cognates.meaning: Sanskrit borrowing from the same word

कारण.etymology: Learned Sanskrit borrowing कारण (kāraṇa, 'cause, reason, motive'), from कृ ('to do, make').

कारीगरी.etymology: Derived from कारीगर (kārīgar, 'artisan, skilled craftsman') with the abstract feminine suffix -ई (-ī). The base कारीगर is borrowed from Classical Persian کاریگر (kārīgar), formed from کار (kār, 'work, deed', Old Persian *kāra-, cognate with Sanskrit कार्य) and the agentive suffix -गर (-gar). Thus कारीगरी denotes the skill, precision, and beauty of handmade or engineered work.

कार्ड.etymology: Borrowed from English card, ultimately from Latin charta and Greek χάρτης (khártēs, 'leaf of papyrus').

rootFamily.gloss: slip of paper; short written note; chit

कार्डिगन.etymology: Borrowed from English cardigan, named after the seventh Earl of Cardigan.

कार्यक्रम.etymology: A modern Sanskritized compound (tatpuruṣa) composed of कार्य (kārya, 'work, affair, task', gerundive of कृ 'to do') and क्रम (krama, 'order, sequence, course'). Literally 'order of proceedings', it was coined and popularized in standard Hindi to translate 'programme', 'agenda', and 'scheduled event'. It is an invariable consonant-final masculine noun.

कार्यशाला.etymology: Learned Sanskrit compound कार्यशाला (kāryaśālā): कार्य ('work, task') + शाला ('hall, room, house').

कार्यालय.etymology: A modern tatsama-style sandhi compound formed from कार्य (kārya, 'work, business') and आलय (ālaya, 'abode, house, place', from आ + ली 'to settle'). Literally 'place of work', it became the standard administrative Hindi equivalent for Persian-derived दफ़्तर (daftar) and English 'office'. Vowel sandhi merges the final -a of कार्य and initial ā- of आलय into -ā-.

काला.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit काल (kāla, 'black, dark blue'), via Prakrit काल (kāla).

काव्या.etymology: From Sanskrit काव्या / काव्य (kāvya, 'poetry, lyric composition, wisdom of a seer'), from कवि ('poet, sage').

rootFamily.gloss: Mohan (warm, slightly absent-minded owner of Aangan Haveli)
Pratap (longtime caretaker and handyman at Aangan Haveli)
Diya (young morning cook and baker at Aangan Haveli)

कि.etymology: Borrowed/converged from Classical Persian که (ki, 'that, who, when'), reinforced by Indo-Aryan किम्.

कितना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit कियत् (kiyat, 'how much?'), via Prakrit केत्तिअ / कित्तण.

rootFamily.gloss: so much; this much; so (before an adjective)

किताब.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic كِتَاب (kitāb, 'book, writing'), from root ك-ت-ب (k-t-b, 'to write'), via Classical Persian کتاب.

किनारा.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian کناره (kināra, 'side, edge, shore, border').

किराया.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian کرایه (kirāya) from Arabic كِرَاء (kirāʾ, 'hire, rent, fare').

कुंडी.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit कुण्डल / कुण्डी (kuṇḍī, 'ring, loop, metal catch'), via Prakrit कुंडी.

कुछ.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit किञ्चित् (kiñcit, 'something, a little'), via Prakrit किंपि / किच्छु (kicchu).

rootFamily.gloss: someone; anyone; any (before singular count noun)
a little; some; a few (in plural)

कुदरत.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian قدرت (qudrat, 'power, ability, nature, providence') from Arabic قُدْرَة (qudra, 'power, omnipotence, creative capacity'), from the root ق-د-ر (q-d-r, 'to have power, measure'). In Persian and Urdu-Hindi usage, 'divine creative power' shifted seamlessly to mean 'Nature' itself as an active force. It takes feminine agreement in Hindi.

कुर्सी.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian کرسی (kursī) from Arabic كُرْسِيّ (kursiyy, 'chair, seat, throne'), ultimately Aramaic/Akkadian.

कुल.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic كُلّ (kull, 'all, whole, total'), via Classical Persian کل (kul), reinforced by Sanskrit कुल ('whole group').

कूड़ेदान.etymology: Hybrid compound of Hindi कूड़ा (kūṛā, 'sweepings, rubbish') + Persian suffix -दान (-dān, 'receptacle, holder').

कृपया.etymology: Learned Sanskrit instrumental singular कृपया (kṛpayā, literally 'with kindness, out of grace'), from कृपा ('grace, kindness').

rootFamily.gloss: just; a little; kindly (polite request softener)

केक.etymology: Borrowed from English cake, ultimately from Old Norse kaka.

केतली.etymology: Nativised borrowing from English kettle with Hindi feminine suffix -ई, from Old Norse ketill.

कैफ़े.etymology: Borrowed via English café from French café ('coffee; coffeehouse').

कैसा.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit कीदृश (kīdṛśa, 'of what sort?'), via Prakrit केरिस / कइस (kaïsa).

कॉपी.etymology: Borrowed from English 'copy' (originally via Old French copie and Latin cōpia, 'abundance, transcript, duplicate'). In Indian English and Hindi school culture, 'copy' came to mean specifically a ruled exercise book or notebook (from 'copybook'), alongside its standard sense of a duplicate or sheet of music. Ending in -ई, it inflects regularly as a feminine noun (कॉपियाँ).

कॉफ़ी.etymology: Borrowed from English coffee, via Dutch koffie and Ottoman Turkish kahve from Arabic قَهْوَة (qahwa).

कॉर्ड.etymology: Borrowed from English 'chord' in Western classical and modern music instruction in India. English 'chord' is an altered spelling (influenced by Latin chorda 'string') of earlier 'cord', shortened from 'accord' (from Old French acorder and Latin accordāre, 'to be in harmony', literally 'heart to heart' from cor 'heart'). In Hindi it is an invariable masculine noun.

कॉलर.etymology: Borrowed from English 'collar' via modern tailoring and shirt-making terminology in South Asia. English 'collar' comes from Old French colier and Latin collāre ('neckband, collar'), derived from collum ('neck'). Adopted into everyday Hindi as an invariable masculine noun, it covers both shirt collars and jacket lapels.

को.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit कक्षे / कृते ('at the side of; for the sake of'), reduced in Apabhramsha to कहुँ -> को.

कोई.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit कोऽपि (ko'pi, 'someone, anyone'), via Prakrit कोवि (kovi).

कोट.etymology: Borrowed from English coat ('sleeved outer garment, suit jacket'), which entered Middle English from Old French cote ('tunic, overgarment'), ultimately of Frankish origin (*kotta, 'coarse woollen cloak').

history.meaning: outer tunic -> tailored jacket or overcoat

कोट.notes: Masculine in Hindi (मेरा कोट); English alveolar -t is adapted regularly with retroflex ट (koṭ).

कोना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit कोण (koṇa, 'angle, corner'), via Prakrit कोण (koṇa).

rootFamily.gloss: side; next to (के बगल में / बगल वाला 'adjacent, side')
middle; centre (के बीच 'between / in the middle of')

कोमलता.etymology: A tatsama borrowing from Sanskrit कोमलता (komalatā, 'softness, tenderness, delicacy'), formed from the adjective कोमल (komala, 'soft, tender, delicate') with the abstract feminine suffix -ता (-tā, analogous to Latin -tās and English -ty). In musical and literary Hindi, कोमलता expresses gentle touch, soft phrasing, or tenderness of manner.

कोयला.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit कोकिल (kokila) or more directly Middle Indo-Aryan *koïla / *koyala, ultimately related to Old Indo-Aryan *kokila- / *kūla- ('glowing ember, blackened wood'; compare Prakrit कोइल / कोयल koïla, 'charcoal'). Note the exact phonetic merger with कोयला from *koïla in northern Indo-Aryan, giving Hindi कोयला (koylā) for both mineral coal and artist's charcoal.

कोरा.etymology: Inherited Indo-Aryan adjective कोरा (korā, 'unbleached, untouched, blank, sheer').

कौन.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit कः पुनः (kaḥ punaḥ, 'who then?'), contracted via Prakrit कवण (kavaṇa) to कौन.

rootFamily.gloss: someone; anyone; any (before singular count noun)

क्या.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit किम् (kim, 'what?'), via Prakrit किअ / काइं, from PIE *kʷís.

क्या-क्या.etymology: Distributive reduplication of क्या ('what?'), a hallmark of Hindi question syntax asking for an itemized list.

rootFamily.gloss: one each; one by one; every single

क्यों.etymology: Inherited from Prakrit किउँ (kiũ, 'how? why?'), from Sanskrit किम् पुनः.

क्योंकि.etymology: Compound of क्यों ('why') + कि ('that'), formed on the model of Persian چونکه (čūn-ki).

rootFamily.gloss: that (introducing a clause); or (in quick spoken questions)

क्रम.etymology: A tatsama borrowing from Sanskrit क्रम (krama, 'step, stride, regular order, succession'), derived from the verbal root क्रम् (kram-, 'to step, stride, proceed'). From the physical image of one footstep following another evenly, क्रम came to signify systematic sequence, serial order, and arrangement. In Hindi it is an invariable consonant-final masculine noun.

rootFamily.gloss: number (room number, phone number, shoe size)

क्रीम.etymology: Borrowed from English 'cream' into modern Hindi culinary and colour vocabulary. English 'cream' derives from Old French cresme, blending Late Latin crāma ('cream') and Christian Latin chrīsma ('anointing oil', from Greek χρῖσμα). In Hindi it is treated as a feminine noun and is frequently used attributively with रंग ('colour') to describe off-white paper or fabric.

क्लास.etymology: Borrowed from English class ('school group, lesson, railway carriage grade'), adapted via seventeenth-century French classe from Classical Latin classis ('division of Roman citizens, fleet, school group').

history.meaning: civic division -> group of students, lesson

क्लास.notes: Feminine in everyday Hindi (मेरी पियानो क्लास, 'my piano class'), influenced by feminine कक्षा (kakṣā, 'classroom, class').

खट-खट.etymology: Native Indo-Aryan echoic/onomatopoeic reduplication खट-खट imitating sharp knocking against wood or metal.

खड़ा.etymology: Inherited from Prakrit खड्ड / खड (khaḍa, 'erect, standing upright'), related to Sanskrit स्तब्ध.

rootFamily.gloss: to stop; to wait; to stay overnight (at an inn)

खनक.etymology: An expressive onomatopoeic Indo-Aryan noun paired with the verb खनकना (khanaknā, 'to clink, jingle, ring'), formed on the imitative root खन-खन (khan-khan) representing the crisp sound of metal, glass, or porcelain striking lightly, with the sound-verb suffix -क (-k). Parallel imitative formations in Sanskrit include खणखणायते (khaṇakhaṇāyate, 'tinkles, clinks'). In Hindi it is a feminine noun.

ख़त्म.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic خَتْم (ḵatm, 'sealing, conclusion, completion'), via Classical Persian ختم.

ख़बर.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian خبر (xabar) from Arabic خَبَر (ḵabar, 'news, report, message').

ख़याल.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian خیال (khayāl, 'thought, imagination, idea') from Arabic خَيَال (khayāl, 'image, apparition, imagination, thought'), derived from the root خ-ي-ل (kh-y-l, 'to imagine, suppose'). In Hindustani it became one of the most versatile everyday nouns for 'thought, opinion, care, or attention', and also names a major genre of Hindustani classical vocal music. It is masculine.

ख़राब.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic خَرَاب (ḵarāb, 'ruined, desolate, broken'), via Classical Persian خراب.

ख़रीददार.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian خریدار (xarīdār, 'buyer, customer'), from خرید ('purchase') + agentive -دار.

ख़रीदना.etymology: Denominative verb from Classical Persian خرید (xarīd, 'purchase; bought'), past stem of خریدن (xarīdan, 'to buy'), cognate with Sanskrit क्रीणाति (krīṇāti).

ख़र्च.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian خرج (kharj, 'expenditure, outlay', often pronounced kharch in Persianate South Asia) from Arabic خَرْج (kharj, 'output, expense, tax'), derived from the root خ-ر-ج (kh-r-j, 'to go out'). Just as English 'expense' literally means 'paying out', Arabic kharj meant money going out. In Hindi the devoiced final consonant gives ख़र्च (kharch) as a masculine noun.

ख़ाली.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic خَالٍ / خَالِي (ḵālī, 'empty, vacant, free'), via Classical Persian خالی.

ख़ास.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic خَاصّ (ḵāṣṣ, 'special, private, select'), via Classical Persian خاص.

ख़ुद.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian خود (xwad / xud, 'self, oneself'), cognate with Sanskrit स्व (sva) and English self.

rootFamily.gloss: one's own (my, your, his, her, our, their)

ख़ुशबू.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian خوشبو (xušbū, 'fragrant; fragrance'), from خوش (xuš, 'sweet, pleasant') + بو (bū, 'scent').

ख़ुशी.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian خوشی (xušī, 'happiness, gladness'), from خوش (xuš, 'happy, pleasant') + -ई.

rootFamily.gloss: peace of mind; cosy calm; tranquillity

ख़ुशी-ख़ुशी.etymology: Adverbial reduplication of ख़ुशी (xušī, 'happiness, pleasure', from Classical Persian خوشی).

ख़ून.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian خون (xūn, 'blood'), from Middle Persian xōn.

ख़ूब.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian خوب (xūb, 'good, fair, well, plentiful'), cognate with Sanskrit सु-.

ख़्याल.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian خیال (xayāl) from Arabic خَيَال (ḵayāl, 'imagination, thought, care').

rootFamily.gloss: mind; heart; mood / inclination (मन करना 'to feel like')

खाना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit खादति (khādati, 'chews, eats'), via Prakrit खाइ (khāi).

खिंचना.etymology: Intransitive passive-sense stem corresponding to the transitive verb खींचना (khīnchnā, 'to pull, draw'), displaying the regular Indo-Aryan shortening of the stem vowel (ई -> इ) to mark intransitivity. The base खींचना likely derives from Middle Indo-Aryan *khinc- / *kheñc- (compare Prakrit खंचइ / खेंचइ, 'pulls, drags'), possibly connected to Sanskrit कर्षति (karṣati, 'drags') via regional Prakrit developments.

खिड़की.etymology: Inherited from Middle Indo-Aryan खडक्किआ (khaḍakkiā, 'small side door, shuttered opening'), of early Indic vernacular origin.

खिलना.etymology: Inherited from Middle Indo-Aryan *khillaï / Prakrit खिल्लइ ('opens up, blossoms, expands'), possibly related to Sanskrit स्फल् / खुलति (khulati) or a regional Indo-Aryan root *khil- ('to open, burst into bloom'). From botanical blossoming, the verb naturally extended in Hindi to joyful facial expressions and luminous musical notes blooming into clarity, especially in the compound खिल उठना.

खिलाड़ी.etymology: Derived within Indo-Aryan from खेल (khela, 'sport, play', Sanskrit खेलति khelati) + agentive suffix -आड़ी (-āṛī).

rootFamily.gloss: fast; heavy (rain); strong/sharp (salt, spice, sun, sound)

खिसकना.etymology: Inherited Indo-Aryan motion verb खिसकना ('to slip, shift aside').

rootFamily.gloss: to tilt; to incline; to bow
to step back; to move aside

खिसकाना.etymology: Transitive/causative verb formed with -आ (-ā-) from the intransitive stem खिसकना (khisaknā, 'to slip away, budge, slide'), which derives from Middle Indo-Aryan *khisakka- / *khasakka- (compare Prakrit खसइ, 'slips, gives way'). Its ultimate root is connected with Sanskrit स्कन्दति / स्खलति ('slips, stumbles') or an expressive Indo-Aryan motion root *khas-. In modern Hindi it specifically means shifting something smoothly across a surface.

rootFamily.gloss: to remove; to move aside; to clear away
to put; to place; to keep

खींचना.etymology: Inherited from Middle Indo-Aryan *kheñcaï / *khīñcaï ('pulls, draws'), parallel to Prakrit खेंचइ and connected regionally with Sanskrit कर्षति (karṣati, 'draws, pulls') or an Indo-Aryan expressive stem *khinc-. Nasalization and lengthening of the root vowel yielded Hindi खींचना (khīnchnā). It covers pulling cords, drawing lines, and even taking photographs (तस्वीर खींचना).

rootFamily.gloss: to hold; to catch; to grasp

खुदना.etymology: Intransitive/passive inherited from Sanskrit क्षुद्यते / खनति, via Prakrit खुद्दइ ('is dug, is carved').

rootFamily.gloss: to carve; to sculpt; to whittle

खुलना.etymology: Inherited Middle Indo-Aryan intransitive खुलइ (khullaï, 'opens, comes untied'), paired with transitive खोलना.

rootFamily.gloss: to open; to unlock; to unwrap

खूँटी.etymology: Feminine diminutive of खूँटा (khūnṭā, 'wooden stake, peg'), inherited from Middle Indo-Aryan *khuṇṭa / Prakrit खुंट (khuṇṭa, 'peg, stump, corner'). Related to Sanskrit कुण्ट / खुण्ट- (a regional Indo-Aryan stem denoting a projecting point or post), the noun developed nasalization and compensatory lengthening in Hindi to give खूँटी (khūnṭī). Today it refers to small wall pegs and key hooks.

खेप.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit क्षेप (kṣepa, 'throw, cast, dispatch, load'), derived from क्षिप् (kṣip-, 'to throw, send'). In Prakrit खेप्प / खेव (kheppa / kheva), the initial cluster kṣ- regularly became kh-, yielding Hindi खेप (khep) with feminine gender shift. From 'a single dispatch or load sent out', it naturally evolved to mean a batch of baking or a consignment trip.

खेलना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit खेलति (khelati, 'plays, sports, sways'), via Prakrit खेलइ (khelaï). The Sanskrit root खेल् (khel-, 'to move to and fro, play') also produced the noun खेल (khel, 'game, sport'). Preserving its consonant-final stem, it gave modern Hindi खेलना (khelnā), the standard verb for playing games or sports (while musical instruments use बजाना).

खोना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit क्षोभयति / क्षपयति (kṣapayati, 'destroys, loses, wastes'), via Prakrit खोएइ (khoeï).

rootFamily.gloss: to be found; to get/receive (with को); to meet (with से)
to look for; to search for

खोया-पाया.etymology: Compound of perfective participles खोया ('lost', from खोना) + पाया ('found', from पाना).

rootFamily.gloss: to be found; to get/receive (with को); to meet (with से)

खोलना.etymology: Inherited transitive verb from Prakrit खोलेइ (kholeï, 'opens, unties'), paired with खुलना.

rootFamily.gloss: to open (by itself / intransitively); to come open

खौलना.etymology: Inherited from Middle Indo-Aryan *khavala- / *khola- ('bubbling, boiling'), related to Sanskrit क्ष्वेलति / क्वथति or an expressive Indo-Aryan stem *khaula- denoting the bubbling sound and motion of boiling liquid (compare Prakrit खवलइ / खोल्लइ). Contraction of -ava- to -au- yielded Hindi खौलना (khaulnā). Its participle खौलता हुआ is idiomatically used for anything piping or scalding hot.

गज़ब.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian غضب (ghazab, 'wrath, fury, something overwhelming') from Arabic غَضَب (ghaḍab, 'anger, wrath'), from the root غ-ض-ب (gh-ḍ-b). In South Asian Persian and Hindustani, 'wrath' underwent dramatic semantic amelioration via exclamations of awe ('what an overwhelming thing!'), coming to mean 'marvel, wonder, awesome'. Note the voiced uvular-derived ज़ in Hindi.

गड़बड़.etymology: Expressive Indo-Aryan reduplicative formation गड़बड़ ('tumult, muddle, confusion').

गड़बड़ी.etymology: Derived with the feminine nominalizing suffix -ई (-ī) from the expressive echo-word गड़बड़ (gaṛbaṛ, 'confusion, jumble, disorder'). Such reduplicated ablaut compounds in Indo-Aryan (compare तड़फड़, हड़बड़) imitate clattering, tumbled objects or chaotic activity. गड़बड़ी specifically names a discrete mistake, mix-up, or muddle.

गत्ता.etymology: Inherited from Middle Indo-Aryan गत्त / ग्रन्थ ('bound layers, thick board'), related to pasted paper layers.

गमला.etymology: Borrowed into Hindustani from Portuguese gamela ('wooden trough, wide earthen tub or basin'), which entered Indian coastal and garden usage in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries. Portuguese gamela ultimately derives from Latin camella ('goblet, shallow dish'). Adapted to the Hindi masculine -आ declension as गमला (gamlā), it became the universal North Indian word for a flowerpot.

गरम.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian گرم (garm, 'warm, hot'), from PIE *gʷʰermós (cognate with Sanskrit घर्म and English warm).

गरमी.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian گرمی (garmī, 'warmth, heat'), from گرم (garm, 'warm, hot', cognate with Sanskrit घर्म gharma).

rootFamily.gloss: winter; cold weather (often plural सर्दियों में 'in winter')

गरिमा.etymology: Learned Sanskrit borrowing गरिमा (garimā, 'weight, dignity, venerable worth'), from गुरु (guru, 'heavy, weighty').

गर्मी.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian گرمی (garmī, 'warmth, heat, summer'), formed from the adjective گرم (garm, 'warm, hot') with the abstract suffix -ی (-ī). The Persian adjective گرم continues Old Persian *garma- and Proto-Indo-European *gʷʰermós, making it directly cognate with Sanskrit घर्म (gharma, 'heat') and English 'warm'. In Hindi it inflects as a feminine -ई noun, with the plural regularly naming the summer season.

rootFamily.gloss: winter; cold weather (often plural सर्दियों में 'in winter')

गला.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit गल (gala, 'throat, neck'), cognate with Latin gula ('gullet, throat') and English 'gullet'. Through Prakrit गल (gala) and New Indo-Aryan thematic lengthening to -आ, it became Hindi गला (galā). In everyday speech it denotes both the physical throat/neck and the singing or speaking voice.

rootFamily.gloss: to speak; to say; to talk

गली.etymology: Inherited from Middle Indo-Aryan गल्ली (gallī, 'narrow lane, alley').

गल्ला.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian غله / گله (ġalla, 'grain store; shopkeeper's money-box') from Arabic غَلَّة (ḡalla, 'proceeds, takings').

गहरा.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit गभीर (gabhīra, 'deep, profound, dense'), via Prakrit गहीर (gahīra).

rootFamily.gloss: light (in weight, flavour, sound, or brightness); gentle

ग़लत.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic غَلَط (ḡalaṭ, 'error, mistake'), via Classical Persian غلط (ġalat, 'wrong').

ग़लती.etymology: Formed with abstract suffix -ई from ग़लत ('wrong'), borrowed via Classical Persian غلط (ġalat) from Arabic غَلَط (ḡalaṭ, 'error, slip').

गाँठ.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit ग्रन्थि (granthi, 'knot, joint, bundle'), derived from ग्रन्थ् (granth-, 'to tie, string together'). Through Prakrit गंठि (gaṇṭhi), loss of initial r- in the cluster gr- and simplification of the nasal-stop cluster with compensatory vowel lengthening yielded Hindi गाँठ (gānṭh). It retains the literal sense of a tied knot as well as joints or bundles.

गाइड.etymology: Borrowed from English guide, from Old French guide.

गाड़ी.etymology: Inherited from Prakrit गड्डी (gaḍḍī, 'cart, wheeled vehicle'), from early Indic *गड्ड (*gaḍḍa).

गायब.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian غایب (ghāyib, 'absent, hidden, vanished') from Arabic غَائِب (ghāʾib, 'absent, unseen, invisible'), the active participle of غَابَ (ghāba, 'to be absent, set, disappear'). Entering Hindustani through administrative and conversational Persianate register, it shifted toward 'missing or mysteriously vanished'. In Hindi it is invariable.

rootFamily.gloss: to be found; to get/receive (with को); to meet (with से)
to look; to seem; to be visible

गिनना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit गणयति (gaṇayati, 'counts, reckons, numbers'), via Prakrit गणेइ (gaṇeï).

rootFamily.gloss: account; tally; standard (के हिसाब से 'by the standard of / for')
number (room number, phone number, shoe size)

गिरना.etymology: Inherited from Middle Indo-Aryan गिरइ (giraï, 'falls, drops').

गिलास.etymology: Borrowed from English glass with an epenthetic short i breaking the initial cluster gl-.

गीत.etymology: A tatsama borrowing from Sanskrit गीत (gīta, 'sung, song, chant'), the past passive participle of गै (gai-, 'to sing', whence also गान gāna and गायक gāyaka). Used across Sanskrit poetry, drama, and music theory (including the Bhagavadgītā), it entered Hindi as a clean consonant-final masculine noun alongside the native tadbhava गाना (gānā).

गीला.etymology: Inherited from Prakrit गिल्ल (gilla, 'wet, moist, soft'), related to Sanskrit क्लिन्न / गिल.

गुज़रना.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian گذشتن / گذر (guzar, 'passing, crossing') + Hindi -ना.

rootFamily.gloss: to go; (as light verb) marks transition or completion

गुनगुना.etymology: An expressive reduplicated Indo-Aryan adjective (also echoed in गुनगुनाना 'to hum softly'), formed on an imitative stem गुण-/गुन- denoting soft, mild, or gentle sensation without harshness. Just as 'humming' is a soft, low-intensity sound, गुनगुना describes mild, pleasant heat—neither scalding nor cold. It inflects like a regular -आ adjective in Hindi.

rootFamily.gloss: light (in weight, flavour, sound, or brightness); gentle

गुरु.etymology: A tatsama borrowing from Sanskrit गुरु (guru, 'heavy, weighty, venerable, spiritual teacher, preceptor'), cognate with Greek βαρύς (barýs, 'heavy') and Latin gravis ('heavy, serious'). From 'weighty in wisdom and authority', the adjective became the classic South Asian noun for a revered teacher or master. It remains an invariable -उ masculine noun in Hindi.

गुरुवार.etymology: A Sanskritic calendrical compound of गुरु (guru, 'Jupiter, preceptor of the gods Bṛhaspati') and वार (vāra, 'day of the week, turn'). In classical Indian astronomy, Bṛhaspati (Jupiter) is the planet presiding over the fifth day of the seven-day week, matching Latin Iovis diēs ('Jove's day', French jeudi) and Germanic 'Thor's day'. Hindi uses गुरुवार as a masculine noun.

गुस्सा.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian غصه (ġussa) from Arabic غُصَّة (ḡuṣṣa, 'choking grief, distress, anger').

गूँज.etymology: Derived from Hindi गूँजना ('to echo, hum, reverberate'), inherited from Sanskrit गुञ्जति (guñjati, 'hums, buzzes').

गेट.etymology: Borrowed from English gate, from Old English geat.

गेस्टहाउस.etymology: Borrowed from English guesthouse, compound of guest (from Old Norse gestr, Proto-Indo-European *gʰóstis 'stranger, guest') + house (from Old English hūs 'dwelling').
गेस्टहाउस.notes: Masculine in Hindi (हमारा गेस्टहाउस), following the masculine gender of घर ('house, home').

गोल.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit गोल (gola, 'ball, globe, sphere, round').

गोला.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit गोल (gola, 'ball, globe, sphere') / गोलक (golaka, 'little ball'), via Prakrit गोल (gola) with masculine -आ enlargement in New Indo-Aryan. Related to the adjective गोल ('round'), the noun refers to any three-dimensional spherical object, from paper lantern globes and balls of thread to celestial spheres. It inflects as a regular -आ masculine noun.

गोलाई.etymology: Derived in Hindi from the adjective गोल (gol, 'round', from Sanskrit गोल) by adding the abstract feminine suffix -आई (-āī, from Middle Indo-Aryan *-āikā / *-āī). Just as चौड़ा gives चौड़ाई ('width') and लंबा gives लंबाई ('length'), गोल yields गोलाई ('roundness, curvature'). It is treated as a feminine noun.

ग्यारह.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit एकादश (ekādaśa, 'eleven'), via Prakrit एगारह (egāraha).

घंटा.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit घण्टा (ghaṇṭā, 'bell; hour struck on a bell'), via Prakrit घंटा (ghaṇṭā).

घंटाघर.etymology: Compound of घंटा (ghanṭā, 'bell, hour', from Sanskrit घण्टा) + घर (ghar, 'house').

rootFamily.gloss: to ring; to chime; to strike (the hour)
to ring (a bell); to play (a musical instrument)

घड़ियाल.etymology: Derived from घड़ी (ghaṛī, 'water-clock, hour, watch', from Sanskrit घटिका ghaṭikā 'small water-jar used to measure time') with the suffix -आल (-āl). Traditionally, a घड़ियाल was the brass plate or gong struck to announce the passing of each घड़ी (24-minute or hourly interval). Its homonym meaning 'gharial' comes separately from the snout resembling an earthen घड़ा ('pot').

घड़ी.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit घटिका (ghaṭikā, 'water-jar time-measure, period of twenty-four minutes, clock'), via Prakrit घडिआ (ghaḍiā).

घबराना.etymology: Expressive North Indian verb घबराना ('to be agitated, confused, anxious').

घबराहट.etymology: Derived from Hindi घबराना (ghabrānā, 'to be flustered, panic') + abstract suffix -आहट (-āhaṭ).

rootFamily.gloss: to feel nervous; to panic; to get flustered

घर.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit गृह (gṛha, 'house, dwelling'), via Prakrit घर (ghara) with metathesis.

घिसना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit घृष्यति / घर्षति (gharṣati, 'rubs, grinds'), via Prakrit घिसइ.

rootFamily.gloss: to polish; to shine; to brighten

घुटना.etymology: Inherited from Prakrit घुट्ट (ghuṭṭa, 'ankle, knee joint').

घुमाना.etymology: Causative of घूमना ('to turn, stroll'), from Middle Indo-Aryan घुम्मइ.

rootFamily.gloss: to turn; to bend; to be folded

घुमाव.etymology: Verbal noun in -आव from घुमाना ('to turn, spin'), causative of घूमना ('to revolve').

rootFamily.gloss: to turn; to rotate; to spin

घुलना-मिलना.etymology: Idiomatic Hindi compound verb pairing घुलना ('to dissolve, blend in', Sanskrit घूर्णते) + मिलना ('to meet, mix').

rootFamily.gloss: to be found; to get/receive (with को); to meet (with से)

घूँट.etymology: Inherited from Prakrit घुट्ट (ghuṭṭa, 'draught, swallow, sip').

घूमना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit घूर्णति (ghūrṇati, 'rolls, revolves, whirls, wavers'), via Prakrit घुम्मइ (ghummaï). Simplification of the geminate nasal -mm- with compensatory lengthening of the preceding vowel produced the Hindi stem घूम- (ghūm-) and infinitive घूमना (ghūmnā). From physical spinning and turning, it broadened naturally to strolling and touring around.

rootFamily.gloss: to turn; to bend; to be folded
to walk; to go; to move; to come along

घूरना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit घूर्णति (ghūrṇati, 'rolls, turns the eyes'), via Prakrit घुरइ / घूरइ.

rootFamily.gloss: to look; to see; to check; (after -कर) to try out

घोल.etymology: Deverbal masculine noun from Hindi घोलना (gholnā, 'to dissolve, stir into liquid, mix'), which traces back to Sanskrit घूर्ण / घोलयति (gholayati, 'stirs up, mixes together', attested in classical medical and culinary texts) via Prakrit घोलइ (gholaï). Used equally in baking for cake batter and in chemistry or painting for solutions, it stays masculine in Hindi.

चंपा.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit चम्पक (campaka, Magnolia champaca, prized golden-blossomed fragrant tree).

चक्कर.etymology: Inherited (semi-tatsama) from Sanskrit चक्र (cakra, 'wheel, circle, turn'), from PIE *kʷékʷlos ('wheel').

चखना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit चक्षति (cakṣati) / चषति (caṣati, 'eats, tastes') or Middle Indo-Aryan *चक्खइ (*cakkhaï, 'tastes', compare Prakrit चक्खइ, 'tastes, relishes'). Simplification of the geminate -kkh- gave the Hindi stem चख- (chakh-) and infinitive चखना (chakhnā). It specifically means sampling food or drink to check its flavour.

rootFamily.gloss: sweet; pleasant (of voice, music, or scent)

चचेरा.etymology: Formed from चाचा (cācā, 'father's younger brother') + kinship suffix -एरा (-erā).

चढ़ना.etymology: Inherited from Middle Indo-Aryan चड्ढइ (caḍḍhaï, 'mounts, climbs').

rootFamily.gloss: to come down; to get off (a train); to descend
floor / storey of a building; destination

चपटा.etymology: Inherited from Middle Indo-Aryan *cappaṭṭa / Prakrit चप्पट्ट (cappaṭṭa, 'flat, flattened, squashed'), formed from an expressive Indo-Aryan root *capp- ('to press flat, flatten'; compare Sanskrit चिपिट cipiṭa, 'flat-nosed, flattened'). Loss of gemination yielded the Hindi -आ adjective चपटा (chapṭā). It contrasts with गोल ('round') and उभरा ('raised').

चमकना.etymology: Derived in Indo-Aryan from an expressive root चम- (cham-, denoting sudden flash or glitter, compare Sanskrit चमत्कार 'astonishment, marvel') extended with the verbal suffix -क (-k-), parallel to Prakrit चमक्कइ (chamakkaï, 'flashes, sparkles'). The same root gives the feminine noun चमक ('shine, lustre') and the causative verb चमकाना ('to polish').

rootFamily.gloss: to polish; to shine; to brighten

चमकाना.etymology: Causative of चमकना ('to shine, sparkle'), formed with -आ- (-ā-).

चमचा.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian چمچه (chamcha, 'ladle, large spoon'), derived from चम् (cham-, related to Persian چمیدن 'to scoop/bend' or Middle Persian *čamčak) with the diminutive suffix -چه (-cha). Entering Hindustani through Mughal and urban kitchenware vocabulary, it adapted smoothly to the masculine -आ declension as चमचा (chamchā), alongside the shorter variant चम्मच.

चमड़ा.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit चर्मन् (carman, 'skin, hide, leather') + extension -ड, via Prakrit चम्मड (cammaḍa).

चमत्कार.etymology: A tatsama borrowing from Sanskrit चमत्कार (camatkāra, 'astonishment, poetic wonder, spectacle, miracle'), formed from the exclamation चमत् (camat, expressing sudden wonder) and कार (kāra, 'making', from कृ 'to do/make'). In classical Sanskrit poetics it signified the flash of aesthetic delight, before widening in Hindi to mean any astonishing marvel or miracle.

चम्मच.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit चमस (camasa, 'ladle, drinking vessel, spoon') or via Persian چمچه (čamča, itself related to Indo-Iranian *čamasa-).

चलन.etymology: A verbal noun derived from चलना (chalnā, 'to walk, move, be current') and corresponding to Sanskrit चलन (calana, 'moving, walking, currency', from चल् 'to move'). Just as 'current' in English comes from 'running/flowing', चलन evolved from 'movement/circulation' to mean 'what is currently practised, prevailing custom, or fashion'. It is masculine in Hindi.

rootFamily.gloss: to walk; to go; to move; to come along

चलना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit चलति (calati, 'moves, walks, stirs'), via Prakrit चलइ (calaï).

rootFamily.gloss: to go; (as light verb) marks transition or completion

चलाना.etymology: Causative of चलना ('to walk, move'), from Sanskrit चालयति (cālayati, 'sets in motion').

rootFamily.gloss: to walk; to go; to move; to come along

चश्मा.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian چشمه (čašma, 'eyeglass; spring of water'), from چشم (čašm, 'eye', cognate with Sanskrit चक्षुस् cakṣus).

rootFamily.gloss: to look; to see; to check; (after -कर) to try out

चहकना.etymology: Echoic/onomatopoeic Indo-Aryan verb चहकना ('to warble, chirp brightly').

चाँद.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit चन्द्र (candra, 'moon, shining, bright'), related to चन्दति ('shines') and Latin candēre ('to glow, shine white'). Through Prakrit चन्द (canda), loss of the medial nasal consonant with compensatory lengthening and nasalization of the vowel yielded Hindi चाँद (chānd). It is one of the most poetic and everyday nouns in Hindi.

चाँदी.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit चन्द्रिका (candrikā, 'moonlight; bright silver'), from चन्द्र ('moon'), via Prakrit चंदिआ (candiā).

चाचा.etymology: Inherited or formed as a nursery/affectionate kinship term in Indo-Aryan (compare Prakrit चच्च / चच्चा, and Sanskrit तात tāta 'father/dear one' alongside regional reduplicated *cāccā-). Like दादा ('paternal grandfather') and मामा ('maternal uncle'), चाचा preserves its final -आ without inflecting to -ए in the direct plural or oblique singular. It denotes specifically the father's younger brother.

चादर.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian چادر (čādar, 'sheet, cloth wrap, tent'), from Middle Persian čādur.

चाबी.etymology: Borrowed from Portuguese chave ('key'), ultimately from Latin clāvis ('key').

चाय.etymology: Borrowed via Persian چای (čāy) from Sinitic 茶 (chá, 'tea'), diffused overland along Asian trade routes.

चाय-पानी.etymology: Idiomatic Hindi dvandva compound pairing चाय ('tea', from Persian/Chinese) + पानी ('water', from Sanskrit पानीय pānīya) to mean 'light refreshments and hospitality'.

चायदानी.etymology: Compound of चाय (chāy, 'tea') + Persian suffix -दानी (-dānī, 'small vessel, holder').

चार.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit चत्वारि (catvāri, 'four'), via Prakrit चत्तारि (cattāri), from PIE *kʷetwóres.

चालीस.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit चत्वारिंशत् (catvāriṃśat, 'forty'), via Prakrit चत्तालीसा (cattālīsā).

चालू.etymology: Derived from the Hindi verbal stem चल- / चाल- (from संस्कृत चल् 'to move, go') by adding the expressive/agentive suffix -ऊ (-ū, as in कमाऊ 'earning' or बिकाऊ 'for sale'). Literally 'moving, current, in operation', चालू came to denote switches turned on, running machines, and ongoing operations. It remains completely invariable in Hindi.

rootFamily.gloss: to walk; to go; to move; to come along

चाहना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit चक्षते / उत्साहते or Prakrit चाहइ (cāhaï, 'looks for, wishes, desires').

cognates.meaning: impersonal 'is needed' from the same verb
