चाहिए.etymology: Grammaticalised old passive/precative form of चाहना ('is desired -> is needed, ought').

rootFamily.gloss: to want; to wish (माफ़ी चाहता/चाहती हूँ 'I apologise')
to; for; definite direct-object marker; at (times of day)

चिंता.etymology: Learned Sanskrit borrowing चिन्ता (cintā, 'thought, care, anxiety'), from root चिन्त् ('to think, reflect').

चिकना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit चिक्कण (cikkaṇa, 'smooth, glossy, unctuous, slippery'), attested in classical Sanskrit medical and poetic texts. Through Prakrit चिक्कण (cikkaṇa), simplification of the geminate -kk- and syncope of the medial vowel -a- produced Hindi चिकना (chiknā). It applies both to silky-smooth surfaces and greasy or glossy textures.

चिट.etymology: A native Indo-Aryan noun (compare Hindi चिट्ठी 'letter, note' and Prakrit चिट्ठ / *ciṭṭha-, 'written slip'), further reinforced in urban Indian usage by Anglo-Indian 'chit' ('short note, voucher, signed slip'). The English word 'chit' itself was borrowed directly from Hindustani चिट / चिट्ठी during the seventeenth century. In Hindi it is a feminine consonant-final noun.

rootFamily.gloss: slip of paper; short written note; chit

चिट्ठी.etymology: Inherited from Prakrit चिट्ठिआ (ciṭṭhiā, 'written slip, note'), source of Anglo-Indian English chit.

चिड़िया.etymology: Inherited from Prakrit चडिआ (caḍiā, 'small bird, sparrow'), from Sanskrit चटका (caṭakā).

चित्र.etymology: Learned borrowing from Sanskrit चित्र (citra, 'bright, variegated; picture, sketch').

चिपकना.etymology: Expressive Middle Indo-Aryan verb चिप्पकइ ('adheres, clings closely').

rootFamily.gloss: to be tied; to be fastened

चिमटी.etymology: Feminine diminutive of Hindi चिमटा (chimṭā, 'tongs, pincers'), derived from the verb चिमटना / चिपटना ('to cling, pinch, clasp together', related to Middle Indo-Aryan *cimp- / *cimm- 'to press, squeeze'). Just as चिमटा denotes large hearth tongs, the feminine diminutive चिमटी (chimṭī) denotes any small spring-clip, pinch-grip, clothespin, or pair of tweezers.

चिल्लाना.etymology: Inherited from Middle Indo-Aryan चिल्लइ (cillaï, 'cries out, shrieks').

चिह्न.etymology: A learned tatsama borrowing from Sanskrit चिह्न (cihna, 'mark, sign, emblem, badge, symptom'). In classical Sanskrit it denoted any identifying token, royal insignia, or landmark. Modern Hindi preserves the literary spelling ह्न (though commonly pronounced with metathesis as 'chinh' in speech) and treats it as a masculine noun.

चीज़.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian چیز (čīz, 'thing'), from Middle Persian tis / čīz.

चीनी.etymology: Literally 'Chinese (white refined sugar)', from चीन ('China') + -ई, referring historically to fine white crystalline sugar associated with Chinese trade.

rootFamily.gloss: sweet; pleasant (of voice, music, or scent)

चुकना.etymology: Inherited from Prakrit चुक्कइ (cukkaï, 'comes to an end, is settled, finishes').

rootFamily.gloss: to go; (as light verb) marks transition or completion
to take; to buy; light verb for inward/self-benefiting action
to give; to let (after -ने); light verb marking outward/completed action

चुनना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit चिनोति (cinoti, 'gathers, selects'), via Prakrit चुणइ (cuṇaï).

चुपचाप.etymology: Expressive reduplicative compound built on चुप (cup, 'silent, quiet').

चूड़ी.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit चूडिका / चूडा (cūḍā, 'bracelet, ring, crest'), via Prakrit चूडी (cūḍī).

चूल्हा.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit चुल्लि / चुल्ली (culli / cullī, 'hearth, fireplace, stove'), via Prakrit चुल्ल (culla) / *चुल्ह (*culha). Aspiration of the geminate -ll- and lengthening of the root vowel gave Hindi चूल्हा (chūlhā) with masculine -आ ending. From village mud hearths to contemporary gas stoves, it remains the core domestic term for a cooking burner.

चेक-इन.etymology: Borrowed from English check-in, nominalisation of the phrasal verb check in ('to verify and register one's arrival at a hotel desk or station'; English check itself derives via Old French eschec from Persian šāh 'king' in chess).

history.meaning: arrival registration at a hotel or terminal

चेक-इन.notes: Masculine noun in Hindi; turns into an active verb with करना (चेक-इन करना, 'to check in').

चेन.etymology: Borrowed from English chain, semantically extended in Indian English and Hindi to slide fasteners (zippers).

history.meaning: linked metal series; zipper (South Asian usage)

चेहरा.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian چهره (čihra, 'face, countenance, visage'), from Middle Persian čihrak.

चौक.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit चतुष्क (catuṣka, 'four-way courtyard or square'), via Prakrit चउक्क (caükka).

चौकोर.etymology: A native Hindi compound of चौ- (chau-, 'four', from Sanskrit चतुर् catur) and कोर (kor, 'edge, corner, side', from Middle Indo-Aryan कोरा / Sanskrit कोटि 'edge, point'). Literally 'having four corners or edges', it functions as an invariable adjective meaning 'square' or 'quadrangular', parallel to चौकोना.

चौड़ा.etymology: Inherited from Prakrit चउड (caüḍa, 'broad, flat, wide'), linked to चतुर ('four-sided, square-spread').

rootFamily.gloss: big; large; elder; very (in expressions like बड़े शौक़ से)

चौड़ाई.etymology: Derived within Hindi from चौड़ा (chauṛā, 'wide') + abstract noun suffix -आई (-āī).

चौथा.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit चतुर्थ (caturtha, 'fourth'), formed from चतुर् (catur, 'four') with the ancient ordinal suffix -थ (-tha, cognate with English '-th' in 'fourth'). Through Prakrit चउत्थ (caüttha), contraction of -aü- into the diphthong -au- and simplification of -tth- yielded Hindi चौथा (chauthā). It inflects regularly for gender and case.

चौदह.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit चतुर्दश (caturdaśa, 'fourteen'), via Prakrit चउद्दह (caüddaha).

चौबीस.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit चतुर्विंशति (caturviṃśati, 'twenty-four'), composed of चतुर् (catur, 'four') and विंशति (viṃśati, 'twenty'). Via Prakrit चउवीस / चउब्बीस (caüvīsa / caübbīsa), the vowel hiatus -aü- contracted to -au- and medial -vv- became -b-, yielding Hindi चौबीस (chaubīs). Like all Hindi numerals, it does not inflect.

छज्जा.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit छद्य (chadya, 'covering, roof, overhang') or छदिस् (chadis, 'roof, thatch', from छद् 'to cover'), via Prakrit छज्ज (chajja, 'eaves, projecting balcony'). Retaining the palatal geminate -jj- and adding the masculine -आ ending, it became Hindi छज्जा (chhajjā). In Jaipur havelis, it refers specifically to overhanging stone eaves or upper courtyard balconies.

छड़.etymology: Inherited from Middle Indo-Aryan छड (chaḍa) / *छडि (*chaḍi), likely connected to Sanskrit यष्टि (yaṣṭi, 'staff, rod') or शलाका / छटा ('long thin stick, rod') via regional Indo-Aryan *chaḍa- denoting a straight rod or shaft. Its consonant-final form छड़ (chhaṛ) denotes thicker structural rods, dowels, or spacer bars, whereas the -ई form छड़ी denotes a cane or slender stick.

छड़ी.etymology: Feminine diminutive of छड़ (chhaṛ, 'rod, staff'), continuing Prakrit छडी (chaḍī, 'cane, switch, wand') and related to Sanskrit चटी / शलाका ('slender stick'). In everyday Hindi, छड़ी is the primary word for a gentleman's walking stick or cane as well as a slender wooden dowel.

छत.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit छत्त्र (chattra, 'parasol, covering, shelter'), via Prakrit छत्त (chatta).

छपना.etymology: Intransitive stem derived in Indo-Aryan alongside the transitive verb छापना (chhāpnā, 'to stamp, print'), connected to Sanskrit छप् / क्षप् or Prakrit छप्पइ (chhappaï, 'presses, stamps'). Originally referring to block-printing textiles with carved wooden stamps—a craft famous in Jaipur—it naturally extended to modern printing presses and newspapers. Short vowel -अ- marks the intransitive form.

छपाक.etymology: An expressive onomatopoeic formation in Hindi imitating the sudden slap and burst of water when a flat or heavy object hits a pool or basin, formed from the imitative base छप- (chhap-, compare छप-छप 'splashing') and the abrupt sound-ending -आक (-āk, as in धमाक 'bang' and तड़ाक 'crack'). It is used both as an interjection and a sound noun.

छल्ला.etymology: Inherited from Prakrit छल्ल (challa, 'ring, loop, bark').

छह.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit षष् (ṣaṣ, 'six'), via Prakrit छ (cha), from PIE *swéḱs.

छाँव.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit छाया (chāyā, 'shade, shadow, reflection', cognate with Greek σκιά skiā). Through Prakrit छाआ / छाँह (chāā / chāṁha, with spontaneous nasalization and glide development -h-/-v-), the word evolved into Hindi छाँव (chhānv) alongside poetic छाँह. While छाया remained in formal Hindi, छाँव became the warm, everyday spoken word for shade under a tree.

छात्र.etymology: A tatsama borrowing from Sanskrit छात्र (chātra, 'pupil, disciple, student'), derived from छत्र (chattra, 'umbrella, shelter', from छद् 'to cover/protect') with vriddhi strengthening of the first vowel. Traditionally, a pupil was one who covered or sheltered the faults of his preceptor or sat under the teacher's sheltering protection. In modern Hindi it is the standard masculine noun for a student.

छायादार.etymology: A classic Perso-Sanskrit hybrid adjective combining Sanskrit-derived छाया (chāyā, 'shade') with the Persian productive suffix -दार (-dār, 'having, holding', from داشتن 'to have/hold', cognate with Sanskrit धर्). Literally 'shade-bearing', छायादार functions as an invariable adjective across Hindi prose and everyday speech to describe leafy trees and cool courtyards.

छिड़कना.etymology: Inherited from Middle Indo-Aryan छिट्टक्कइ ('scatters drops, sprinkles').

छिपना.etymology: Inherited Indo-Aryan intransitive verb छिपना ('to be covered, hide').

छिपाना.etymology: Transitive/causative of छिपना ('to hide'), formed with -आ- (-ā-).

rootFamily.gloss: slip of paper; short written note; chit

छिलका.etymology: Derived in Hindi from the verbal stem छील- / छिल- (chhīlnā, 'to peel, pare, scrape'), which descends from Sanskrit छल्ल (challa, 'bark, skin, peel') or शल्क (śalka, 'scale, bark, chip') via Prakrit छल्लि / छिल्ल (challi / chilla). Extended with the diminutive-noun suffix -का (-kā), it became the standard masculine noun छिलका (chhilkā) for fruit peels, rinds, and husks.

छूट.etymology: Deverbal feminine noun from छूटना (chūṭnā, 'to be released, remitted'), from Sanskrit छुट् / क्षुट् via Prakrit छुट्टइ.

छूना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit छुपति (chupati, 'touches'), via Prakrit छुवइ (chuvaï).

छेड़ना.etymology: Inherited from Prakrit छेडइ (cheḍaï, 'touches, stirs, teases').

rootFamily.gloss: to make laugh; to cheer up

छेद.etymology: Learned/semi-learned borrowing from Sanskrit छेद (cheda, 'cut, slit, perforation, hole'), from छिद् ('to pierce').

छोटा.etymology: Inherited from Prakrit छुट्ट / छोट्ट (choṭṭa, 'small, short, slender').

less; little; fewer; कम से कम 'at least'
a little; some; a few (in plural)

छोड़ना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit छोरयति / क्षोडयति ('releases, lets go, leaves'), via Prakrit छोडेइ (choḍeï).

rootFamily.gloss: to put; to place; to keep

जँचना.etymology: Inherited from Middle Indo-Aryan जच्चइ ('is tested, proves fitting, looks becoming').

history.meaning: to be tested; to look becoming

जग.etymology: Borrowed in this household sense from early modern and modern English jug ('deep spouted vessel with a handle for pouring water or milk', attested in sixteenth-century English, likely a familiar transfer from the pet name Jug for Joan/Judith).
जग.notes: Unrelated to its native homograph जग ('the world', inherited from Sanskrit जगत् jagat); पानी का जग means 'a pitcher of water'.

जगह.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian جایگاه (jāygāh, 'place, station'), shortened in spoken Hindustani to जगह.

जज़्बात.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian جذبات (jazbāt, 'feelings, emotions') from Arabic جَذَبَات (jaḏabāt), the feminine sound plural of جَذْبَة (jaḏba, 'impulse, attraction, emotion', from the root ج-ذ-ب j-ḏ-b 'to draw, attract'). In Hindustani, the Arabic plural form was lexicalized as a masculine plural-only noun meaning 'feelings, sentiment, emotions', pairing with the adjective जज़्बाती.

जज़्बाती.etymology: Formed in Hindustani from the Arabic-Persian loanword जज़्बात (jazbāt, 'emotions, feelings') by attaching the adjectival suffix -ई (-ī). Literally 'pertaining to emotions', it describes both emotionally sensitive people and sentimental gestures or situations. Like other -ई adjectives, it is completely invariable in Hindi.

जब.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit यदा (yadā, 'when [relative]'), via Prakrit जइया / जब्ब.

rootFamily.gloss: then; at that time; तब तक 'until then'
just then; at that very moment; that explains why

जबकि.etymology: A compound conjunction formed in Hindi by joining the relative temporal adverb जब (jab, 'when', from Sanskrit यदा yadā via Prakrit जह / जब्ब) with the subordinating complementizer कि (ki, 'that', from Persian که). Literally 'when that', the pair developed a strong contrastive sense equivalent to English 'whereas' or 'while'.

rootFamily.gloss: when (in a statement or time clause, never a question!)

जमा.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic جَمْع (jamʿ, 'gathering, sum, deposit'), via Classical Persian جمع (jam').

जयपुर.etymology: Sanskrit compound जयपुर (Jayapura, 'City of Jai / Victory'), named after its founder Sawai Jai Singh II (1727).

जलना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit ज्वलति (jvalati, 'burns, shines, glows'), via Prakrit जलइ (jalaï).

rootFamily.gloss: to switch on / light (a lamp); to kindle

जलरंग.etymology: A modern Hindi calque (loan-translation) of English 'watercolour' (or 'watercolor'), compounding tatsama जल (jal, 'water', from Sanskrit जल) and रंग (rang, 'colour, dye', from Sanskrit रङ्ग). Used as an uncountable masculine noun for the painting medium and attributively before कला or चित्र ('watercolour painting'), it neatly parallels other modern compound art terms.

जलाना.etymology: Causative in -आना from जलना, from Sanskrit ज्वालयति (jvālayati, 'lights, kindles').

rootFamily.gloss: to burn; to be lit / switched on (of a light)

जल्द.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian جلد (jald, 'quick, swift, brisk, soon'), from Arabic جَلْد.

rootFamily.gloss: for now; at present; for the moment

जल्दी.etymology: Derived from جلد (jald, 'swift') + Persian suffix -ई (-ī), used both as noun ('haste') and adverb ('quickly, early').

rootFamily.gloss: fast; heavy (rain); strong/sharp (salt, spice, sun, sound)

जल्दी-जल्दी.etymology: Distributive/intensive reduplication of जल्दी (jaldī, 'speed, quickly', from Persian جلدی).

rootFamily.gloss: fast; heavy (rain); strong/sharp (salt, spice, sun, sound)

जवान.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian جوان (jawān, 'young, youth'), cognate with Sanskrit युवन् (yuvan) and English young.

जवानी.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian جوانی (jawānī, 'youth, youthfulness'), derived from the adjective جوان (jawān, 'young', continuing Old Persian *yuvān- and cognate with Sanskrit युवन् yuvan and Latin iuvenis) with the abstract suffix -ی (-ī). In Hindi it functions as a feminine noun denoting the prime period of young adulthood.

जवाब.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian جواب (jawāb) from Arabic جَوَاب (jawāb, 'answer, reply').

जश्न.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian جشن (jashn, 'feast, festival, celebration'), continuing Middle Persian jašn ('ritual feast, thanksgiving festival') and Old Iranian *yasna- ('worship, sacrifice, sacred feast', cognate with Sanskrit यज्ञ yajña). Moving from Zoroastrian seasonal feasts into courtly and popular Persianate culture, it became a warm, everyday masculine noun in Hindustani for any joyful celebration.

जहाँ.etymology: Inherited from Prakrit जहँ (jahã, 'where [relative]'), from Sanskrit यत्र (yatra).

जहाज़.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian جهاز (jahāz, 'equipment, gear, vessel, ship') from Arabic جِهَاز (jihāz, 'outfit, apparatus, equipment, ship's rigging'), from the root ج-ه-ز (j-h-z, 'to equip, fit out'). Because an ocean vessel was viewed as a fully outfitted expedition ('equipment'), the word specialized in Persian and Hindustani maritime usage to mean 'ship'.

ज़रा.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic ذَرَّة (ḏarra, 'tiny speck, atom'), via Classical Persian ذره (zarra -> zarā, 'a tiny bit, just').

rootFamily.gloss: a little; some; a few (in plural)

ज़रूर.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic ضَرُور (ḍarūr, 'necessity, inevitable'), via Classical Persian ضرور (zarūr, 'certainly, without fail').

rootFamily.gloss: completely; absolutely; (with नहीं) not at all

ज़रूरत.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian ضرورت (zarūrat, 'necessity, need') from Arabic ضَرُورَة (ḍarūra, 'compulsion, necessity, exigency'), derived from the root ض-ر-ر (ḍ-r-r, 'to press, constrain, harm'). The Arabic emphatic stop ض (ḍ) regularly became the voiced fricative ज़ (z) in Persian and Hindustani pronunciation. It is one of the highest-frequency feminine nouns in everyday Hindi.

ज़रूरी.etymology: Derived from Arabic loanword ज़रूर (ḍarūr, 'necessity') + Indo-Persian adjectival suffix -ई.

rootFamily.gloss: is needed; is wanted; should (with infinitive)

ज़िंदगी.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian زندگی (zindagī, 'life, living'), from زنده (zinda, 'alive').

ज़िद्दी.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian ضدی (ziddī, 'obstinate, stubborn'), from Arabic ضِدّ (ḍidd, 'opposition').

ज़ोर.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian زور (zōr, 'strength, force, vigour'), from Middle Persian zōr.

rootFamily.gloss: fast; heavy (rain); strong/sharp (salt, spice, sun, sound)

ज़्यादा.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic زِيَادَة (ziyāda, 'increase, excess, more'), via Classical Persian زیاده (ziyāda).

rootFamily.gloss: less; little; fewer; कम से कम 'at least'

ज़्यादातर.etymology: Indo-Persian formation: ज़्यादा (from Arabic زِيَادَة) + comparative suffix -तर (-tar).

जाँच.etymology: Deverbal feminine noun from Hindi जाँचना (jānchnā, 'to test, examine, investigate, verify'), which traces back to Middle Indo-Aryan *जंचइ (*jañcaï, 'inspects, estimates') or Sanskrit यांचति / याचति ('asks, requests, tests', via Prakrit जंचइ jañcaï). Nasalization and compensatory lengthening produced the stem जाँच- (jānch-). It is used equally for casual checks and formal inspections.

जागना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit जाग्रति (jāgrati, 'is awake, watches'), via Prakrit जग्गइ (jaggaï).

rootFamily.gloss: to rise; to get up; (compound) to burst into

जादुई.etymology: Formed from Persian جادو (jādū, 'magic, charm') + -ई (-ī); Classical Persian جادویی.

जान.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian جان (jān, 'life, soul, vital spirit'), from Middle Persian gyān.

जानना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit जानाति (jānāti, 'knows'), via Prakrit जाणइ (jāṇaï), from PIE *ǵneh₃- ('to know').

rootFamily.gloss: to understand; to realise; to figure out

जाना.etymology: Present/future stem जा- from Sanskrit याति (yāti, 'goes') via Prakrit जाइ; suppletive perfective गया from Sanskrit गत (gata, 'gone').

rootFamily.gloss: to walk; to go; to move; to come along
to come out; to leave; to emerge

जानी-पहचानी.etymology: Paired participial compound from जानना ('to know') + पहचानना ('to recognise', from Sanskrit प्रत्यभिजानाति).

जाल.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit जाल (jāla, 'net, web, lattice, snare').

जाली.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit जालिका (jālikā, 'net, lattice, meshwork'), from जाल (jāla, 'net').

जी.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit जीव (jīva, 'life, living soul'), reduced via Prakrit जीअ (jīa) into Hindi's signature particle of warmth and respect.

जीतना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit जयति / जित (jayati, 'conquers, wins'), via Prakrit जित्तइ (jittaï).

जुगलबंदी.etymology: A hybrid compound of Indo-Aryan जुगल (jugal, 'pair, couple', tadbhava from Sanskrit युगल yugala) and Persian-origin बंदी (bandī, 'tying together, composition, arrangement', from بند 'to bind'). Literally 'tying together of a pair', जुगलबंदी became the celebrated technical term in North Indian classical music for a lively duet between two soloists or instruments. It is feminine.

जुड़वाँ.etymology: Derived within Indo-Aryan from जुड़ना ('to be joined, paired') + suffix -वाँ.

rootFamily.gloss: to join; to connect; to mend; to bring together

जूता.etymology: Inherited from Middle Indo-Aryan जुत्ता (juttā, 'pair of shoes, footwear'), connected to Sanskrit युक्त (yukta, 'yoked, paired').

rootFamily.gloss: cloth; piece of fabric; clothes (in plural कपड़े)

जूस.etymology: Borrowed from English juice, via Old French jus from Latin iūs ('broth, juice').

जेब.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian جیب (jayb / jēb) from Arabic جَيْب (jayb, 'bosom of a garment, pocket').

rootFamily.gloss: cloth bag; tote bag; shopping sack

जेलीफ़िश.etymology: Borrowed from English 'jellyfish' into modern Hindi biological and descriptive vocabulary. English 'jellyfish' is a transparent compound of 'jelly' (from Old French gelee 'frost, jelly', Latin gelāta) and 'fish' (Old English fisc), named for the translucent gelatinous bell of medusae. In Hindi it takes feminine gender by analogy with मछली ('fish').

जैम.etymology: Borrowed from English jam ('sweet preserve made by boiling crushed fruit with sugar', attested in eighteenth-century English from the verb jam 'to crush, press tightly together').

history.meaning: crushed fruit boiled thick with sugar

जैम.notes: Spelled जैम ([dʒɛːm]) with ऐ to render English /æ/, distinguishing breakfast fruit jam from ट्रैफ़िक जाम ('traffic jam', spelled with आ).

जैसा.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit यादृश (yādṛśa, 'like which, of whichever sort'), via Prakrit जइस (jaïsa).

rootFamily.gloss: what kind of; how (in quality or state)

जो.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit यः (yaḥ, 'who, which'), via Prakrit जो (jo), from PIE *yós.

जोड़.etymology: Verbal root noun from जोड़ना ('to join, connect'), inherited from Prakrit जोडेइ (joḍeï).

rootFamily.gloss: to join; to connect; to mend; to bring together

जोड़ना.etymology: Inherited from Prakrit जोडइ (joḍaï, 'yokes, unites, fastens'), related to Sanskrit युज्.

जोड़ा.etymology: Derived from जोड़ना ('to join, pair'), from Prakrit जोडेइ (joḍeï), connected to Sanskrit जुटति / युक्त.

झाँकना.etymology: Expressive Middle Indo-Aryan verb झंकइ ('peeps, glancesfurtively').

rootFamily.gloss: to look; to see; to check; (after -कर) to try out

झाड़ना.etymology: Inherited from Middle Indo-Aryan झाडइ (jhāḍaï, 'shakes off, sweeps').

झाड़ू.etymology: Derived from झाड़ना ('to sweep, brush off'), inherited from Prakrit झाडेइ (jhāḍeï).

झिझक.etymology: Inherited from Prakrit jhijjha, an expressive Indo-Aryan formation denoting sudden drawing back, shrinking, or hesitation.

झिलमिली.etymology: Derived from the expressive Indo-Aryan stem झिलमिल (jhilmil, 'shimmering, twinkling, lattice-like interplay of light and shadow') with the feminine suffix -ई (-ī). Because slatted wooden window shutters break bright sunlight into flickering bands of light and shade, North Indian architecture named Venetian blinds and louvered shutters झिलमिली (jhilmilī). It is a feminine -ई noun.

झुकाना.etymology: Transitive/causative of झुकना ('to bend, lean'), from Prakrit झुक्कइ.

झूमना.etymology: Inherited from Middle Indo-Aryan *jhumm- / Prakrit झुम्मइ ('sways, reels, nods'), an expressive Indo-Aryan verb connected with rhythmic nodding or swinging motion (compare Sanskrit घूर्ण 'revolving' or regional *jhūm-). Simplification of the geminate nasal -mm- with compensatory lengthening of the preceding vowel yielded Hindi झूमना (jhūmnā). It describes both trees swaying in a breeze and joyous rhythmic movement.

झूलना.etymology: Inherited from Middle Indo-Aryan *jhullaï / Prakrit झुल्लइ ('swings, dangles, oscillates'), related to Sanskrit दोला / *झोला (jholā, 'swinging motion') via expressive palatalization and aspiration. Loss of the geminate -ll- with vowel lengthening produced the Hindi stem झूल- (jhūl-) and infinitive झूलना (jhūlnā). It pairs closely with the noun झूला ('swing').

झेलना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit झेल् / Prakrit झेल्लइ (jhellaï, 'catches, bears, endures').

rootFamily.gloss: to save; to protect; to spare

झोंका.etymology: Derived from the Hindi verb झोंकना (jhonknā, 'to cast, hurl, blow in a rush'), from Middle Indo-Aryan *jhumpa- / *jhoṅka- ('sudden thrust, push, sweep'). Like a sudden shove or fling of air, झोंका (jhonkā) specialized in Hindustani for a sharp gust of wind or a brief drift of sleep (नींद का झोंका). It inflects as a regular masculine -आ noun.

टकराना.etymology: Denominative from टक्कर ('collision, bump'), an expressive Indo-Aryan word for impact.

टपकना.etymology: Expressive Indo-Aryan verb टपकना imitating falling drops (टप-टप).

rootFamily.gloss: to drip (something); to let water drip

टपकाना.etymology: Causative/transitive in -आना formed from टपकना ('to drip').

टाँगना.etymology: Inherited from Middle Indo-Aryan टंगइ (ṭaṅgaï, 'hangs, suspends').

टाइल.etymology: Borrowed from English 'tile' through colonial-era masonry, roofing, and modern interior construction in India. English 'tile' descends from Old English tigele, itself an early Germanic borrowing from Latin tēgula ('roof tile', from tegere 'to cover'). In Hindi it is a feminine consonant-final noun, with the English-style plural टाइलें.

टाई.etymology: Borrowed from English tie ('band of silk or cloth knotted neatly under a shirt collar', shortened in eighteenth- and nineteenth-century English from neck-tie, itself from Old English tēag 'cord, band').
टाई.notes: Feminine in Hindi (नीली टाई, 'a blue tie') because loanwords ending in long -ई (-ī) regularly join the feminine declension.

टायर.etymology: Borrowed from English tyre (British spelling of tire).

टिकना.etymology: Inherited from Middle Indo-Aryan *ṭikkaï / Prakrit टिक्कइ ('stays, remains fixed, lasts'), connected to an Indo-Aryan stem *ṭikk- ('to stop, prop, stay firm', compare Sanskrit स्था/तिष्ठति influenced by regional retroflex forms). Simplification of the geminate -kk- produced Hindi टिकना (ṭiknā). It covers physical resting/perching as well as endurance.

rootFamily.gloss: to stop; to wait; to stay overnight (at an inn)
to stay (as a guest); to stop; to pause
to put; to place; to keep

टिन.etymology: Borrowed from English 'tin' via nineteenth- and twentieth-century metalware, packaging, and bakery terminology in South Asia. English 'tin' comes from Old English tin and Proto-Germanic *tiną ('tin metal'), later metonymically designating tin-plated canisters and baking pans. In Hindi it is an invariable masculine noun.

टीचर.etymology: Borrowed from English teacher, agent noun formed from teach (from Old English tǣċan 'to show, point out, instruct', Proto-Germanic *taikijaną, related to token) + agentive suffix -er.
टीचर.notes: Used everyday alongside formal अध्यापक / अध्यापिका and गुरुजी, taking masculine or feminine agreement according to the teacher's sex.

टुकड़ा.etymology: Inherited from Middle Indo-Aryan टुक्कड (ṭukkaḍa, 'piece, fragment').

टूटना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit त्रुट्यति (truṭyati, 'breaks, snaps, splits'), via Prakrit तुट्टइ (tuṭṭaï).

टेप.etymology: Borrowed from English tape ('narrow strip of woven cloth, adhesive film, or measuring ribbon'), descending from Old English tæppe ('narrow strip or fillet of cloth').

history.meaning: cloth ribbon -> adhesive or measuring tape
adhesive tape, packing tape, measuring tape

टेप.notes: Masculine in Hindi; टेप लगाना means 'to stick or seal with adhesive tape'.

टैक्सी.etymology: Borrowed from English taxi, shortened from taximeter cab.

टैग.etymology: Borrowed from English tag ('small hanging card or label fastened to luggage or clothing'), attested since Middle English tagge ('hanging point or tab of cloth or metal', likely of Scandinavian origin).

history.meaning: hanging tab -> identification or price tag
luggage label, name tag, price tag

टैग.notes: Masculine in Hindi (सूटकेस का टैग, 'the luggage tag on the suitcase').

टैबलेट.etymology: Borrowed from English tablet ('flat touch-screen computer'), ultimately from Old French tablete.

टॉर्च.etymology: Borrowed from British/Indian English torch ('handheld battery flashlight'), ultimately from Old French torche.

टोकरी.etymology: Diminutive in -ई of टोकरा ('large basket'), from Middle Indo-Aryan *टोक्कड (*ṭokkaḍa, 'wicker basket').

टोपी.etymology: Feminine diminutive of टोप (ṭop, 'helmet, large hat, crown'), inherited from Middle Indo-Aryan *ṭoppa / Prakrit टोप्प (ṭoppa, 'cap, cover, top'), related to regional Indo-Aryan *ṭop- ('something covering the top/head', also comparing Sanskrit स्तूप 'crest, mound'). Entering Portuguese and Anglo-Indian usage as 'topi' (as in 'pith topi'), it remains the everyday Hindi feminine noun for any hat or cap.

ट्रेन.etymology: Borrowed from English train, via Old French trahiner.

ट्रैफ़िक.etymology: Borrowed from English traffic ('flow and congestion of road vehicles'), which entered English via sixteenth-century French trafic from Old Italian traffico ('commercial trade, bustle of goods and carriers').

history.meaning: commerce -> movement of vehicles along streets

ट्रैफ़िक.notes: Masculine in Hindi (आज बहुत ट्रैफ़िक था, 'there was heavy traffic today'); written with nuqta फ़ for labiodental [f].

ट्रैवल.etymology: Borrowed from English travel ('journeying, tourism'), which split in Middle English from travail ('toil, arduous journey'), borrowed from Old French travailler ('to labour, toil on the road').

history.meaning: travel (especially in compounds like ट्रैवल गाइड and ट्रैवल बैग)

ट्रैवल.notes: Used chiefly in modern compounds such as ट्रैवल गाइड ('travel guidebook') and ट्रैवल एजेंसी, while standalone 'journey/trip' is सफ़र or यात्रा.

ठंडा.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit स्तब्ध (stabdha, 'stiffened, numbed, chilled'), via Prakrit ठद्ध -> ठंड (ṭhaṇḍa).

ठहरना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit प्रस्थिर / Middle Indo-Aryan ठहरइ ('stands firm, halts, lodges').

rootFamily.gloss: to stop; to wait; to stay overnight (at an inn)

ठीक.etymology: Inherited from Prakrit ठिक्क (ṭhikka, 'firmly set, exact, proper'), related to Sanskrit स्थित ('standing firm').

ठीक-ठीक.etymology: Reduplication of ठीक ('exact, right') expressing precision.

ठोकना.etymology: Inherited from Middle Indo-Aryan *ṭhokkaï / Prakrit ठोक्कइ ('strikes, knocks, pounds'), derived from an expressive Indo-Aryan imitative stem *ṭhokk- representing a dull solid knock on wood or stone. Loss of gemination yielded Hindi ठोकना (ṭhoknā), covering both light celebratory taps on wood and heavy hammering.

डर.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit दर (dara, 'fear, terror'), from दृ ('to burst, fear').

डरना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit दरति (darati, 'fears, splits'), via Prakrit डरइ (ḍaraï).

डरपोक.etymology: Compound Indo-Aryan adjective built from डर (ḍar, 'fear') + expressive element -पोक.

डाकिया.etymology: Formed within Indo-Aryan from डाक (ḍāk, 'post, mail relay') + agentive suffix -इया (-iyā).

डायरी.etymology: Borrowed from English diary, from Latin diārium ('daily allowance, journal'), broadened in South Asia to mean any bound pocket notebook.

डालना.etymology: Inherited from Middle Indo-Aryan डल्लइ / डालइ ('casts in, pours, places').

rootFamily.gloss: to put; to place; to keep

डाली.etymology: Feminine form of डाल (ḍāl, 'bough, branch'), inherited from Sanskrit दाल / *डाल (ḍāla, 'branch, shoot, twig') via Prakrit डाल / डाली (ḍāla / ḍālī), likely connected to Sanskrit दल (dala, 'leaf, shoot, split portion'). In Hindi both डाल and डाली name tree branches, with डाली particularly common for leafy boughs and smaller limbs.

डिब्बा.etymology: Inherited from Middle Indo-Aryan डिब्ब (ḍibba, 'small box, casket').

डुबोना.etymology: Transitive/causative counterpart of the intransitive verb डूबना (ḍūbnā, 'to sink, drown, plunge'), formed with the causative suffix -ओ (-o-) and shortening of the root vowel (ऊ -> उ). The base डूबना derives from Middle Indo-Aryan *ḍubbaï / Prakrit डुब्बइ ('sinks, plunges'). Thus डुबोना means 'to cause to sink, dip, or immerse'.

डेढ़.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit द्व्यर्ध (dvyardha, 'the second half-complete = 1½'), via Prakrit दिवड्ढ (divaḍḍha).

rootFamily.gloss: half past; plus a half (with numbers 3 and above)

डेसिबल.etymology: Borrowed from English decibel (deci- + bel, named after Alexander Graham Bell).

डेस्क.etymology: Borrowed from English 'desk' through modern office, school, and hotel reception vocabulary in India. English 'desk' derives from Medieval Latin desca ('table to write on'), itself from Italian desco and Latin discus ('flat circular plate, table'). In Hindi it is used as an invariable consonant-final noun, especially for front-desk and station counters.

डोरी.etymology: Feminine diminutive of डोर (ḍor, 'string, cord, thread'), inherited from Sanskrit दोरक (doraka, 'string, thread, cord') / डोर (ḍora) via Prakrit दोर / डोर (dora / ḍora), with retroflexion of the initial dental d-. In Hindi, डोरी specifically denotes a slender braided cord, twine, or hanging line.

ढंग.etymology: Inherited from Middle Indo-Aryan ढंग (ḍhaṅga, 'way, mode, fashion').

ढक्कन.etymology: Instrument noun formed from the Hindi verb ढकना (ḍhaknā, 'to cover, shut') with the nominal suffix -अन (-an). The verb ढकना descends from Middle Indo-Aryan *ḍhakkaï / Prakrit ढक्कइ ('covers, hides'), connected with Sanskrit स्थगयति (sthagayati, 'covers, conceals'). Thus ढक्कन literally means 'that which covers', i.e. a lid or cap.

ढलना.etymology: Inherited from Middle Indo-Aryan *ḍhallaï / Prakrit ढल्लइ ('slopes down, declines, tilts, pours'), connected to Sanskrit ध्वल् / ह्वल् or regional Indo-Aryan *ḍhal- ('to incline, slant downward'). From sloping downward, the verb came to describe the afternoon sun descending toward sunset and evening waning.

ढाई.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit अर्धतृतीय (ardhatṛtīya, 'half of the third = 2½'), via Prakrit अड्ढाइअ (aḍḍhāia).

rootFamily.gloss: half past; plus a half (with numbers 3 and above)

ढीला.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit शिथिल (śithila, 'loose, slack, relaxed'), via Prakrit सिढिल -> ढिल्ल (ḍhilla).

ढूँढना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit ढुण्ढति (ḍhuṇḍhati, 'searches, seeks out'), via Prakrit ढुंढइ (ḍhuṇḍhaï).

rootFamily.gloss: to be found; to get/receive (with को); to meet (with से)

तक.etymology: Inherited from Prakrit तक्क (takka, 'up to, touching upon').

तकिया.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian تکیه (takya, 'support, bolster, pillow'), ultimately from Arabic تَكْأَة / اتِّكَاء ('leaning, cushion').

तख़्ती.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian تخته / تختی (takhta / takhtī, 'small wooden board, writing tablet'), diminutive of تخت (takht, 'plank, board, throne') with the suffix -ی (-ī). In South Asia, a तख़्ती was traditionally the handheld wooden board coated with clay on which pupils practiced calligraphy, as well as any small wooden or metal plaque/signboard.

तथा.etymology: A tatsama borrowing from Sanskrit तथा (tathā, 'so, thus, in that manner, and also'), derived from the demonstrative base त- (ta-, 'that') with the manner suffix -था (-thā, parallel to यथा yathā 'as'). Originally an adverb meaning 'thus/likewise', it evolved in formal Hindi prose into a clean coordinating conjunction meaning 'and, as well as'.

rootFamily.gloss: with; together with (के साथ); together (एक साथ)

तब.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit तदा (tadā, 'then, at that time'), via Prakrit तब्ब (tabba).

rootFamily.gloss: when (in a statement or time clause, never a question!)
just then; at that very moment; that explains why

तभी.etymology: Formed within Early Hindi by fusing तब (tab, 'then, at that time', inherited via Prakrit तब्ब from Sanskrit तदा tadā) with the exclusive emphatic particle ही (hī, < Prakrit हिअ < Sanskrit हि hi), coalescing -ब + ह- into aspirated -भ- (तभी).

morphemes.meaning: right then, at that exact moment

history.meaning: just then, at that very instant; that's why!

तभी.notes: Part of Hindi's symmetrical चार-way time set: अब -> अभी ('right now'), तब -> तभी ('right then / no wonder!'), कब -> कभी ('ever'), जब -> जभी ('the moment when').

तय.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic طَيّ (ṭayy, 'folding up, concluding, settling'), via Classical Persian طی (tay).

तरक़्क़ी.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic تَرَقٍّ (taraqqin, 'rising, advancement'), via Classical Persian ترقی (taraqqī).

तरफ़.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian طرف (taraf) from Arabic طَرَف (ṭaraf, 'side, edge, direction').

rootFamily.gloss: near (के पास); in one's possession ('to have')

तरह.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian طرح (tarh) from Arabic طَرْح (ṭarḥ, 'casting, design, manner, sort').

तराशना.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian تراشیدن / تراش (tarāš, 'carving, paring, shaping') + Hindi -ना.

rootFamily.gloss: to be engraved; to be dug

तश्तरी.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian تشت / تشتری (tasht / tashtarī, 'small basin, shallow dish, saucer'), a diminutive formed from تشت (tasht, 'bowl, basin', from Middle Persian tašt and Old Iranian *tašta-). Entering Hindustani through Mughal dining and tea service, it became the standard feminine noun for a teacup saucer or small serving plate.

तहख़ाना.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian تهخانه (tah-xāna, 'cellar, underground room'), from ته (tah, 'bottom, underneath') + خانه (xāna, 'house, room').

ताँबा.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit ताम्र (tāmra, 'copper, dark red metal'), via Prakrit तंब (tamba).

ताकि.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian تا که (tā ki, 'until that, in order that, so that'), combining Persian تا (tā, 'until, up to, so that', from Middle Persian tā and Old Persian *tāvat) with the complementizer که (ki, 'that'). Absorbed seamlessly into Hindustani syntax, ताकि always introduces a purpose clause governing the subjunctive mood.

ताज़ा.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian تازه (tāza, 'fresh, young, new'), from Middle Persian tāzag.

rootFamily.gloss: sweet; pleasant (of voice, music, or scent)

तान.etymology: A tatsama borrowing from Sanskrit तान (tāna, 'tone, musical note, melodic extension, thread'), derived from तन् (tan-, 'to stretch, draw out, resonate', cognate with Greek τόνος tónos and English 'tone'). In Hindustani music theory, तान denotes a rapid, extended melodic run or arpeggio stretching across an octave. It is feminine in Hindi.

तार.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian تار (tār, 'thread, string, wire'), from Middle Persian tār.

तारा.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit तारा (tārā, 'star, fixed star', from Proto-Indo-European *h₂stḗr, cognate with Greek ἀστήρ, Latin stēlla, and English 'star'). In Prakrit तारा / तार (tārā / tāra), the word shifted in Hindi to the masculine -आ declension as तारा (tārā), with regular plural तारे (tāre). It denotes both stars in the sky and drawn star marks.

तारीफ़.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian تعریف (ta'rīf) from Arabic تَعْرِيف (taʿrīf, 'making known, description, commendation').

ताल.etymology: A tatsama borrowing from Sanskrit ताल (tāla, 'clapping of hands, musical time/measure, rhythm, cymbal'), originally connected to striking the palms together to keep beat. In classical Indian musicology, ताल is the foundational system of rhythmic cycles and measures. In Hindi it is a masculine noun (distinct from its feminine sense 'pond/lake' from तड़ाग).

ताला.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit ताल / तालक (tālaka, 'bolt, latch, lock'), via Prakrit तालअ (tālaa).

ताली.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit तालिका / ताली (tālikā / tālī, 'palm of the hand, clapping of hands', feminine diminutive of ताल tāla 'palm, beat') via Prakrit ताली (tālī). In modern Hindi, तालियाँ बजाना ('to strike claps') is the universal idiom for applauding a performance or celebration.

तिरछा.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit तिरश्च / तिर्यञ्च् (tiraśca / tiryañc, 'oblique, transverse, going across', from तिरस् tiras 'across, askance'). Through Prakrit तिरिच्छ (tiriccha), syncope of the medial vowel yielded Hindi तिरछा (tirchhā), which adapted to the inflecting -आ adjective pattern. It contrasts directly with सीधा ('straight').

तीन.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit त्रीणि (trīṇi, 'three'), via Prakrit तिण्णि (tiṇṇi), from PIE *tréyes.

तीनों.etymology: Formed from तीन (tīn, 'three') + Hindi aggregative numeral suffix -ओं (-õ, 'all N').

तीस.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit त्रिंशत् (triṃśat, 'thirty'), via Prakrit तीस (tīsa).

तीसरा.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit तृतीय (tṛtīya) + सर extension, via Prakrit तइअ / तीसइ.

तीसवाँ.etymology: Formed regularly in Hindi by adding the productive ordinal suffix -वाँ (-vān, from Sanskrit -तम / Prakrit -वंत / -म) to the cardinal numeral तीस (tīs, 'thirty', from Sanskrit त्रिंशत् triṃśat via Prakrit तीस tīsa). Like all -वाँ ordinals above fourth, it inflects across gender and case as तीसवाँ / तीसवीं / तीसवें.

तुम.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit युष्मे / तुष्मे, via Prakrit तुम्हे (tumhe, 'you'), shifted to familiar singular and plural.

तुरंत.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit त्वरन्तम् (tvarantam, 'hastening, swiftly'), present participle of त्वर् ('to hurry').

rootFamily.gloss: right now; just now; still / yet

तू.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit त्वम् (tvam, 'thou, you sg.'), via Prakrit तुवं / तू, from PIE *túh₂.

तेज़.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian تیز (tēz, 'sharp, swift, pungent, keen'), from Middle Persian tēz.

rootFamily.gloss: slow; low; soft/quiet (of voice or light)
light (in weight, flavour, sound, or brightness); gentle

तेज़ी.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian تیزی (tēzī, 'sharpness, speed'), from تیز (tēz).

rootFamily.gloss: fast; heavy (rain); strong/sharp (salt, spice, sun, sound)

तैयार.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian تیار (tayyār, 'ready, prepared'), from Arabic طَيَّار ('swift, ready').

rootFamily.gloss: to make; to prepare; to build

तैयारी.etymology: Derived from the adjective तैयार (taiyār, 'ready, prepared') by adding the abstract feminine suffix -ई (-ī). The base तैयार was borrowed via Classical Persian تیار (tayyār) from Arabic طَيَّار (ṭayyār, 'ready to fly, nimble, alert', intensive of طَارَ ṭāra 'to fly'). In Hindi, तैयारी became the core everyday noun for preparations and arrangements.

तैरना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit तरति (tarati, 'crosses over, floats, swims', cognate with Latin trāns and English 'through') via Prakrit तरइ / तइरइ (taraï / taïraï). Vowel epenthesis and contraction of -aï- yielded the diphthong -ai- in Hindi तैरना (tairnā). It covers swimming, floating on water, and gliding smoothly on air currents.

तो.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit ततः (tataḥ, 'thence, then, therefore'), via Prakrit तओ -> तो.

rootFamily.gloss: then; at that time; तब तक 'until then'

तौर.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian طور (ṭaur, 'manner, mode, condition') from Arabic طَوْر (ṭawr, 'stage, condition, manner, kind'), from the root ط-و-ر (ṭ-w-r). Entering Hindustani through administrative and idiomatic prose, तौर became indispensable in fixed adverbial phrases such as के तौर पर ('as, by way of') and आम तौर पर ('usually').

तौलिया.etymology: Borrowed from Portuguese toalha ('towel') or early English towel, integrated into North Indian -इया masculine declension.

थपथपाना.etymology: Formed by reduplicating the imitative stem थप- (thap-, representing a soft flat slap or pat of the palm, compare थप्पड़ 'slap' and थाप 'palm-beat on a drum') with the transitive verbal suffix -आना (-ānā). Parallel onomatopoeic formations exist in Prakrit थप्पइ ('strikes lightly'). In Hindi, थपथपाना specifically expresses affectionate or reassuring patting.

थामना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit स्तम्भति / स्तभ्नाति (stambhati / stabhnāti, 'props up, supports, stops, holds firm'), via Prakrit थंभइ (thambhaï). Loss of initial s- in the cluster st- yielded aspirated th-, while simplification of the nasal cluster -mbh- with compensatory vowel lengthening gave Hindi थामना (thāmnā) alongside the regional variant थाम्हना.

rootFamily.gloss: to hold; to catch; to grasp
to handle; to look after; to hold steady
to stop (someone/something); to block; to hold back

थैला.etymology: Inherited from Middle Indo-Aryan थइल्ल (thaïlla, 'bag, pouch'), connected to Sanskrit स्थवि (sthavi, 'weaver's sack, pouch').

थोड़ा.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit स्तोक (stoka, 'a drop, a little, small amount'), via Prakrit थोअ + ड (thoaḍa).

rootFamily.gloss: less; little; fewer; कम से कम 'at least'
-ish; a bit (with थोड़ा/छोटा); which (in कौन सा)

दंग.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian دنگ (dang, 'bewildered, astonished, struck dumb').

rootFamily.gloss: belief; certainty (यक़ीन होना 'to believe, be sure')

दक्षिण.etymology: Learned Sanskrit borrowing दक्षिण (dakṣiṇa, 'right-hand; southern'), from Proto-Indo-European *deḱs- ('right').

दफ़्तर.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian دفتر (daftar, 'register, ledger; office') and Arabic دَفْتَر, ultimately from Ancient Greek διφθέρα (diphthéra, 'parchment').

दबाना.etymology: Causative/transitive in -आना from दबना ('to be pressed'), from Middle Indo-Aryan दब्बइ (dabbaï).

दरअसल.etymology: Borrowed from Perso-Arabic در اصل (dar aṣl, literally 'in origin / in reality').

rootFamily.gloss: truth (सच में? 'Really?'; सच कहूँ तो 'To tell the truth')

दरवाज़ा.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian دروازه (darwāza, 'door, gate'), from Middle Persian darwāzag, connected to در (dar, 'door', cognate with Sanskrit द्वार dvāra).

दराज़.etymology: Borrowed from English drawers (chest of drawers), adapted phonetically into Hindustani as दराज़.

history.meaning: sliding storage box in a desk

दरार.etymology: Inherited from Indo-Aryan verbal root दल् / दर् ('to split, burst', Sanskrit दारयति dārayati).

दरी.etymology: Native North Indian textile term दरी (darī, 'flat-woven cotton carpet'), borrowed into English as dhurrie.

दर्द.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian درد (dard, 'pain, ache'), from Middle Persian dard.

दवा.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic دَوَاء (dawāʾ, 'medicine, cure'), via Classical Persian دوا (dawā).

दशमलव.etymology: A modern Sanskritic mathematical compound formed from दशम (daśama, 'tenth', from दश 'ten') and लव (lava, 'fraction, small part, particle', from लू 'to cut'). Literally 'a tenth-fraction', दशमलव was standardized in Hindi mathematics and engineering education to translate 'decimal' and 'decimal point'. It behaves as an invariable masculine noun.

दस.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit दश (daśa, 'ten'), via Prakrit दस (dasa), from PIE *déḱm̥.

दस्तख़त.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian دستخط (dast-xatt, 'handwriting, signature'), from دست (dast, 'hand') + Arabic خَطّ (ḵaṭṭ, 'line, script').

दहलीज़.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian دهلیز (dihlīz, 'vestibule, entrance hall, threshold') from Arabic دِهْلِيز (dihlīz, 'corridor, entryway between the outer gate and house'), which itself was an early Arabic borrowing from Middle Persian or Aramaic (compare Persian دالان 'hall'). Entering Hindustani architectural vocabulary as a feminine noun, दहलीज़ specialized to mean the raised stone threshold or doorstep.

दाएँ.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit दक्षिण (dakṣiṇa, 'right-hand; south'), via Prakrit दक्खिण -> दाहिना -> दायाँ/दाएँ.

rootFamily.gloss: to the left; on the left
ahead; forward; further on; in front (के आगे)

दाग़.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian داغ (dāġ, 'brand, mark, stain, scar'), from Middle Persian dāg.

rootFamily.gloss: cloth; piece of fabric; clothes (in plural कपड़े)

दादा.etymology: Inherited Indo-Aryan kinship nursery word दद्दा / दादा ('paternal grandfather, elder brother').

दादाजी.etymology: Compound of Hindi दादा (dādā, 'paternal grandfather; elder brother') and the honorific enclitic जी (jī, from Sanskrit जीव jīva, 'life, soul').

history.meaning: life, living being (source of honorific जी)

दायाँ.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit दक्षिण (dakṣiṇa, 'right, southern, skilled', cognate with Latin dexter). Through Prakrit दक्खिण / *दाहिण (dakkhiṇa / dāhiṇa), loss of the medial -h- and nasalization of the final syllable yielded Hindi दाहिना (dāhinā) and its contracted standard form दायाँ (dāyān, feminine दाईं). It is the direct counterpart of बायाँ ('left').

दालचीनी.etymology: Compound of दारु / दाल ('wood, bark') + चीनी ('Chinese'), describing aromatic cassia/cinnamon bark.

दिक्कत.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian دقت (diqqat) from Arabic دِقَّة (diqqa, 'fineness, subtlety; difficulty, trouble').

दिखना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit दृश्यते (dṛśyate, 'is seen, appears'), via Prakrit दीसइ / दिखइ.

rootFamily.gloss: to look; to see; to check; (after -कर) to try out
to seem; to feel; to be attached; to take (time/effort)

दिखाना.etymology: Causative of दिखना / देखना, inherited via Prakrit दिक्खइ ('sees, shows').

rootFamily.gloss: to look; to see; to check; (after -कर) to try out
to look; to seem; to be visible

दिन.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit दिन (dina, 'day'), from Proto-Indo-European *dey- ('to shine').

दिमाग़.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian دماغ (dimāġ) from Arabic دِمَاغ (dimāḡ, 'brain').

rootFamily.gloss: mind; heart; mood / inclination (मन करना 'to feel like')

दिल.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian دل (dil, 'heart'), from Middle Persian dil, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *ȷʰŕ̥dayam.

rootFamily.gloss: mind; heart; mood / inclination (मन करना 'to feel like')

दिशा.etymology: A tatsama borrowing from Sanskrit दिशा / दिश् (diśā / diś, 'point of the compass, quarter of the sky, direction'), derived from दिश् (diś-, 'to point out, show', cognate with Greek δείκνυμι 'show' and Latin dīcere). In Hindi it behaves as a feminine -आ noun, forming plural दिशाएँ and oblique दिशाओं.

दीया.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit दीपक / दीप (dīpa, 'lamp, light'), via Prakrit दीवअ -> दीया.

rootFamily.gloss: Kavya (young woman managing reception at Aangan Haveli)

दीवार.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian دیوار (dīwār, 'wall'), from Middle Persian dēwār.

दुकान.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian دکان (dukān) from Arabic دُكَّان (dukkān, 'bench, shop'), ultimately from Aramaic/Sumerian.

दुकानदार.etymology: From Classical Persian دکاندار (dukāndār, 'shopkeeper'): دکان (dukān, 'shop') + دار (-dār, 'holder, keeper').

दूध.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit दुग्ध (dugdha, 'milk; milked'), past participle of दुह् ('to milk'), via Prakrit दुद्ध (duddha).

rootFamily.gloss: near (के पास); in one's possession ('to have')
ahead; forward; further on; in front (के आगे)

दूरी.etymology: From दूर ('far, distant', Sanskrit दूर dūra / Persian دور dūr) + abstract feminine suffix -ई.

rootFamily.gloss: near (के पास); in one's possession ('to have')

दूसरा.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit द्विसर / द्वितीय, via Prakrit दुसर (dusara, 'second, other').

देखना.etymology: Inherited from Middle Indo-Aryan देखइ (dekhaï, 'sees, looks at'), blend of Sanskrit द्रक्ष्यति (drakṣyati) and प्रेक्षते.

rootFamily.gloss: to look; to seem; to be visible

देना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit ददाति / दान (dāna, 'giving'), via Prakrit देइ (deï), from PIE *deh₃- ('to give').

rootFamily.gloss: to take; to buy; light verb for inward/self-benefiting action
to put; to place; to keep

देर.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian دیر (dēr, 'late, slow, long time'), from Middle Persian dēr (cognate with Sanskrit दीर्घ dīrgha, 'long').

देव.etymology: From Sanskrit देव (deva, 'heavenly, shining, divine'), from PIE *deywós ('sky, god').

rootFamily.gloss: Kabir (quiet architectural draughtsman staying in the attic room)

देवदार.etymology: Inherited/borrowed from Sanskrit देवदारु (devadāru, literally 'timber of the gods').

history.meaning: Himalayan cedar; tree of the gods

देवी.etymology: A tatsama borrowing from Sanskrit देवी (devī, 'goddess, queen, respected lady'), feminine of देव (deva, 'shining one, god, king', cognate with Latin dīvus / dea). From its primary sense of 'goddess' and royal title, it became a courteous formal term of address in Hindi (especially in the vocative plural देवियों, 'ladies!').

देसी.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit देशीय / देशी (deśīya / deśī, 'belonging to the country/region, native, local'), derived from देश (deśa, 'region, country, homeland') via Prakrit देसी (desī). In everyday Hindi, देसी (desī) conveys authenticity, local origin, and warm rustic charm—from homemade cooking to traditional crafts.

दो.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit द्वौ / द्व (dvau, 'two'), via Prakrit दो (do), from PIE *dwóh₁.

दोगुना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit द्विगुण (dviguṇa, 'twofold, double'), via Prakrit दुगुण (duguṇa).

दोनों.etymology: Aggregative plural in -ओं built on दो ('two'), marking totality ('both together').

rootFamily.gloss: with; together with (के साथ); together (एक साथ)

दोपहर.etymology: Inherited compound of दो ('two') + पहर ('watch of three hours', Sanskrit प्रहर prahara): literally 'the second watch of the day', i.e. midday.

दोबारा.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian دوباره (dōbāra, 'a second time, again'), from دو + باره.

दोस्त.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian دوست (dōst, 'friend'), from Old Persian dauštar- ('friend, one who loves'), cognate with Sanskrit जोष्टृ (joṣṭṛ).

mutual relation; each other (in आपस में)

दोहरा.etymology: Formed in Indo-Aryan from दो (do, 'two', from Sanskrit द्वि dvi) and the multiplicative suffix -हरा (-harā, from Sanskrit -सरा / -सृत 'fold, strand', compare एकहरा 'single' and तिहरा 'triple'). Literally 'two-stranded' or 'twofold', दोहरा inflects regularly as an -आ adjective and gave rise to the verb दोहराना ('to repeat').

rootFamily.gloss: to repeat; to go over again

दोहराना.etymology: Denominative verb from दोहरा ('double, twofold', from दो 'two').

दौड़ना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit द्रवति (dravati, 'runs, hastens') + extension -ड, via Prakrit दवडइ (davaḍaï).

धक्का.etymology: Expressive Middle Indo-Aryan noun धक्का (dhakkā, 'push, shock, shove').

धड़कन.etymology: Formed from Hindi verb stem धड़क- (dhaṛak-, 'to throb, palpitate') + verbal noun suffix -अन.

rootFamily.gloss: to beat; to pound (of the heart)

धड़कना.etymology: Expressive Indo-Aryan verb धड़कना imitating the rhythmic thumping beat of the heart (धड़-धड़).

धनिया.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit धान्यक / धनिका (dhānyaka / dhanikā, 'coriander plant or seed', related to धान्य 'grain'). Through Prakrit धणिया (dhaṇiyā), the word entered Hindi as धनिया (dhaniyā), taking masculine gender by alignment with culinary herbs like पुदीना ('mint'). It names both the fresh green herb and the dried spice.

धन्यवाद.etymology: Learned Sanskrit compound धन्यवाद (dhanyavāda): धन्य ('blessed, fortunate') + वाद ('speech, declaration of praise').

धातु.etymology: Learned Sanskrit borrowing धातु (dhātu, 'layer, element, mineral, metal'), from धा ('to place').

धारा.etymology: Learned Sanskrit borrowing धारा (dhārā, 'flow, current, continuous section or clause').

धारीदार.etymology: A hybrid Hindi-Persian adjective combining Indo-Aryan धारी (dhārī, 'stripe, streak, line', from Sanskrit धारा 'stream, edge, line') with the Persian possessive suffix -दार (-dār, 'having, bearing'). Literally 'bearing stripes', धारीदार is invariable across masculine and feminine nouns.

धीमा.etymology: Inherited from Prakrit धिम्म (dhimma, 'gentle, slow, subdued').

धीरे.etymology: Oblique/adverbial form of the adjective धीरा (dhīrā, 'slow, steady, gentle, calm'), inherited from Sanskrit धीर (dhīra, 'firm, steady, calm, gentle') via Prakrit धीर (dhīra). Using the oblique singular -ए ending adverbially, Hindi formed धीरे (dhīre, 'slowly, softly'). It applies equally to slow speed, gentle touch, and quiet voice.

rootFamily.gloss: fast; heavy (rain); strong/sharp (salt, spice, sun, sound)

धीरे-धीरे.etymology: Reduplication of धीरे (dhīre, 'slowly, gently'), from Sanskrit धीर ('steady, calm').

धुँधला.etymology: Derived from धुँध ('mist, haze') + suffix -ला, inherited from Sanskrit धूम्र ('smoky, hazy').

धुन.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit ध्वनि (dhvani, 'sound, tone, voice, resonant echo', from ध्वन् 'to sound'), via Prakrit धुनि / धुणि (dhuni / dhuṇi). Loss of the final short vowel yielded Hindi धुन (dhun), retaining feminine gender in Hindustani. While ध्वनि was reborrowed as a learned word for general sound, धुन specialized to mean a musical tune or an absorbing mental focus.

धुलना.etymology: Intransitive passive-sense verb formed in Hindi from the root धो- / धु- (from Sanskrit धाव् dhāv- 'to wash, rinse' or धु/धौत dhauta 'washed', via Prakrit धुव्वइ dhuvvaï) by attaching the intransitive-forming suffix -ल (-l-). Pairing with transitive धोना (dhonā, 'to wash'), धुलना expresses 'to get washed, wash out, or be washable'.

धूप.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit धूप (dhūpa, 'incense vapour, warmth, glow'), shifting in NIA to 'sunshine'.

धूल.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit धूलि (dhūli, 'dust, powder'), via Prakrit धूली (dhūlī).

rootFamily.gloss: to brush off; to dust; to sweep off

धैर्य.etymology: Learned borrowing from Sanskrit धैर्य (dhairya, 'firmness, constancy, patience'), from धीर (dhīra, 'steady, calm').

rootFamily.gloss: peace of mind; cosy calm; tranquillity

धोखा.etymology: Inherited from Prakrit धोक्खा (dhokkhā, 'illusion, perplexity, deceit').

rootFamily.gloss: truth (सच में? 'Really?'; सच कहूँ तो 'To tell the truth')

धोना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit धावति (dhāvati, 'washes, cleanses', distinct from homophonous धावति 'runs') via Prakrit धोवइ / धोअइ (dhovaï / dhoaï, influenced by the past participle धौत dhauta 'washed'). Contraction of -ova- to -o- gave the Hindi stem धो- (dho-) and infinitive धोना (dhonā). It is the basic verb for washing hands, dishes, clothes, and fruit.

ध्यान.etymology: Learned borrowing from Sanskrit ध्यान (dhyāna, 'meditation, heed, close attention'), from root ध्यै ('to contemplate').

ध्वनि.etymology: Learned Sanskrit borrowing ध्वनि (dhvani, 'sound, tone, resonance'), from ध्वन् ('to sound').

न.etymology: Inherited directly from Sanskrit न (na, 'not'), from PIE *ne ('not').

नंबर.etymology: Borrowed from English number, via Old French nombre from Latin numerus.

नक़द.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic نَقْد (naqd, 'ready money, cash, coin'), via Classical Persian نقد.

नक़ल.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian نقل (naql, 'transfer, transcript, copy, anecdote') from Arabic نَقْل (naql, 'carrying over, transferring, copying, narration'), from the root ن-ق-ل (n-q-l, 'to move from one place to another'). Just as Latin trānscrībere meant 'writing across', Arabic naql shifted from 'moving across' to 'copying text or imitating'. In Hindi it is feminine.

नक़्शा.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic نَقْشَة (naqša, 'drawing, design, map'), via Classical Persian نقشه (naqša).

नक़्शानवीस.etymology: A classical Perso-Arabic compound formed in Hindustani from नक़्शा (naqshā, 'map, plan, sketch', from Arabic نَقْشَة naqsha 'drawing, engraving') and the Persian agentive suffix -नवीस (-navīs, 'writer, drafter', present stem of Classical Persian نوشتن navishtan 'to write'). Literally 'map-drafter', it denotes a professional cartographer or draftsman.

नज़र.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic نَظَر (naẓar, 'sight, look, glance'), via Classical Persian نظر.

rootFamily.gloss: to look; to see; to check; (after -कर) to try out

नज़ारा.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian نظاره (nazāra) from Arabic نَظَارَة (naẓāra, 'looking, spectacle, view'), from root ن-ظ-ر ('to look').

rootFamily.gloss: to look; to see; to check; (after -कर) to try out

नदी.etymology: Inherited/borrowed from Sanskrit नदी (nadī, 'river, flowing stream').

नन्हा.etymology: Inherited affectionate Indo-Aryan adjective नन्हा ('tiny, tender, very young'), via Prakrit णण्ह.

नमक.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian نمک (namak, 'salt'), from Middle Persian namak.

नमकीन.etymology: Derived from नमक ('salt', from Persian نمک namak) + Persian suffix -ईन (-īn, 'characterised by').

नमस्ते.etymology: Learned Sanskrit greeting नमस्ते (namas te, literally 'a bow to you'), from नमस् ('bow, reverence') + ते ('to you').

नया.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit नव (nava) / नवक (navaka, 'new, fresh, young'), via Prakrit णवअ (ṇavaa), from PIE *néwos.

rootFamily.gloss: old (of things, places, memories, or friendships)

नरम.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian نرم (narm, 'soft, gentle, tender'), from Middle Persian narm.

rootFamily.gloss: light (in weight, flavour, sound, or brightness); gentle

नल.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit नल (nala, 'hollow reed, tube, water pipe').

नहाना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit स्नाति (snāti, 'bathes, washes'), via Prakrit ण्हाइ (ṇhāi).

नहीं.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit न हि (na hi, 'surely not') or नास्ति ('is not'), fused in Prakrit णहिं (ṇahiṃ).

नाक.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit नक्र / नासिका (nāsikā, 'nose'), via Prakrit णक्क (ṇakka).

नाज़ुक.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian نازک (nāzuk, 'delicate, slender, fragile, subtle'), continuing Middle Persian nāzuk ('tender, fine, delicate') from an Iranian root *nāz- ('tender, graceful'). Entering Hindustani through poetic, artistic, and everyday domestic speech, नाज़ुक serves as an invariable adjective for anything fragile, fine-textured, or sensitive.

rootFamily.gloss: light (in weight, flavour, sound, or brightness); gentle

नाटक.etymology: A tatsama borrowing from Sanskrit नाटक (nāṭaka, 'drama, play, actor'), derived from नट् (naṭ-, 'to dance, act, perform', itself a Prakritization of नृत् nṛt- 'to dance'). In classical Indian aesthetics (Nāṭyaśāstra), नाटक is the premier dramatic genre. In everyday Hindi it means both theatrical drama and 'put-on pretence'.

नाप.etymology: Deverbal noun from नापना (nāpnā, 'to measure'), inherited from Sanskrit ज्ञापयति / मापयति (māpayati, 'causes to measure') via Prakrit मापेइ / नापेइ.

rootFamily.gloss: number (room number, phone number, shoe size)

नापना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit ज्ञापयति / मापयति (māpayati, 'measures out'), via Prakrit मावइ / नापइ.

नाम.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit नामन् (nāman, 'name') via Prakrit नाम (nāma), reinforced by Persian نام (nām); from PIE *h₁nómn̥.

नाराज़.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian ناراض (nārāz, 'displeased'), from نا- (nā-, 'not') + راضی (rāzī, 'pleased').

नाल.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian نعل (naʿl, 'horseshoe, sandal, sole') from Arabic نَعْل (naʿl, 'sandal, shoe, horseshoe'), from the root ن-ع-ل (n-ʿ-l, 'to shoe a horse, wear sandals'). In Persian and Hindustani, نعل specialized for the U-shaped iron shoe nailed to a horse's hoof, adapting in Hindi without the Arabic glottal stop as feminine नाल (nāl).

नाव.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit नौ / नावा (nau / nāvā, 'boat, ship', from Proto-Indo-European *néh₂us, directly cognate with Greek ναῦς naûs and Latin nāvis). Through Prakrit नावा (nāvā), loss of the final vowel yielded Hindi नाव (nāv), retaining its feminine grammatical gender. It is one of the oldest maritime words in Indo-European.

नाविक.etymology: A tatsama borrowing from Sanskrit नाविक (nāvika, 'sailor, helmsman, pilot, pertaining to ships'), formed by vriddhi strengthening from नौ (nau, 'ship, boat') with the relational suffix -इक (-ika). Literally 'pertaining to a boat' or 'one who works a boat', it functions in Hindi both as an invariable masculine noun for a mariner and attributively ('nautical').

नाश्ता.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian ناشتا (nāštā, 'fasting; morning meal breaking the fast').

निकलना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit निष्क्रमति / निष्कलति (niṣkalati, 'goes out, issues forth'), via Prakrit निक्कलइ (nikkalaï).

rootFamily.gloss: to go; (as light verb) marks transition or completion

निकालना.etymology: Transitive/causative counterpart of निकलना (nikalnā, 'to come out, emerge'), formed by lengthening the stem vowel (अ -> आ). Both verbs trace back to Sanskrit निष्कालयति (niṣkālayati, 'drives out, expels') / निष्क्रामति via Prakrit निक्कालइ / णिक्कलइ (nikkālaï / ṇikkalaï). In everyday Hindi, निकालना covers taking out items, unpacking bags, and solving problems.

निगम.etymology: Learned Sanskrit borrowing निगम (nigama, 'guild, market town, corporate body').

निचला.etymology: Derived in Hindi from the adverb and postposition नीचे (nīche, 'below, beneath') by shortening the initial vowel and attaching the positional adjective suffix -ला (-lā, parallel to पिछला 'back/previous' from पीछे and अगला 'next/front' from आगे). Its base नीचे continues Sanskrit नीचैः (nīcaiḥ, 'low, below'). It inflects regularly for gender and number.

निजी.etymology: Formed from Sanskrit निज (nija, 'one's own, innate') + Hindi suffix -ई (-ī).

rootFamily.gloss: one's own (my, your, his, her, our, their)

निडर.etymology: Inherited prefixal formation नि- (from Sanskrit निर्-, 'without') + डर ('fear').

निभाना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit निर्वाहयति (nirvāhayati, 'carries through, accomplishes'), via Prakrit निब्बहइ.

rootFamily.gloss: with; together with (के साथ); together (एक साथ)

निमंत्रण.etymology: A tatsama borrowing from Sanskrit निमन्त्रण (nimantraṇa, 'calling in, inviting, invitation'), formed from the prefix नि- (ni-, 'in, down') and मन्त्रण (mantraṇa, 'counseling, addressing', from मन्त्र् 'to speak solemnly, summon'). Originally denoting a respectful summons to a feast or ceremony, it serves in modern Hindi as the standard formal noun for an invitation.

नियम.etymology: Learned Sanskrit borrowing नियम (niyama, 'restraint, rule, fixed observance'), from नि- + यम् ('to hold, regulate').

निरीक्षक.etymology: Learned Sanskrit borrowing निरीक्षक (nirīkṣaka, 'observer, examiner, inspector'), from निर्- + ईक्ष्.

निरीक्षण.etymology: Learned Sanskrit borrowing निरीक्षण (nirīkṣaṇa, 'careful examination, inspection').

निवाला.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian نواله (nawāla, 'mouthful, morsel of food').

निशान.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian نشان (nišān, 'mark, sign, emblem'), from Middle Persian nišān.

निशानी.etymology: Formed from Persian نشان (nišān) + -ई (-ī), Classical Persian نشانی (nišānī, 'souvenir, token').

नींद.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit निद्रा (nidrā, 'sleep'), via Prakrit निद्दा (niddā) with spontaneous nasalisation.

नींबू.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit निम्बू / निम्बूक (nimbūka, 'lime, lemon').

नीचा.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit नीच (nīca, 'low, situated below'), via Prakrit णीच (ṇīca).

नीचे.etymology: Oblique locative of नीचा ('low'), inherited from Sanskrit नीचैस् (nīcais, 'below, downward').

नीम.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit निम्ब (nimba, 'neem tree'), via Prakrit निंब (nimba).

नीला.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit नील (nīla, 'dark blue, indigo'), source of Persian نیل and English aniline / lilac.

ने.etymology: Inherited from Apabhramsha instrumental-agentive postposition ने / णें, replacing older Sanskrit instrumental endings.

नैपकिन.etymology: Borrowed from English napkin, diminutive of Old French nappe ('tablecloth').

नोटबुक.etymology: Borrowed from English 'notebook' through modern schooling, architecture, and office stationery in South Asia. English 'notebook' compounds 'note' (from Old French note and Latin nota 'mark, sign') and 'book' (Old English bōc). In Hindi it adopts feminine grammatical gender by analogy with किताब ('book') and कॉपी ('copybook').

नोटिस.etymology: Borrowed from English notice, from Old French notice / Latin nōtitia.

नोट्स.etymology: Borrowed from English notes (plural of note, from Latin nota).

नौ.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit नव (nava, 'nine'), via Prakrit णव (ṇava), from PIE *h₁néwn̥.

नौकरी.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian نوکری (nawkarī, 'service, employment'), from نوکر (nawkar, 'servant, employee').

नौवाँ.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit नवम (navama, 'ninth'), reshaped in Hindi from नौ + ordinal suffix -वाँ.

पंक्ति.etymology: Learned Sanskrit borrowing पङ्क्ति (paṅkti, 'row, line, series of five'), from पञ्चन् ('five').

पंखा.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit पक्षक (pakṣaka, 'wing, side, fan', diminutive of पक्ष pakṣa 'wing, feather'), via Prakrit पक्ख (pakkha) with spontaneous nasalization (*पंखा *paṅkhā) and masculine -आ ending. पंचर.etymology: Borrowed from English puncture, from Late Latin pūnctūra ('a pricking').

पंद्रह.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit पञ्चदश (pañcadaśa, 'fifteen'), via Prakrit पण्णरह (paṇṇaraha).

पकड़ना.etymology: Inherited from Middle Indo-Aryan पक्कडइ (pakkaḍaï, 'seizes, grips').

पकड़ाना.etymology: Causative of पकड़ना ('to hold, grasp'), meaning 'to place in someone's grip, hand over'.

पकना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit पचति / पच्यते (pacati / pacyate, 'cooks, bakes, ripens', from पच् pac-, cognate with Greek πέσσω, Latin coquere, and English 'cook') or directly the participial stem पक्व (pakva, 'cooked, ripe'). पका.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit पक्व (pakva, 'cooked, baked, mature, ripe', past passive participle of पच् 'to cook, ripen') via Prakrit पक्क (pakka). While the geminate form gave पक्का (pakkā, 'solid, permanent, well-baked'), the single-consonant variant पका (pakā) aligned with the verb पकना and specialized for ripe fruit and cooked dishes. It inflects regularly for gender and number.

पकाना.etymology: Causative inherited from Sanskrit पचति / पाचयति (pācayati, 'cooks, bakes, ripens').
