पक्का.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit पक्व (pakva, 'cooked, ripe, fired brick, mature, solid'), via Prakrit पक्क (pakka).

पचास.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit पञ्चाशत् (pañcāśat, 'fifty'), via Prakrit पंचासा (pañcāsā).

पच्चीस.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit पञ्चविंशति (pañcaviṃśati, 'twenty-five'), via Prakrit पच्चीसइ (paccīsaï).

पटरी.etymology: Feminine diminutive of पटरा / पाट (paṭrā / pāṭ, 'plank, flat wooden strip'), inherited from Sanskrit पट्ट / पट्टिका (paṭṭa / paṭṭikā, 'flat slab, plank, strip') via Prakrit पट्ट / पट्टी (paṭṭa / paṭṭī) with the diminutive suffix -री (-rī). Originally denoting a narrow wooden strip or roadside footpath, it naturally extended in the railway era to steel rail tracks.

पट्टा.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit पट्ट (paṭṭa, 'tablet, copperplate charter, lease document').

पट्टिका.etymology: A tatsama borrowing from Sanskrit पट्टिका (paṭṭikā, 'small flat plate, tablet, strip, document'), feminine diminutive of पट्ट (paṭṭa, 'flat slab, metal plate, royal charter'). While its tadbhava descendant पट्टी means a narrow strip or bandage, learned पट्टिका was retained in formal Hindi for commemorative metal or stone plaques and nameplates.

पट्टी.etymology: Feminine diminutive of पट्टा, from Sanskrit पट्टिका (paṭṭikā, 'narrow plate, ribbon, strip').

पड़ना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit पतति (patati, 'falls, alights'), via Prakrit पडइ (paḍaï).

rootFamily.gloss: is needed; is wanted; should (with infinitive)

पड़ोसी.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit प्रतिवेशिन् (prativeśin, 'living nearby, neighbour'), via Prakrit पडिवेसिअ.

पढ़ना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit पठति (paṭhati, 'reads aloud, recites, studies'), via Prakrit पढइ (paḍhaï).

पतला.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit प्रतनु / पत्रल ('thin, slender'), via Prakrit पत्तल (pattala).

पता.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit पत्रक / प्रत्यय ('token, trace, whereabouts'), giving Middle/Early Hindi पता ('trace, address, awareness').

पति-पत्नी.etymology: Sanskrit dvandva compound पति-पत्नी: पति (pati, 'husband, master', PIE *pótis) + पत्नी (patnī, 'wife', PIE *pótnih₂).

पत्ता.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit पत्र (patra, 'leaf, wing, page'), via Prakrit पत्त (patta).

पत्ती.etymology: Diminutive in -ई from पत्ता ('leaf'), inherited from Sanskrit पत्र (patra, 'leaf, wing, page') via Prakrit पत्त (patta).

पत्थर.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit प्रस्तर (prastara, 'flat stone, rock slab'), via Prakrit पत्थर (patthara).

पनीर.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian پنیر (panīr, 'cheese'), from Middle Persian panīr.

पन्ना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit पर्ण (parṇa, 'leaf, betel leaf, written leaf/page'), via Prakrit पण्ण (paṇṇa).

पर.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit उपरि (upari, 'above, upon') for 'on', and परम् (param, 'further, however') for 'but', merged in Prakrit परि / पर.

rootFamily.gloss: upstairs; above; on top of (के ऊपर)

परख.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit परीक्षा (parīkṣā, 'examination, test'), via Prakrit परिक्खा (parikkhā).

परखना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit परीक्षते (parīkṣate, 'looks around carefully, examines, tests', from परि- 'around' + ईक्ष् 'to see'). Through Prakrit परिक्खइ (parikkhaï), lowering of the vowel and loss of gemination produced the Hindi verb परखना (parakhnā) alongside the feminine noun परख ('assay, test, discernment'). It is the everyday tadbhava counterpart of learned परीक्षा करना.

rootFamily.gloss: to look; to see; to check; (after -कर) to try out

परत.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit पर्पट / परत ('thin layer, crust, fold').

परिवार.etymology: Learned Sanskrit borrowing परिवार (parivāra, 'surrounding circle, household, family').

परेशान.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian پریشان (parēšān, 'scattered, dishevelled, distressed').

परेशानी.etymology: From Classical Persian پریشانی (parēšānī, 'distress, trouble'), from پریشان (parēšān, 'scattered, troubled') + -ई.

परोसना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit परिवेषयति (pariveṣayati, 'waits upon, serves food around'), via Prakrit परिवेसइ.

पर्ची.etymology: Diminutive in -ई from पर्चा, borrowed from Classical Persian پرچه (parča, 'piece of cloth or paper, slip').

पर्दा.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian پرده (parda, 'curtain, screen, veil'), from Middle Persian pardag.

rootFamily.gloss: cloth; piece of fabric; clothes (in plural कपड़े)

पल.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit पल (pala, 'a tiny measure of time, one-sixtieth of a ghaṭikā; twenty-four seconds').

पलंग.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit पर्यङ्क (paryaṅka, 'bed, couch, litter'), via Prakrit पल्लंक (pallaṅka).

cognates.meaning: via Portuguese from the same Sanskrit word

पल्ला.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit पल्लव (pallava, 'sprout, shoot, lappet, skirt-hem') or पटल (paṭala, 'covering, leaf, shutter'), via Prakrit पल्ल / पल्लव (palla / pallava, 'hem, flap, panel'). With masculine -आ enlargement in Hindi, पल्ला (pallā) came to denote a hinged flap, door leaf, window shutter, or balance pan.

पसंद.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian پسند (pasand, 'approval, choice, pleasing'), from Middle Persian pasand.

rootFamily.gloss: mind; heart; mood / inclination (मन करना 'to feel like')

पसंदीदा.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian پسندیده (pasandīda, 'chosen, approved, favourite'), past participle of پسندیدن ('to approve, like').

पहचानना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit प्रत्यभिजानाति (pratyabhijānāti, 'recognises'), via Prakrit पच्चभिजाणइ.

पहनना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit परिदधाति / पिनह्यति (pinahyati, 'ties on, puts on attire'), via Prakrit पइण्हइ.

rootFamily.gloss: cloth; piece of fabric; clothes (in plural कपड़े)

पहला.etymology: Inherited from Prakrit पहिल / पडमिल्ल (pahila, 'first, foremost'), from Sanskrit प्रथम (prathama).

पहले.etymology: Oblique/adverbial form of पहला ('first'), inherited from Prakrit पहिले ('at first, earlier').

पहिया.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit प्रधि (pradhi, 'wheel rim'), via Prakrit पहिअ (pahia).

rootFamily.gloss: to turn; to rotate; to spin

पहुँचना.etymology: Inherited from Prakrit पहुच्चइ (pahuccaï, 'reaches, arrives, suffices'), from Sanskrit प्रभूयते.

rootFamily.gloss: to come down; to get off (a train); to descend

पाँच.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit पञ्च (pañca, 'five'), via Prakrit पंच (pañca), from PIE *pénkʷe.

पाइप.etymology: Borrowed from English pipe, from Old English pīpe.

history.meaning: hollow tube for water or steam

पाना.etymology: Regional/technical Indo-Aryan workshop noun पाना (pānā, 'grip-spanner, wrench'), related to पाणि ('hand, grip').

पानी.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit पानीय (pānīya, 'drinkable; water'), gerundive of पा (pā, 'to drink'), via Prakrit पाणीअ (pāṇīa).

पाबंदी.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian پابندی (pābandī, 'adherence, punctuality, restriction').

पार.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit पार (pāra, 'further bank, opposite shore, across'), from PIE *per- ('to cross over').

पारिवारिक.etymology: Learned Sanskrit vriddhi derivative पारिवारिक (pārivārika, 'relating to family'), from परिवार + -इक.

पाल.etymology: Hindi पाल (pāl) descends from Sanskrit पट्ट (paṭṭa) or प्रावार (prāvāra, covering, cloth, mantle) via Prakrit पवाल / पाल, referring to a stretched sheet of woven cloth. In maritime and riverine North Indian usage, the word specialized for a boat's canvas sail and protective awnings. The semantic link between an enclosing cloth sheet and a wind-catching sail is preserved across Indo-Aryan nautical vocabulary.

पालिका.etymology: पालिका (pālikā) is a learned borrowing (tatsama) from Sanskrit पालिका (pālikā), the feminine agentive noun derived from the root पाल् (pāl, 'to protect, guard, govern'). In Classical Sanskrit it meant a female guardian or caretaker, and in modern Hindi administrative terminology it was adopted in compounds like नगर पालिका ('municipality') and कार्यपालिका ('executive branch'). Its transparent derivational suffix -इका marks feminine institutional nouns.

पास.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit पार्श्वे (pārśve, 'at the side of, beside, near'), via Prakrit पस्से (passe).

rootFamily.gloss: with; together with (के साथ); together (एक साथ)

पिघलना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit प्रगलति (pragalati, 'drips, melts away'), via Prakrit पग्घलइ (pagghalaï).

पिछला.etymology: Derived from पीछे ('behind, after') + adjectival suffix -ला, ultimately from Sanskrit पश्चात (paścāt).

rootFamily.gloss: old (of things, places, memories, or friendships)

पियानो.etymology: Borrowed via English piano from Italian pianoforte ('soft-loud').

rootFamily.gloss: to ring (a bell); to play (a musical instrument)

पिलाना.etymology: पिलाना (pilānā) is the regular Hindi causative verb formed from पीना (pīnā, 'to drink'), which itself descends from Sanskrit पिबति (pibati, 'drinks') via Prakrit पिअइ (piai). When forming the causative in -आना, the long stem vowel of पी- shortens to पि-, and an epenthetic -ल्- is inserted between the vowel-final root and the causative suffix. This -ल्- insertion is a hallmark of Hindi vowel-final causative stems such as दिलाना and सिलाना.

cognates.meaning: to cause to drink; to serve a drink

पिसना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit पिनष्टि / पिष्यते (piṣyate, 'is ground, crushed'), via Prakrit पिसइ.

पीछे.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit पश्चात् (paścāt, 'behind, after, in the rear'), via Prakrit पच्छा -> पाछे / पीछे.

rootFamily.gloss: ahead; forward; further on; in front (के आगे)

पीतल.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit पित्तल (pittala, 'brass, bell-metal'), via Prakrit पित्तल (pittala).

पीना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit पिबति (pibati, 'drinks'), via Prakrit पिअइ (piaï), from PIE *peh₃- ('to drink').

पीला.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit पीतल / पीत (pīta, 'yellow, golden'), via Prakrit पीअल (pīala).

पुआल.etymology: पुआल (puāl) derives from Sanskrit पलाल (palāla, 'straw, stalk') through Prakrit पुलाल / पुआल (pulāla / puāla). The intervocalic -ल- weakened and dropped in Middle Indo-Aryan, yielding the hiatus vowel sequence -उआ- preserved in modern Hindi. Related rustic words across North India denote rice or wheat straw used in weaving hats, mats, and animal bedding.

पुकारना.etymology: पुकारना (pukārnā) traces back to a Prakrit expressive verbal base पुक्कारइ (pukkārai, 'cries out, shouts'), related to Sanskrit फुत्कार / पुत्कार (onomatopoeic cries or calls). The initial geminate -क्क- simplified to single -क- with compensatory adjustments in Hindi, producing the modern stem पुकार-. Its core sense encompasses shouting to draw attention, summoning someone, and addressing a person by a specific title.

rootFamily.gloss: to call; to invite; to summon

पुड़िया.etymology: पुड़िया (puṛiyā) is a diminutive feminine noun from Sanskrit पुटिका (puṭikā, 'small fold, pocket, packet'), derived from पुट (puṭa, 'fold, cavity'). Via Prakrit पुडिआ (puḍiā), intervocalic -ट- voiced and flapped to -ड़- in Hindi. Traditional Indian pharmacies and spice shops have long used folded paper पुड़िया sachets to measure single doses or small quantities.

history.meaning: small fold; leaf or paper packet

rootFamily.gloss: small leaf; herb leaf; tea leaf

पुदीना.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian پودینه / پودنه (pūdīna / pūdna, 'mint, pennyroyal'), from Middle Persian pūdag.

rootFamily.gloss: small leaf; herb leaf; tea leaf

पुराना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit पुराण (purāṇa, 'ancient, belonging to former times'), via Prakrit पुराण (purāṇa).

पुल.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian پل (pul, 'bridge'), from Middle Persian puhl, cognate with Avestan pərətu-.

rootFamily.gloss: across; beyond (के पार); पार करना 'to cross'

पुश्तैनी.etymology: Formed from Classical Persian پشت (pušt, 'back, generation, lineage') + Indo-Persian suffix -ऐनी.

पुस्तकालय.etymology: Learned Sanskrit compound पुस्तकालय (pustakālaya, 'house of books'), from पुस्तक + आलय.

पूछना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit पृच्छति (pṛcchati, 'asks, questions'), via Prakrit पुच्छइ (pucchaï), from PIE *preḱ- ('to ask').

rootFamily.gloss: to tell; to explain; to let someone know

पूरा.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit पूरक / पूर्ण (pūrṇa, 'filled, complete'), via Prakrit पूरअ (pūraa), from PIE *pleh₁- ('to fill').

पेंट.etymology: Borrowed from English paint, via Old French peindre from Latin pingere.

पेंसिल.etymology: Borrowed from English pencil, from Old French pincel and Latin pēnicillum ('fine brush').

पेच.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian پیچ (pēč, 'twist, coil, screw'), verbal noun stem of پیچیدن (pēčīdan, 'to twist').

पेचकस.etymology: Hybrid Persian–Hindi compound पेचकस: Persian پیچ (pēč, 'screw') + Hindi stem कस (from कसना kasnā, 'to tighten', Sanskrit कषति).

पेड़.etymology: Inherited from Middle Indo-Aryan पेड्ड / पिण्ड ('trunk, clump, tree'), connected to Sanskrit पिण्ड (piṇḍa, 'mass, trunk').

rootFamily.gloss: small leaf; herb leaf; tea leaf

पेन.etymology: Borrowed from English pen, from Old French penne and Latin penna ('feather quill').

पेस्ट्री.etymology: पेस्ट्री (pesṭrī) is a direct borrowing from English 'pastry', which entered English from Old French 'pastee' / 'paste' and ultimately Late Latin 'pāsta' ('dough'). Adopted into urban Indian bakery and café vocabulary, it regularly takes feminine grammatical gender in Hindi by analogy with native -ई nouns like मिठाई and रोटी.

पैंतीस.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit पञ्चत्रिंशत् (pañcatriṃśat, 'thirty-five'), via Prakrit पणतीसा.

पैकेट.etymology: Borrowed from English packet, diminutive of pack via Anglo-Norman.

rootFamily.gloss: cloth bag; tote bag; shopping sack

पैदल.etymology: पैदल (paidal) derives from Sanskrit पदाति (padāti) or पादतल (pādatala, 'sole of the foot') via Middle Indo-Aryan पयदल / पैदल, literally 'by foot'. In Old and Modern Hindi it solidified as an invariable adverb meaning 'on foot' and an attributive modifier for foot soldiers or hikers. The initial diphthong ऐ reflects contraction across the dropped intervocalic consonant.

rootFamily.gloss: to walk; to go; to move; to come along

पैमाना.etymology: पैमाना (paimānā) is a borrowing from Classical Persian پیمانه (paymāna, 'measure, measuring cup, scale'), derived from the Persian verb پیمودن (paymūdan, 'to measure'). Entering Hindustani through Mughal administration, carpentry, and architecture, it came to denote a physical ruler as well as an abstract yardstick or standard. In Hindi it regularly inflects like native -आ masculine nouns.

पैराग्राफ़.etymology: Borrowed from English paragraph, ultimately from Greek parágraphos ('side-stroke marking a section').

history.meaning: distinct section of a written text

पैसा.etymology: Early Modern Hindi पैसा (paisā, 'copper quarter-anna coin; money'), traditionally connected to Sanskrit पदांश (padāṃśa, 'quarter part').

पॉलिश.etymology: पॉलिश (polish) was borrowed from English 'polish', itself derived via Old French 'poliss-', stem of 'polir', from Latin 'polīre' ('to smooth, polish'). In Indian everyday Hindi it covers shoe polish, metal polish, and wood varnish, and combines easily with करना ('to polish'). It is uniformly assigned feminine gender.

पोंछना.etymology: पोंछना (ponchhnā) descends from Sanskrit प्रोञ्छति (proñchhati, 'wipes off, rubs clean'), a compound of प्र- and उञ्छ् ('to gather, sweep, wipe'), through Prakrit पुंछइ (puñchhai). The initial cluster प्र- simplified to प- while the nasalized palatal cluster -ञ्छ- yielded nasalized -छ- in Hindi. Its core meaning of wiping moisture or dust off a surface has remained unchanged for over two millennia.

पोता.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit पौत्र (pautra, 'son's son, grandson'), via Prakrit पोत्त (potta).

पोस्टकार्ड.etymology: Borrowed from British and Indian English postcard (attested from 1870 when postal administrations introduced open correspondence cards), combining post ('mail service', via French poste and Italian posta < Latin posita 'relay station') + card (via French carte < Latin charta).

history.meaning: open card sent through the post without an envelope

पोस्टकार्ड.notes: Masculine in Hindi; deeply familiar across India both for picture postcards and India Post's classic buff-yellow inland postal card.

पोस्टर.etymology: पोस्टर (posṭar) is an English loanword from 'poster', originally meaning a placard posted on a wall or post, from the verb 'to post' (Latin 'postis', doorpost or pillar). It entered modern Hindi through print media, theatre, and municipal notices. Like most consonant-final English borrowings denoting flat objects, it is masculine and invariable in the direct plural.

पौधा.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit पोतक (potaka, 'young shoot, sapling, young one'), via Prakrit पोअ / पौध.

rootFamily.gloss: small leaf; herb leaf; tea leaf

पौने.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit पादोन (pādona, 'less by a quarter'), from पाद ('quarter') + ऊन ('deficient, less').

rootFamily.gloss: a quarter past; plus a quarter (+¼)
half past; plus a half (with numbers 3 and above)

प्यार.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit प्रियकार (priyakāra, 'showing kindness, affection'), via Prakrit पिआआर.

प्यारा.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit प्रियकार / प्रिय (priya, 'beloved, dear'), via Prakrit पिआर (piāra).

rootFamily.gloss: sweet; pleasant (of voice, music, or scent)

प्याला.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian پیاله (piyāla, 'cup, goblet, bowl'), ultimately from Ancient Greek φιάλη (phiálē, 'broad shallow bowl').

प्याली.etymology: प्याली (pyālī) is the feminine diminutive of प्याला (pyālā, 'cup, goblet'), borrowed from Classical Persian پیاله (piyāla, 'cup, bowl'), which traces back to Middle Persian and Greek 'phiálē' ('shallow bowl'). In Hindi, the feminine suffix -ई creates the smaller, everyday domestic sense of a teacup or small bowl for tea, curd, or chutney. It is a staple word in North Indian hospitality.

प्रताप.etymology: From Sanskrit प्रताप (pratāpa, 'glowing heat, majesty, valour'), from प्र- + ताप ('warmth').

rootFamily.gloss: Mohan (warm, slightly absent-minded owner of Aangan Haveli)
Kavya (young woman managing reception at Aangan Haveli)

प्रेशर.etymology: Borrowed from English pressure, via Old French from Latin pressūra.

प्रोफ़ेसर.etymology: प्रोफ़ेसर (profesar) is borrowed from English 'professor', which derives from Latin 'professor' ('one who professes an art or science'), from 'profitērī' ('to declare publicly'). Introduced into India with nineteenth-century colleges and universities, it is used across Hindi both as an academic title and as a respectful term of reference for senior scholars.

प्लास्टिक.etymology: प्लास्टिक (plāsṭik) comes from English 'plastic', derived via Latin 'plasticus' from Ancient Greek 'plastikós' ('capable of being moulded'), from 'plássein' ('to mould, shape'). Adopted globally in the twentieth century for synthetic polymers, it entered Hindi unchanged in meaning as a masculine material noun.

प्लेट.etymology: प्लेट (pleṭ) is a borrowing from English 'plate', from Old French 'plate' ('thin sheet of metal') and Medieval Latin 'platta', rooted in Ancient Greek 'platýs' ('flat, broad'). Because it rhymes with and functions alongside native feminine tableware terms like तश्तरी and थाली, Hindi consistently assigns it feminine gender with the plural प्लेटें.

प्लेटफ़ॉर्म.etymology: Borrowed from English platform, from French plate-forme ('flat form').

फँसना.etymology: फँसना (phansnā) stems from Sanskrit स्पर्श (sparśa) or a Middle Indo-Aryan expressive root फंस- (phansa-, 'to stick fast, be snared'), possibly connected with Sanskrit पाश (pāśa, 'noose, snare') with aspiration transfer. Its nasalized vowel -अँ- reflects the older nasal cluster. In modern Hindi it forms a productive pair with the transitive verb फँसाना ('to trap, entangle').

cognates.meaning: to get stuck; to be trapped

rootFamily.gloss: to tuck in; to wedge; to slip (a note into a handle)

फँसाना.etymology: Causative of फँसना ('to be caught/wedged'), from Prakrit फंसइ.

rootFamily.gloss: slip of paper; short written note; chit
to put; to place; to keep

फटना.etymology: फटना (phaṭnā) derives from Sanskrit स्फटति (sphaṭati, 'bursts, splits open') via Prakrit फट्टइ (phaṭṭai). The initial sibilant cluster स्फ- simplified to aspirated फ- in Prakrit, and the geminate -ट्ट- shortened to single -ट- in Hindi. It retains the intransitive sense of splitting, bursting, or ripping on its own.

फ़र्श.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian فرش (farš) from Arabic فَرْش (farš, 'spreading out; carpet, paved floor').

rootFamily.gloss: woven cotton rug; flat-weave floor mat

फ़व्वारा.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic فَوَّارَة (fawwāra, 'jet of water, fountain'), via Classical Persian فواره.

फ़ाउंटेन.etymology: फ़ाउंटेन (fāunṭen) is borrowed from English 'fountain', from Old French 'fontaine' and Late Latin 'fontāna' ('spring of water'). In Hindi, while a courtyard water fountain is usually called फ़व्वारा, the English loanword फ़ाउंटेन became firmly established for stationery items like फ़ाउंटेन पेन ('fountain pen') and फ़ाउंटेन स्याही ('fountain-pen ink').

फ़िलहाल.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic فِي الْحَال (fī l-ḥāl, literally 'in the present state / at the moment'), via Persian فی‌الحال.

rootFamily.gloss: right now; just now; still / yet
then; at that time; तब तक 'until then'

फ़ैशन.etymology: फ़ैशन (faishan) comes from English 'fashion', derived via Old French 'façon' ('make, form, manner') from Latin 'factiō' ('a making, doing'). Entering urban Hindi during the colonial and modern eras, it covers clothing styles, social trends, and popular customs, taking masculine gender.

फ़ैसला.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic فَيْصَلَة (fayṣala, 'settlement, judgement, decision'), via Classical Persian فیصله.

rootFamily.gloss: settled; arranged; decided (तय करना 'to plan, arrange')

फ़ोन.etymology: Borrowed from English phone, clipped from telephone (Greek τῆλε 'far' + φωνή 'voice').

rootFamily.gloss: number (room number, phone number, shoe size)

फ़्रिज.etymology: Borrowed from English fridge, colloquial shortening of refrigerator.

फ़्रेंच.etymology: Borrowed from English French ('of or relating to France'), descending from Old English Frencisc and Proto-Germanic *frankiskaz ('of the Franks').

history.meaning: pertaining to France or its language

फ़्रेंच.notes: Invariable adjective in spoken Hindi (फ़्रेंच विंडो, फ़्रेंच टोस्ट), coexisting with literary फ़्रांसीसी.

फ़्रेम.etymology: फ़्रेम (frem) is borrowed from English 'frame', which originates from Old English 'framian' ('to profit, construct, build'). In Hindi it is universally used for picture frames, eyeglass frames, and structural borders, carrying masculine grammatical gender and taking -ओं only in the oblique plural.

फिर.etymology: Inherited from Prakrit फिरइ ('turns around, comes back'), used adverbially for 'again, next, then'.

rootFamily.gloss: then; at that time; तब तक 'until then'

फिसलना.etymology: Inherited Indo-Aryan verb फिसलना ('to slip, glide'), from Prakrit फिसल्लइ.

फुलाना.etymology: Causative of फूलना ('to swell, expand'), formed with -आ- (-ā-).

rootFamily.gloss: to swell; (साँस फूलना) to be out of breath
to make laugh; to cheer up

फूल.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit फुल्ल (phulla, 'blown, blooming flower'), via Prakrit फुल्ल (phulla).

फूलना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit फुल्लति (phullati, 'blooms, expands, swells').

rootFamily.gloss: to puff up; (मुँह फुलाना) to sulk, pout

फेंकना.etymology: Inherited from Middle Indo-Aryan फिक्कइ / फेंकइ ('flings, hurls').

rootFamily.gloss: to put; to place; to keep
to save; to protect; to spare

फेंटना.etymology: फेंटना (phenṭnā) is traced to a Middle Indo-Aryan verbal root फेंट- / फिट्ट- (pheṇṭ- / phiṭṭ-, 'to beat, strike, mix by beating'), linked to Sanskrit स्फिट् / स्फुट् or regional Prakrit culinary vocabulary. It originally meant beating or shuffling (including shuffling playing cards, ताश फेंटना) and whipping ingredients smoothly together. The nasalized vowel reflects the historical nasal+stop cluster -ण्ट-.

cognates.meaning: to beat; to whisk; to shuffle

rootFamily.gloss: to dial (a phone number); to mix; to match/compare

फैलना.etymology: फैलना (phailnā) derives from Middle Indo-Aryan फल्ल- / फइल- (phalla- / phaila-, 'to spread out, open wide'), related to Sanskrit प्रथति / स्फल् ('to expand, spread'). Through Prakrit फइलइ, the vowel sequence coalesced into the Hindi diphthong ऐ in फैल-. It denotes both physical expansion and the bleeding or smudging of ink on paper.

बँधना.etymology: Intransitive/passive counterpart of बाँधना ('to tie'), inherited from Sanskrit बध्यते (badhyate, 'is bound') via Prakrit बंधइ.

बंडल.etymology: बंडल (banḍal) is borrowed from English 'bundle', which comes from Middle English 'bundel' and is related to Dutch 'bondel' and the verb 'bind' ('to tie'). Adopted into South Asian postal, shopkeeping, and household Hindi, it refers to both tied bundles and wrapped parcels, carrying masculine gender.

बंद.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian بند (band, 'bound, fastened, closed'), from PIE *bʰendʰ- ('to bind').

rootFamily.gloss: to open (by itself / intransitively); to come open
to open; to unlock; to unwrap
to stop (someone/something); to block; to hold back

बंदरगाह.etymology: बंदरगाह (bandargāh) is a Classical Persian compound noun بندرگاه (bandargāh), combining بندر (bandar, 'port, haven, trading city') and گاه (gāh, 'place, station'). The element bandar derives from Middle Persian and ultimately shares roots with 'band' ('embankment, mooring'). It entered Hindustani through maritime commerce along the Indian Ocean coast.

बक्सा.etymology: Early nativised borrowing from English box with Hindi masculine -आ declension (बक्सा / बक्से / बक्सों).

बगल.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian بغل (baġal, 'armpit, side, flank').

rootFamily.gloss: near (के पास); in one's possession ('to have')

बगीचा.etymology: बगीचा (bagīchā) is borrowed from Persian باغیچه (bāghīcha, 'little garden'), formed from باغ (bāgh, 'garden, orchard') plus the Persian diminutive suffix -چه (-cha). In Hindi the long vowel ā in the first syllable shortened to a, and Persian घ was simplified to ग in everyday speech. It regularly inflects as a masculine -आ noun (बगीचे).

बचना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit वच्यते / वञ्चति (vañcati, 'escapes, avoids'), via Prakrit वच्चइ / बच्चइ.

rootFamily.gloss: to save; to protect; to spare

history.meaning: state of being a child; childhood

बचाना.etymology: Causative/transitive in -आना formed from बचना ('to be saved, escape').

rootFamily.gloss: to be left over; to be saved; to avoid

बच्चा.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit वत्सक (vatsaka, 'little calf, child'), via Prakrit वच्छअ (vacchaa).

बच्ची.etymology: Feminine counterpart of बच्चा, from Prakrit वच्छिआ (vacchiā).

बजना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit वाद्यते (vādyate, 'is sounded, rings'), via Prakrit वज्जइ (vajjaï).

rootFamily.gloss: to ring (a bell); to play (a musical instrument)

बजाना.etymology: Causative/transitive in -आना from बजना, inherited from Sanskrit वादयति (vādayati, 'causes to sound, plays music').

rootFamily.gloss: to ring; to chime; to strike (the hour)

बजाय.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian بجای (ba-jā-yi, literally 'in the place of'), from بـ ('in') + جای ('place').

rootFamily.gloss: to change; to swap; to replace

बजे.etymology: Frozen masculine plural/oblique perfective participle of बजना ('to strike, chime'): सात बजे = 'seven [hours] struck'.

rootFamily.gloss: to ring; to chime; to strike (the hour)

बटन.etymology: बटन (baṭan) is borrowed from English 'button', from Old French 'boton' ('bud, button'), related to 'bouter' ('to push out'). Upon entering Hindi, it expanded naturally from coat and shirt buttons to mechanical push-buttons and electrical switches on appliances. It is an invariable consonant-final masculine noun.

बड़ा.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit वड्र / वृद्ध (vṛddha, 'grown, large'), via Prakrit वड्ड (vaḍḍa).

बढ़ई.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit वर्धकि (vardhaki, 'carpenter, wood-cutter'), via Prakrit वड्ढइ (vaḍḍhaï).

rootFamily.gloss: to carve; to sculpt; to whittle

बढ़िया.etymology: Derived from बढ़ना ('to advance, excel', from Sanskrit वर्धते vardhate) + suffix -इया.

बताना.etymology: Denominative verb from बात ('word, matter'), from Sanskrit वार्ता (vārtā) via Prakrit वत्ता.

rootFamily.gloss: to explain; to help someone understand

बत्ती.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit वर्तिका (vartikā, 'lamp-wick, taper'), via Prakrit वत्तिआ (vattiā).

बदलना.etymology: Denominative verb built on Arabic loanword बदल (badal, 'exchange, replacement').

बदलाव.etymology: Derived within Hindi from बदलना (badalnā, 'to change') + abstract suffix -आव (-āv).

rootFamily.gloss: to change; to swap; to replace

बधाई.etymology: बधाई (badhāī) descends from Sanskrit वर्धापन (vardhāpana, 'congratulation, festivity on growth or birth', from वृध् 'to grow, prosper') via Prakrit वड्ढावणा / वधाइआ (vaḍḍhāvaṇā). In Hindi, initial व- shifted to ब- and the intervocalic -ढ- simplified to -ध-, yielding बधाई. Traditionally sung or offered at weddings, births, and auspicious milestones, it is today's standard word for congratulations.

बन.etymology: Borrowed from English bun ('small soft bread roll').

बनना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit वर्ण्यते / वन्यते or Prakrit बणइ (baṇaï, 'is made, is prepared, turns out').

rootFamily.gloss: to make; to prepare; to build

बनाना.etymology: Transitive/causative in -आना formed from बनना ('to be made, become').

rootFamily.gloss: to be made; to turn out; to become

बनावट.etymology: Derived within Hindi from बनाना (banānā, 'to make, fashion') + abstract feminine suffix -आवट (-āvaṭ).

rootFamily.gloss: to make; to prepare; to build

बराबर.etymology: बराबर (barābar) is a borrowing from Classical Persian برابر (barābar, 'abreast, equal, level, opposite'), literally 'breast to breast', formed from بر (bar, 'chest, on') + آ (ā, linking vowel) + بر (bar, 'chest'). Entering Hindustani in the medieval period, it gained wide spatial, mathematical, and figurative currency for anything level, matched, or equivalent.

बर्फ़.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian برف (barf, 'snow, ice'), from Middle Persian wafr.

rootFamily.gloss: winter; cold weather (often plural सर्दियों में 'in winter')

बर्बाद.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian برباد (barbād, literally 'given to the wind; ruined').

rootFamily.gloss: to save; to protect; to spare

बल.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit वल / वलि (vali, 'fold, wrinkle, twist; curve'), homophonous with Sanskrit बल (bala, 'strength').

rootFamily.gloss: to turn; to bend; to be folded

बल्कि.etymology: बल्कि (balki) is borrowed from Classical Persian بلکه (balke, 'rather, on the contrary, nay even'), itself a compound of Persian بل (bal, from Arabic بل 'nay, rather') and the subordinating particle که (ke, 'that'). Adopted early into Hindustani prose and conversation, it serves as the primary corrective conjunction following a negated statement.

बल्ब.etymology: Borrowed from English bulb ('electric light bulb'), from Latin bulbus.

बस.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian بس (bas, 'enough, sufficient, only'), from Middle Persian bas.

rootFamily.gloss: just; a little; kindly (polite request softener)

बहना.etymology: बहना (bahnā) descends from Sanskrit वहति (vahati, 'flows, carries, blows') through Prakrit वहइ (vahai). As in many inherited Indo-Aryan words in Hindi, initial व- shifted regularly to ब-, yielding the stem बह-. It preserves both the liquid sense of flowing and the older Vedic and Classical sense of wind moving.

बहस.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic بَحْث (baḥṯ, 'inquiry, discussion, debate'), via Classical Persian بحث (bahs).

बहुत.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit बहुत्व / प्रभूत (bahu, 'much, abundant, many'), via Prakrit बहुत्त (bahutta).

rootFamily.gloss: very, very much; warm/heartfelt (in thanks and wishes)

बहुत-बहुत.etymology: Intensifying reduplication of बहुत ('very, much'), standard in warm expressions of gratitude.

बाँधना.etymology: बाँधना (bāndhnā) derives from Sanskrit बध्नाति (badhnāti, 'binds, ties', root बन्ध्) via Prakrit बन्धइ (bandhai). In the development to Hindi, the consonant cluster -न्ध- simplified to -ध- with compensatory lengthening and nasalization of the preceding vowel, yielding बाँध-. Its forms remain central to everyday physical and figurative binding expressions.

बाएँ.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit वाम (vāma, 'left, left-hand'), via Prakrit वाम -> बायाँ/बाएँ.

rootFamily.gloss: to the right; on the right
to turn; to bend; to be folded

बाक़ी.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic بَاقٍ / بَاقِي (bāqī, 'remaining, enduring, balance'), via Classical Persian باقی.

rootFamily.gloss: to be left over; to be saved; to avoid

बाज़ार.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian بازار (bāzār, 'market'), from Middle Persian wāzār.

बाज़ी.etymology: बाज़ी (bāzī) is borrowed from Classical Persian بازی (bāzī, 'play, game, sport, wager'), derived from the Persian verbal stem باز- (bāz-, 'to play, lose/stake') from باختن (bākhtan). Entering Hindustani through courtly games, chess, and literature, it became embedded in idiomatic phrases such as बाज़ी जीतना and बाज़ी मारना ('to win the contest or day').

rootFamily.gloss: to win; to overcome; to beat

बात.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit वार्ता (vārtā, 'news, tidings, talk, matter'), via Prakrit वत्ता (vattā).

rootFamily.gloss: to speak; to say; to talk

बाथरूम.etymology: Borrowed from English bathroom, compound of bath (Old English bæþ, 'warm immersion washing') + room (Old English rūm, 'space, chamber').

history.meaning: room equipped for bathing and washing

बाथरूम.notes: Masculine in Hindi (कमरे के साथ अटैच बाथरूम), preferred in everyday urban speech over formal स्नानघर.

बाद.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic بَعْد (baʿd, 'after, afterwards'), via Classical Persian بعد (baʿd -> bād).

rootFamily.gloss: then; at that time; तब तक 'until then'

बादल.etymology: बादल (bādal) traces back to Sanskrit वारिद (vārida, 'water-giver, raincloud') or वार्दल (vārdala, 'rainy weather') via Prakrit वद्दल / बाअल (vaddala / bāala). Initial व- shifted to ब- in Hindi, while the cluster simplified with compensatory lengthening of the first vowel. It serves as the primary spoken Hindi term for a raincloud or sky cloud.

बादाम.etymology: बादाम (bādām) comes from Classical Persian بادام (bādām, 'almond'), continuing Middle Persian 'wādām' and Old Iranian roots for the almond tree and nut. Brought to North India through Central Asian and Persian trade and culinary traditions, it became indispensable in South Asian sweets, breads, and festive baking.

बाप.etymology: Inherited from Middle Indo-Aryan बप्प (bappa, 'father'), an expressive kinship word widespread across Indo-Aryan.

rootFamily.gloss: oh!; hey!; wait a moment! (surprise or sudden realisation)
Ram (invoked in mild everyday exclamations like हाय राम!)

बायाँ.etymology: बायाँ (bāyān) descends from Sanskrit वाम (vāma, 'left, reverse, pleasant') via Prakrit वामअ / वायाँ (vāmaa). Initial व- shifted to ब- in Hindi and the intervocalic -म- lenited into nasalization (-याँ), giving the inflecting pair बायाँ / बाईं / बाएँ. It stands opposite दायाँ ('right').

बार.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit वार (vāra, 'turn, appointed time, occasion').

history.meaning: turn; time; day of the week

cognates.meaning: -वार suffix for days of the week

बार-बार.etymology: Distributive reduplication of बार (bār, 'turn, time', from Sanskrit वार).

बारह.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit द्वादश (dvādaśa, 'twelve'), via Prakrit बारह (bāraha).

बारिश.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian بارش (bāriš, 'rain, rainfall'), verbal noun from باریدن (bārīdan, 'to rain').

बारी-बारी.etymology: बारी-बारी (bārī-bārī) is a distributive reduplication of बारी (bārī, 'turn, time, occasion'), which descends from Sanskrit वार (vāra, 'turn, appointed time, day') via Prakrit वारिया (vāriyā). Initial व- shifted to ब- in Hindi. Repeating the noun creates an adverbial expression meaning 'by turns' or 'in alternation'.

rootFamily.gloss: one each; one by one; every single

बारे.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian باره (bāra, 'regard, respect, matter, turn'), used in درباره / के बारे में.

बाहर.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit बहिर् / बाह्य (bahir, 'outside, out of doors'), via Prakrit बाहिर (bāhira).

बिक्री.etymology: Derived within Indo-Aryan from बिकना ('to be sold'), from Sanskrit विक्रय (vikraya, 'sale').

बिखेरना.etymology: बिखेरना (bikhernā) derives from Sanskrit विकिरति (vikirati, 'scatters, pours out', from वि- + कृ) via Prakrit विक्खिरइ / विक्खेरइ (vikkhirai). Initial वि- shifted to बि- and the geminate -क्ख- simplified to -ख- in Hindi, while -ए- marks the transitive/causative vowel grade opposite intransitive बिखरना.

rootFamily.gloss: to pour; to put in; to add

बिजली.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit विद्युल्लता / विद्युत् (vidyut, 'lightning, flash'), via Prakrit विज्जुलिआ (vijjuliā).

बिताना.etymology: Causative of बीतना ('to pass, elapse'), inherited from Sanskrit व्यती- ('to pass by').

rootFamily.gloss: peace of mind; cosy calm; tranquillity

बिना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit विना (vinā, 'without, except'), via Prakrit विणा (viṇā).

rootFamily.gloss: with; together with (के साथ); together (एक साथ)

बिल्कुल.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic بِالْكُلّ (bi-l-kull, literally 'in the entirety, wholly'), via Classical Persian بالکل.

बीच.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit विच् / वृत्य or Middle Indo-Aryan विच्च (vicca, 'interval, midst, middle').

बीचोंबीच.etymology: बीचोंबीच (bīchonbīch) is an emphatic iterative compound of बीच (bīch, 'middle, centre'), linked with the emphatic oblique-plural infix -ओं- (comparable to दिनोंदिन and हाथोंहाथ). The base word बीच descends from Sanskrit वीचि / मध्य-विच् or Prakrit विच्च (vicca, 'interval, middle'). The reduplicated construction intensifies precision to mean 'right at the exact centre'.

rootFamily.gloss: middle; centre (के बीच 'between / in the middle of')

बीस.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit विंशति (viṃśati, 'twenty'), via Prakrit वीसइ (vīsaï), from PIE *wídḱm̥ti.

बुआ.etymology: बुआ (buā) derives from Sanskrit पितृष्वसृ (pitṛṣvasṛ, 'father's sister') or affectionate Prakrit पिउच्छा / बुआ (piucchā / buā, also connected to nursery/respectful address बऊ / बुआ for an elder woman). Hindi preserves distinct kinship terms for maternal versus paternal aunts, with बुआ specifically denoting the father's sister.

बुक.etymology: Borrowed from English book / booked (in the hospitality and travel reservation sense).

history.meaning: to register or reserve in a ledger

बुकिंग.etymology: Borrowed from English booking ('reservation entered in a register').

बुधवार.etymology: Learned Sanskrit compound बुधवार (budhavāra, 'day of Mercury / Wednesday').

बुनना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit वयति / उत (uta, 'woven'), via Prakrit बुणइ (buṇaï, 'weaves').

rootFamily.gloss: woven cotton rug; flat-weave floor mat
cloth; piece of fabric; clothes (in plural कपड़े)

बुरा.etymology: Inherited from Prakrit बुर (bura, 'bad, defective, wicked').

बुलबुला.etymology: Echoic formation shared across Indo-Aryan and Persian بلبلہ / बुलबुला imitating bubbling water.

बुलाना.etymology: Causative formation from बोलना ('to speak, utter'), via Middle Indo-Aryan बोल्लावेइ.

बूँद.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit बिन्दु (bindu, 'drop, dot, globule'), via Prakrit बिंदु / बुंद.

बेंच.etymology: बेंच (bench) is a loanword from English 'bench', which comes from Old English 'benc' ('long seat', cognate with German 'Bank'). Introduced into Indian schools, parks, courts, and music rooms during the British period, it was absorbed as a feminine noun in Hindi, taking the plural बेंचें.

history.meaning: long seat for two or more

बेकर.etymology: बेकर (bekar) is borrowed from English 'baker', derived from Old English 'bæcere' ('one who bakes', from 'bacan'). In modern urban Hindi it sits alongside native terms like नानबाई and हलवाई specifically for Western-style bread and cake bakers.

बेकरी.etymology: बेकरी (bekarī) is borrowed from English 'bakery', formed from 'bake' plus the place-denoting suffix '-ery'. Its final -y sound aligned cleanly with native Hindi feminine nouns ending in -ई, making it feminine and fully regular in plural inflection (बेकरियाँ).

history.meaning: place where bread and cakes are baked

बेकार.etymology: बेकार (bekār) is a Persian compound adjective بیکار (bīkār), formed from the privative prefix بی (bī-, 'without') and کار (kār, 'work, use, business'). Originally meaning 'unemployed, without work', it broadened in Hindustani to mean 'useless, wasted, futile, or broken'. It never inflects for gender or number.

बेकिंग.etymology: बेकिंग (beking) is a modern borrowing from English 'baking', the gerund of 'bake' (Old English 'bacan', 'to cook by dry heat'). Adopted into urban Hindi culinary and café speech, it names the craft or process of oven baking and takes feminine agreement as an abstract activity noun.

history.meaning: cooking in an oven by dry heat

बेचना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit विक्रीणाति / व्यययति, via Prakrit वेच्चइ ('spends, sells').

बेजान.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian بی‌جان (bē-jān, 'without life, inanimate'), from बे- + जान.

बेटा.etymology: Inherited from Middle Indo-Aryan बेट्ट / बिट्ट (beṭṭa, 'child, boy, youngster').

बेरी.etymology: बेरी (berī) is borrowed from English 'berry', from Old English 'berie' ('grape, berry'). While native Indian jujube berries are called बेर (ber), the English borrowing बेरी is widely used in baking and café menus for strawberries, blueberries, and summer berries, naturally taking feminine -ई declension.

बेशक.etymology: बेशक (beshak) is a compound adverb formed from the Persian privative prefix بی (bē-, 'without') and Arabic شک (shakk, 'doubt'), literally meaning 'without doubt'. Widely naturalized across Hindi-Urdu speech, it serves as an idiomatic equivalent to 'of course' or 'certainly'.

rootFamily.gloss: completely; absolutely; (with नहीं) not at all

बेस.etymology: बेस (bes) is borrowed from English 'bass', which derives from Old French 'bas' ('low') and Late Latin 'bassus' ('short, low'), altered in spelling under Italian 'basso'. In Indian musical and audio vocabulary it refers to the lowest pitch register or bassline, treated as a masculine noun.

बेहतर.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian بهتر (bihtar, 'better'), comparative of به (bih, 'good').

बेहद.etymology: Indo-Persian compound from Persian بے (bē-, 'without') + Arabic حد (ḥadd, 'limit, boundary'), literally 'boundless'.

बैग.etymology: Borrowed from English bag ('flexible carrying sack, handbag, or travel valise'), which entered Middle English bagge from Old Norse baggi ('pack, bundle, bag').

history.meaning: pack, bundle -> carrying sack or travel bag
travelling bag, shoulder bag, backpack, handbag

बैग.notes: Masculine in Hindi (मेरा बैग भारी है); covers backpacks, handbags, and overnight duffels, while native थैला usually means a cloth market tote.

बैज.etymology: बैज (baij) is borrowed from English 'badge', from Middle English 'bage' (probably via Anglo-French from Medieval Latin 'bagia', 'distinctive mark or emblem'). Adopted into Indian institutional, school, and event vocabulary, it functions as a regular consonant-final masculine noun.

बैठना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit उपविशति / उपविष्ट (upaviṣṭa, 'seated'), via Prakrit उवइट्ठइ -> बइट्ठइ (baïṭṭhaï).

rootFamily.gloss: to stop; to wait; to stay overnight (at an inn)

बॉयलर.etymology: Borrowed from English boiler ('water-heating tank'), from Old French boillir.

बॉस.etymology: बॉस (bos) is borrowed from English 'boss', which entered American English from Dutch 'baas' ('master, foreman'). In contemporary Indian workplaces and colloquial Hindi, it is widely used both respectfully and playfully when addressing a manager, shop owner, or friend.

बोतल.etymology: Early borrowing from Portuguese botelha or English bottle, adapted as a feminine consonant-stem noun बोतल / बोतलें.

बोरिंग.etymology: Borrowed from nineteenth- and twentieth-century English boring ('tedious, dull, wearisome'), participial adjective of bore ('to weary by dull repetition', figuratively pressing on a listener slowly like an auger boring wood).
बोरिंग.notes: Invariable adjective across genders and numbers in Hindi (बोरिंग किताब, बोरिंग दिन); pairs with बोर होना ('to get bored').

बोर्ड.etymology: Borrowed from English board ('signboard, wooden plank').

बोलना.etymology: Inherited from Prakrit बोल्लइ (bollaï, 'speaks, utters'), widely attested across Middle Indo-Aryan.

rootFamily.gloss: to tell; to explain; to let someone know

ब्रश.etymology: ब्रश (brash) is borrowed from English 'brush', from Old French 'broisse' ('brush, brushwood') and ultimately Vulgar Latin 'brustia'. It has largely replaced older terms in modern Hindi for painting, baking, and grooming brushes, taking masculine grammatical gender.

ब्रेड.etymology: Borrowed from English bread (specifically baker's yeast loaf bread, distinct from unleavened रोटी).

भंडार.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit भाण्डागार (bhāṇḍāgāra, 'storehouse, treasury, pantry'), from भाण्ड ('vessel, goods') + आगार ('house').

भगवान.etymology: Learned borrowing from Sanskrit भगवान् (bhagavān, nominative singular of भगवत् bhagavat, 'blessed,fortunate,revered Lord').

rootFamily.gloss: Ram (invoked in mild everyday exclamations like हाय राम!)

भटकना.etymology: भटकना (bhaṭaknā) traces to a Middle Indo-Aryan verbal root भट्ठ- / भटक- (bhaṭṭha- / bhaṭak-, 'to fall away, stray, wander'), connected with Sanskrit भ्रष्ट (bhraṣṭa, 'strayed, fallen, lost'). The retroflex stop -ट- preserves the Prakrit reflex of the Sanskrit cluster, while the suffix -क- adds a frequentative sense of aimless wandering.

भरना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit भरति (bharati, 'bears, fills'), via Prakrit भरइ, from PIE *bʰer-.

rootFamily.gloss: assent; nod of agreement (हामी भरना 'to nod in agreement')

भरा.etymology: Perfective participle of भरना ('to fill'), inherited from Sanskrit भृत / भरति (bharati, 'fills, bears') via Prakrit भरइ.

भरोसा.etymology: भरोसा (bharosā) descends from Sanskrit वरवस / परावस (or भद्राशा bhadrāśā, 'good hope, confident expectation') via Prakrit भरवसा / भरोसअ (bharavasā). The contraction of -अव- into -ओ- is characteristic of Western Hindi phonological development. Today it expresses both interpersonal trust and reliance on someone's responsibility.

rootFamily.gloss: with; together with (के साथ); together (एक साथ)

भरोसेमंद.etymology: Hybrid Indo-Persian adjective: Hindi भरोसा ('trust, reliance') + Persian suffix -मंद (-mand).

भला.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit भद्र (bhadra, 'auspicious, good, gracious, kind'), via Prakrit भल्ल (bhalla).

भवन.etymology: Learned Sanskrit borrowing भवन (bhavana, 'dwelling, mansion, building'), from भू ('to become, exist').

भाई.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit भ्रातृ (bhrātṛ, 'brother'), via Prakrit भाइअ (bhāia), from PIE *bʰréh₂tēr.

भागदौड़.etymology: Hindi dvandva verbal-stem compound: भाग (from भागना 'to flee, run') + दौड़ (from दौड़ना 'to sprint').

rootFamily.gloss: to run; to rush; to hurry off

भागना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit भज्यते / भग्न (bhagna, 'broken, routed, fled'), via Prakrit भग्गइ (bhaggaï).

rootFamily.gloss: rush; hustle and bustle; running around

भारी.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit भारिन् (bhārin, 'bearing a load, heavy'), from भार ('burden, weight').

rootFamily.gloss: light (in weight, flavour, sound, or brightness); gentle

भारी-भरकम.etymology: Expressive Hindi compound combining भारी ('heavy') + भरकम ('weighty, imposing').

rootFamily.gloss: big; large; elder; very (in expressions like बड़े शौक़ से)

भाव.etymology: भाव (bhāv) is a learned borrowing (tatsama) from Sanskrit भाव (bhāva, 'being, state, condition, value, sentiment'), derived from the root भू (bhū, 'to become, be'). In commercial Hindi it specialized to mean market rate or price, while in literature and music it retains the classical meaning of mood, sentiment, or expression.

भावुकता.etymology: Learned Sanskrit formation भावुकता (bhāvukatā, 'emotional sensitivity, sentiment'), from भावुक + -ता.

भाषण.etymology: Learned Sanskrit borrowing भाषण (bhāṣaṇa, 'speaking, talk, formal speech'), from भाष् ('to speak').

rootFamily.gloss: to speak; to say; to talk

भिजवाना.etymology: भिजवाना (bhijvānā) is the double-causative verb formed from भेजना (bhejnā, 'to send'), which derives from Prakrit भिज्जइ / भेअइ (bhijjai, connected to Sanskrit प्रेषयति / अभ्याज-). As regular in Hindi causative morphology, adding the -वा- suffix shortens the stem vowel ए to इ, yielding भिजवा-. It highlights delegation of the act of sending.

rootFamily.gloss: to call; to invite; to summon

भी.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit अपि (api, 'also, even'), combined with emphatic हि -> Prakrit बि / भि -> भी.

rootFamily.gloss: then (after अगर/जब); as for (topic/contrast); why don't you!

भीगा.etymology: Perfective adjectival participle of भीगना ('to get wet, be soaked'), via Prakrit भिज्जइ.

भुना.etymology: भुना (bhunā) is the adjectival past participle of भूनना (bhūnnā, 'to roast, parch, fry'), which descends from Sanskrit भृज्जति / भर्जयति (bhṛjjati / bharjayati, 'roasts, fries') via Prakrit भुज्जइ / भुणइ. The vowel shortening from ऊ to उ reflects the intransitive/stative stem used to form the passive-participial modifier meaning 'roasted'.

भूखा.etymology: Derived from भूख ('hunger'), inherited from Sanskrit बुभुक्षा (bubhukṣā, 'desire to eat, hunger') via Prakrit बुभुक्खा -> भुक्खा.

भूरा.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit बभ्रु (babhru, 'reddish-brown, tawny'), via Prakrit भूर (bhūra), from PIE *bʰébʰrus ('brown; beaver').

भूर्ज.etymology: भूर्ज (bhūrj) is a learned borrowing (tatsama) from Sanskrit भूर्ज (bhūrja, 'the Himalayan birch tree, Betula utilis'), a word with deep Indo-European cognates including English 'birch' and Latin 'fraxinus' (from PIE *bherHǵos, 'shining, white-barked tree'). In South Asia its pale bark and smooth timber have been prized since antiquity for manuscripts and fine woodwork.

भूलना.etymology: Inherited from Prakrit भुल्लइ (bhullaï, 'forgets, errs, goes astray').

भेजना.etymology: Inherited from Prakrit भिज्जइ / भेज्जइ (bhejjaï, 'sends, dispatches').

rootFamily.gloss: to give; to let (after -ने); light verb marking outward/completed action

भैया.etymology: Affectionate/diminutive Indo-Aryan form of भाई, from Sanskrit भ्रातृक (bhrātṛka).

भोजपत्र.etymology: भोजपत्र (bhojpatra) is a Sanskrit-derived compound (tatsama/semi-tatsama) from भूर्ज (bhūrja, 'birch') + पत्र (patra, 'leaf, sheet'), evolving through Prakrit भोज्जपत्त into Hindi भोजपत्र. Historically, peeled layers of Himalayan birch bark served as the principal writing material across northern India before paper became widespread.

मंगलवार.etymology: Learned Sanskrit compound मङ्गलवार (maṅgalavāra): मङ्गल ('auspicious; the planet Mars') + वार ('day of the week').

मंज़िल.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian منزل (manzil) from Arabic مَنْزِل (manzil, 'halting-place, stage, house, storey'), from root ن-ز-ل ('to alight').

मई.etymology: मई (maī) is borrowed via English 'May' from Old French 'mai' and Latin 'Māius (mēnsis)', named after the Roman goddess Maia. Integrated into the Hindi Gregorian calendar, its final -ई vowel aligns it grammatically with feminine nouns, unlike months ending in consonants such as मार्च or जून.

मकान.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic مَكَان (makān, 'place, dwelling'), via Classical Persian مکان (makān, 'house').

मक्खन.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit म्रक्षण (mrakṣaṇa, 'ointment, oil, butter for spreading'), via Prakrit मक्खण (makkhaṇa).

मगर.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian مگر (magar, 'but, unless, perhaps'), from Middle Persian magar.

मज़बूत.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic مَضْبُوط (maḍbūṭ, 'held fast, firm, well-built, accurate'), via Classical Persian مضبوط.

मज़बूती.etymology: मज़बूती (mazbūtī) is formed in Hindi-Urdu by adding the Persian abstract noun suffix -ई (-ī) to मज़बूत (mazbūt, 'strong, firm, well-fastened'). The base adjective मज़बूत comes via Persian from Arabic مضبوط (maḍbūṭ, passive participle of ضبط ḍabaṭa, 'to hold fast, secure'). Combined with से, मज़बूती से functions as a common adverb meaning 'firmly'.

मज़ाक़.etymology: मज़ाक़ (mazāq) is borrowed via Classical Persian مذاق (mazāq) from Arabic مذاق (madhāq, 'taste, palate, discernment, wit'), derived from the Arabic root ذ-و-ق (dh-w-q, 'to taste'). In Persian and Hindustani, the sense evolved from 'refined taste or pleasantry' to 'banter, humour, or a joke'. The final क़ preserves the original Arabic uvular stop.

मत.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit मा स्म / मा तद् (mā, prohibitive 'do not!'), extended in Prakrit मत्त / मत.

rootFamily.gloss: not (with subjunctive, infinitive, or न ... न 'neither ... nor')

मतलब.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian مطلب (matlab) from Arabic مَطْلَب (maṭlab, 'object sought, intention, meaning'), from root ط-ل-ب.

rootFamily.gloss: to understand; to realise; to figure out

मदद.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian مدد (madad) from Arabic مَدَد (madad, 'help, reinforcement, aid').

rootFamily.gloss: with; together with (के साथ); together (एक साथ)

मधुर.etymology: मधुर (madhur) is a direct borrowing (tatsama) from Sanskrit मधुर (madhura, 'sweet, honeyed, melodious, charming'), derived from मधु (madhu, 'honey, mead', cognate with English 'mead' and Greek 'méthy'). From the literal sweetness of honey, Sanskrit and Hindi extended it to gentle voices, pleasant melodies, and agreeable manners.

rootFamily.gloss: sweet; pleasant (of voice, music, or scent)

मध्य.etymology: मध्य (madhya) is a learned borrowing (tatsama) from Sanskrit मध्य (madhya, 'middle, central'), inheriting Proto-Indo-European *médʰyos (cognate with Latin 'medius' and English 'mid'). While its inherited tadbhava doublet माँझ / में shifted semantically in Hindi, the Sanskrit form मध्य remains the standard adjective in music, geography, and formal compounds.

rootFamily.gloss: middle; centre (के बीच 'between / in the middle of')

मन.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit मनस् (manas, 'mind, spirit, inclination'), from Proto-Indo-European *ménos.

मना.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic مَنْع (manʿ, 'prohibition, refusal'), via Classical Persian منع (man').

rootFamily.gloss: to accept; to agree; (हार मानना) to give up

मरम्मत.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic مَرَمَّة (maramma, 'repair, mending'), via Classical Persian مرمت (marammat).

rootFamily.gloss: to join; to connect; to mend; to bring together

मर्द.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian مرد (mard, 'man'), from Old Persian martiya-, cognate with Sanskrit मर्त्य (martya, 'mortal, man').

मशहूर.etymology: मशहूर (mashhūr) entered Hindi via Classical Persian مشهور (mashhūr) from Arabic مشهور (mashhūr, 'well-known, publicized, famous'), the passive participle of شهر (shahara, 'to make known, proclaim'). Widely used in both conversational and literary Hindi-Urdu, it is the everyday counterpart to Sanskrit-derived प्रसिद्ध.

rootFamily.gloss: big; large; elder; very (in expressions like बड़े शौक़ से)

मशीन.etymology: Borrowed from English machine, via French from Latin māchina and Greek μηχανή.

महकना.etymology: महकना (mahaknā) is derived from the noun महक (mahak, 'fragrance, aroma'), which traces back to a Middle Indo-Aryan expressive base महक्क- / मह- (mahakka- 'diffused scent'), possibly linked to Sanskrit मघ / मख or Prakrit महमहेइ ('emits perfume'). In Hindi the suffix -क- forms nouns and verbs of sensory diffusion such as महकना and चहकना.

cognates.meaning: to emit fragrance; to smell sweet

महसूस.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic مَحْسُوس (maḥsūs, 'perceived, felt'), via Classical Persian محسوس.

rootFamily.gloss: peace of mind; cosy calm; tranquillity
to seem; to feel; to be attached; to take (time/effort)

महिला.etymology: महिला (mahilā) is a learned borrowing (tatsama) from Sanskrit महिला (mahilā, 'woman, lady'), traditionally linked to मह् (mah, 'to honour, esteem, rejoice'), thus denoting a respected woman. In modern Hindi it is the standard polite and formal term for 'lady' or 'woman', declining cleanly with -एँ in the plural.

महीना.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian مهینه (mahīna, 'monthly pay; month'), from ماه (māh, 'moon, month').

माँगना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit मार्गति (mārgati, 'seeks, asks for, tracks'), via Prakrit मग्गइ (maggaï).

rootFamily.gloss: to want; to wish (माफ़ी चाहता/चाहती हूँ 'I apologise')

माइनर.etymology: माइनर (māinar) is borrowed from English 'minor', itself from Latin 'minor' ('smaller, lesser'). In Indian Western-music education and piano instruction, it was adopted unchanged for minor keys, chords, and intervals, functioning as an invariable modifier.

history.meaning: musical scale or chord with lowered third

माथा.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit मस्तक (mastaka, 'head, skull, forehead'), via Prakrit मत्थअ (matthaa).

मानना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit मानयति / मन्यते (manyate, 'thinks, respects, accepts').

rootFamily.gloss: defeat; giving up (हार मानना 'to give up, admit defeat')
assent; nod of agreement (हामी भरना 'to nod in agreement')

माफ़.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic مُعَاف (muʿāf, 'exempted, pardoned, forgiven'), via Classical Persian معاف (muʿāf -> māf).

माफ़ी.etymology: Formed with Persian/Hindi abstract suffix -ई from माफ़ (Arabic مُعَاف muʿāf, 'excused, pardoned, exempted').

मामूली.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic مَعْمُولِيّ / Indo-Persian معمولی (ma'mūlī, 'customary, ordinary, minor').

मारना.etymology: मारना (mārnā) descends from Sanskrit मारयति (mārayati, 'causes to die, strikes down', causative of मृ 'to die') via Prakrit मारेइ (mārei). In Hindi its meaning broadened widely from striking or killing to tapping, knocking, throwing, and functioning as an expressive light verb in idioms like बाज़ी मारना and हाथ मारना.

cognates.meaning: to hit; to strike; to knock

मारे.etymology: Grammaticalised oblique participle of मारना ('struck by'), used with के as compound postposition के मारे.

मालिक.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic مَالِك (mālik, 'possessor, owner'), via Classical Persian مالک.

मास्टर.etymology: मास्टर (māsṭar) is borrowed from English 'master', which derives via Old French 'maistre' from Latin 'magister' ('chief, teacher, director'). In Indian usage since the nineteenth century, it became deeply naturalized both as an honorific for schoolteachers (मास्टर जी) and in technical compounds like मास्टर चाबी ('master key').

मिनट.etymology: Borrowed from English minute, from Medieval Latin minūta.

मिलन.etymology: Inherited/borrowed from Sanskrit मिलन (milana, 'meeting, union, encounter'), from मिल् ('to meet').

rootFamily.gloss: to be found; to get/receive (with को); to meet (with से)

मिलना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit मिलति (milati, 'meets, joins, comes together'), via Prakrit मिलइ (milaï).

rootFamily.gloss: to dial (a phone number); to mix; to match/compare
to look for; to search for

मिलाना.etymology: Causative/transitive in -आना formed from मिलना ('to meet, come together').

rootFamily.gloss: to be found; to get/receive (with को); to meet (with से)
number (room number, phone number, shoe size)

मिलीमीटर.etymology: Borrowed from English millimetre / millimeter (milli- + metre).

मिस्टर.etymology: Borrowed from English Mister (abbreviated Mr.), weakened unstressed form of early modern English master, descending via Old French maistre from Classical Latin magister ('chief, teacher, master', built on magis 'more').

history.meaning: courteous title placed before a man's surname or full name

rootFamily.gloss: schoolmaster, master tailor/craftsman (earlier doublet from English master)

मिस्टर.notes: Placed before a surname or full name (मिस्टर शर्मा), contrasting with native honorific जी placed after the name (शर्मा जी) and formal श्री.

मीटर.etymology: Borrowed from English metre / meter, from French mètre.

मीठा.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit मिष्ट (miṣṭa, 'sweet, dainty, savoury'), via Prakrit मिट्ठ (miṭṭha).

मुँह.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit मुख (mukha, 'mouth, face, opening'), via Prakrit मुह (muha) with vowel nasalisation.

मुख्य.etymology: Learned Sanskrit borrowing मुख्य (mukhya, 'foremost, chief, principal'), from मुख ('face, front').

rootFamily.gloss: big; large; elder; very (in expressions like बड़े शौक़ से)

मुड़ना.etymology: Inherited from Prakrit मुडइ (muḍaï, 'turns, bends, twists'), related to Sanskrit मुटति.

rootFamily.gloss: to the left; on the left
to the right; on the right

मुफ़्त.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian مفت (muft, 'gratuitous, without payment, free').

मुलायम.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic مُلَايِم (mulāyim, 'gentle, mild, soft, agreeable'), via Classical Persian ملایم.

मुसीबत.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian مصیبت (musībat) from Arabic مُصِيبَة (muṣība, 'misfortune, calamity, affliction').

मुस्कान.etymology: Formed within Hindi from मुस्कुराना / मुस्कना ('to smile') + verbal noun suffix -आन.

मुस्कुराना.etymology: Expressive Indo-Aryan verb मुस्कुराना / मुसकाना ('to smile gently').

मुहर.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian مهر (muhr, 'seal, signet ring'), from Middle Persian muhr.

मूँगा.etymology: मूँगा (mūngā) is connected with Prakrit मुग्ग / मुँग (mugga / muṅga) and Sanskrit मुक्ताफल / मद्रक or regional coastal trade words (compare Tamil/Malayalam or Portuguese 'mungo' theories, though Indo-Aryan मुग्ग for a bright red bead or pulse is well attested). In Jaipur jewellery and textile culture, मूँगा specifically denotes precious red-pink coral and its warm sunset shade.

में.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit मध्ये (madhye, 'in the middle of, inside'), via Prakrit मज्झि -> मइं -> में.

मेज़.etymology: Borrowed via Portuguese mesa ('table') and reinforced via Persian میز (mēz), ultimately from Latin mēnsa ('table').

मेज़पोश.etymology: Indo-Persian compound میزپوش (mēzpōš, 'table-cover'), from میز (mēz, 'table') + پوش (pōš, 'covering').

rootFamily.gloss: cloth; piece of fabric; clothes (in plural कपड़े)

मेहनत.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic مِحْنَة (miḥna, 'trial, toil'), via Classical Persian محنت (mihnat, 'effort, labour').

मेहमान.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian مهمان (mihmān, 'guest'), from Middle Persian mehmān.

मेहमाननवाज़ी.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian مهمان‌نوازی (mihmān-nawāzī, 'hospitality'), from مهمان ('guest') + نوازی ('cherishing, soothing').

मेहरबानी.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian مهربانی (mihrbānī, 'kindness, affection'), from مهربان (mihrbān, 'kind, loving', Old Iranian *miθra-pāna-).

मेहराब.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian محراب (mihrāb) from Arabic مِحْرَاب (miḥrāb, 'arched niche, archway').

मेहराबदार.etymology: मेहराबदार (mehrābdār) is a hybrid Persian-Arabic compound adjective combining मेहराब (mehrāb, 'arch, vaulted niche') with the Persian possessive suffix -दार (-dār, 'having, possessing'). The noun मेहराब entered Persian from Arabic محراب (miḥrāb, 'arched prayer niche'). In Rajasthani and Mughal architecture, मेहराबदार describes curved stone arches over windows and gates.

मैं.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit मया (mayā, instrumental of अहम् 'I'), via Prakrit मइं (maïṃ), reanalysed as direct subject.

rootFamily.gloss: one's own (my, your, his, her, our, their)

मैडम.etymology: Borrowed from English madam, from Old French ma dame ('my lady').

history.meaning: polite form of address to a woman

मैनेजर.etymology: Borrowed from English manager ('person who directs a hotel, shop, or office'), formed from manage (from sixteenth-century Italian maneggiare 'to handle, train a horse by hand', derived from Latin manus 'hand') + agent suffix -er.

history.meaning: to handle -> to direct -> person running an establishment
manager (of a hotel, bank, or business)

cognates.meaning: person in charge of an establishment

मैनेजर.notes: Commonly addressed respectfully in North Indian hotels and offices as मैनेजर साहब ('Manager-sahib').

मोटा.etymology: Inherited from Prakrit मोट्ट (moṭṭa, 'thick, bulky, stout').

मोड़.etymology: Deverbal noun from मोड़ना (moṛnā, 'to turn, bend'), inherited from Prakrit मोडेइ (moḍeï).

rootFamily.gloss: to turn; to bend; to be folded

मोड़ना.etymology: Transitive counterpart of मुड़ना ('to turn, bend'), from Prakrit मोडइ (moḍaï, 'twists, folds').

rootFamily.gloss: to turn; to bend; to be folded

मोम.etymology: मोम (mom) is borrowed from Classical Persian موم (mūm / mōm, 'wax, beeswax'), descending from Middle Persian 'mōm'. It entered Hindustani through candle-making, sealing, and textile waterproofing crafts, giving rise to common Hindi compounds such as मोमबत्ती ('candle') and मोमजामा ('waxcloth').

rootFamily.gloss: cloth; piece of fabric; clothes (in plural कपड़े)

मोर्चा.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian مورچه (mōrča, 'entrenchment, parapet, watch-post').

rootFamily.gloss: to handle; to look after; to hold steady

मोहन.etymology: From Sanskrit मोहन (mohana, 'charming, captivating'), a traditional epithet of Krishna.

यहीं.etymology: Formed in Hindi by contracting यहाँ (yahā̃, 'here') with the exclusive emphatic particle ही (hī, 'right, very, only'), fusing final nasal -आँ + -ही into nasalised -ईं (यहीं, 'right here, in this very spot').

या.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian या / یا (yā, 'or'), from Middle Persian ayāb.

यात्रा.etymology: Learned borrowing from Sanskrit यात्रा (yātrā, 'going, journey, pilgrimage'), from root या (yā, 'to go').

यात्री.etymology: यात्री (yātrī) is a learned borrowing (tatsama) from Sanskrit यात्रिन् (yātrin, 'traveller, pilgrim, wayfarer', nominative singular यात्री), derived from यात्रा (yātrā, 'journey, expedition', from root या 'to go'). Originally prominent for religious pilgrims, in modern Hindi it encompasses train passengers, hikers, and tourists.

याद.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian یاد (yād, 'memory, remembrance'), from Middle Persian ayād.

rootFamily.gloss: mind; heart; mood / inclination (मन करना 'to feel like')

यादगार.etymology: यादगार (yādgār) is borrowed from Classical Persian یادگار (yādgār, 'souvenir, keepsake, monument'), composed of یاد (yād, 'memory, remembrance') and the suffix -گار (-gār, 'maker, token'). The noun یاد itself descends from Middle Persian 'ayād' ('memory'). In Hindi it serves smoothly both as a feminine noun ('a keepsake') and an adjective ('memorable').

युगल.etymology: युगल (yugal) is a learned borrowing (tatsama) from Sanskrit युगल (yugala, 'a pair, couple, brace'), derived from युग (yuga, 'yoke, pair, age', cognate with English 'yoke' and Latin 'iugum'). In modern Hindi arts and music terminology, it naturally translates 'duet' when describing two performers or two voices singing together.

युवा.etymology: युवा (yuvā) is borrowed from Sanskrit युवन् (yuvan, 'young, youthful', nominative singular युवा), an ancient Indo-European word cognate with Latin 'iuvenis' and English 'young'. Unlike its inherited Hindi cognate जवान (via Persian), युवा is preferred in formal, journalistic, and descriptive phrasing such as युवा यात्री ('young traveller').

यूँ.etymology: Inherited from Prakrit एवं / इउँ (iũ, 'thus, in this manner'), from Sanskrit एवम् (evam).

योजना.etymology: Learned Sanskrit borrowing योजना (yojanā, 'arrangement, plan, project'), from युज् ('to join, arrange').

रँगना.etymology: रँगना (rangnā) is a denominative verb formed from रंग (rang, 'colour, dye'), which descends from Sanskrit रङ्ग (raṅga, 'colour, dye, hue', from the root रञ्ज् 'to colour, redden, delight'). In Hindi, the short stem vowel is marked with a chandrabindu (रँ-) to preserve the nasalization of the base noun before -ग-.

रंग.etymology: Inherited/borrowed from Sanskrit रङ्ग (raṅga, 'colour, dye, hue') / Classical Persian رنگ (rang).

रखना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit रक्षति (rakṣati, 'guards, keeps, preserves'), via Prakrit रक्खइ (rakkhaï).

रजिस्टर.etymology: Borrowed from English register, from Medieval Latin registrum.

रजिस्टर्ड.etymology: Borrowed from English registered (as in registered post / registered letter).

रत्न.etymology: रत्न (ratna) is a learned borrowing (tatsama) from Sanskrit रत्न (ratna, 'gift, treasure, jewel, gem'), derived from the root रा (rā, 'to bestow, give'). In Jaipur's renowned lapidary and jewellery culture, रत्न is the standard word for cut and polished precious stones.

रफ़्तार.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian رفتار (raftār, 'gait, pace, speed'), from رفتن (raftan, 'to go').

रसीद.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian رسید (rasīd, 'acknowledgement of arrival, receipt'), past stem of رسیدن (rasīdan, 'to arrive, reach').

रसोई.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit रसवती (rasavatī, 'juicy, savoury; kitchen where meals are prepared'), via Prakrit रसोई (rasoī).

रस्सी.etymology: रस्सी (rassī) derives from Sanskrit रश्मि (raśmi, 'cord, rein, rope, ray') or रज्जु (rajju, 'rope') via Prakrit रस्सी (rassī, 'rope, string'). The geminate -स्स- reflects the assimilation of the Sanskrit consonant cluster -श्म-. Across domestic, maritime, and construction settings, it remains the standard Hindi noun for rope.

रहना.etymology: Inherited from Prakrit रहइ (rahaï, 'remains, stays, dwells').

रहस्यमयी.etymology: Learned Sanskrit formation रहस्यमयी (rahasyamayī, 'full of mystery'), from रहस्य ('secret, mystery') + -मयी.

राजकीय.etymology: राजकीय (rājkīya) is a learned borrowing (tatsama) from Sanskrit राजकीय (rājakīya, 'royal, belonging to a king or state'), formed from राजन् (rājan, 'king, ruler') with the possessive suffix -कीय. In modern Indian Hindi administration it regularly translates 'state', 'official', or 'civic' (as in राजकीय चिह्न, 'official emblem').

राज़.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian راز (rāz, 'secret, mystery'), from Middle Persian rāz.

रात.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit रात्रि (rātri, 'night'), via Prakrit रत्ति (ratti) with compensatory vowel lengthening.

राहत.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian راحت (rāhat) from Arabic رَاحَة (rāḥa, 'rest, ease, relief').

रिबन.etymology: Borrowed from English ribbon, from Middle French ruban.

रिसेप्शनिस्ट.etymology: Borrowed from English receptionist, from reception + -ist.

रुकना.etymology: Inherited from Prakrit रुक्कइ (rukkaï, 'stops, halts, waits').

rootFamily.gloss: to stop (someone/something); to block; to hold back

रुकावट.etymology: रुकावट (rukāvaṭ) is derived from the Hindi verb रुकना (ruknā, 'to stop, halt') using the productive feminine abstract suffix -आवट (-āvaṭ, compare सजावट and लिखावट). रुपया.etymology: From Sanskrit रूप्य (rūpya, 'wrought silver; stamped silver coin'), standardised as rupiya under Sher Shah Suri in the sixteenth century.

रेडिएटर.etymology: Borrowed from English radiator, from Latin radiāre ('to emit rays/heat').

रेत.etymology: रेत (ret) descends from Prakrit रेत्ता / रित्ता (rettā) or Sanskrit रेणु / सिकता-influenced Prakrit रेत (reta, 'sand, dust', also linked to Sanskrit रेत् / रयति 'flows, crumbles'). Across Rajasthan and northern India, रेत is the everyday feminine noun for fine river or desert sand.

रेलगाड़ी.etymology: Classic nineteenth-century hybrid compound joining English rail + native Hindi गाड़ी ('wheeled vehicle, carriage').

रेलवे.etymology: Borrowed in the nineteenth century with the building of Indian Railways from British English railway, compound of rail ('iron track bar', via Old French reille < Latin rēgula 'straight rod, rule') + way (Old English weg 'road, path').

history.meaning: railway (especially in रेलवे स्टेशन and भारतीय रेलवे)

रेलवे.notes: Deeply naturalised across South Asia since the 1850s; रेलवे स्टेशन is the everyday term for a train station.

रेलिंग.etymology: रेलिंग (reling) is borrowed from English 'railing', formed from 'rail' (Old French 'reille', from Latin 'rēgula', 'straight bar, rule') plus '-ing'. In Indian architectural and household speech it refers to staircase banisters and balcony rails, and is treated as a feminine noun.

रोकना.etymology: Causative/transitive counterpart of रुकना ('to stop'), via Prakrit रोक्कइ (rokkaï).

रोज़.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian روز (rōz, 'day; daily'), from Middle Persian rōz.

रोना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit रोदिति (roditi, 'weeps, cries'), via Prakrit रोअइ (roaï).

रोल.etymology: Borrowed from English roll ('small rolled bread or pastry').

रोशन.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian روشن (rōšan, 'bright, luminous, clear'), from PIE *lewk- ('light').

रोशनी.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian روشنی (rōšnī, 'light, brightness'), from روشن (rōšan, 'bright', cognate with Sanskrit रोचन rocana).

लंबा.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit लम्ब (lamba, 'hanging down, long, tall'), via Prakrit लंब (lamba).

लगाना.etymology: Causative/transitive in -आना from लगना ('to be attached, apply'), from Sanskrit लगयति via Prakrit लग्गावेइ.

लटकना.etymology: Inherited Indo-Aryan verb लटकना ('to hang, dangle'), from Prakrit लट्टक्कइ.

लटकाना.etymology: लटकाना (laṭkānā) is the transitive counterpart of लटकना (laṭaknā, 'to hang, dangle'), which traces back to a Middle Indo-Aryan expressive base लट्ट- / लटक- (laṭṭa- / laṭak-, related to Sanskrit लम्बते / लट् 'to sway, hang loose'). rootFamily.gloss: to hang up (on a hook, peg, or wall)

लड़का.etymology: Inherited Indo-Aryan noun लड़का (laṛkā, 'boy, son'), from Middle Indo-Aryan लड्डिक्क.

लड़ना.etymology: Inherited from Middle Indo-Aryan लडइ (laḍaï, 'quarrels, strives').

लड़ी.etymology: लड़ी (laṛī) derives from Prakrit लडिआ / लडी (laḍiā / laḍī, 'string of pearls, strand, row'), related to Sanskrit लता / यष्टि or a Dravidian/Deshya root for a linked chain or thread. Intervocalic -ड- regularly developed into the retroflex flap -ड़- in Hindi. It is widely used for strings of flowers, pearls, and festive courtyard lights.

लपकना.etymology: लपकना (lapaknā) stems from a Middle Indo-Aryan expressive base लप्प- / लपक- (lappa- / lapak-, 'to snatch, dart, leap swiftly'), related to Sanskrit लप् / लम्भ् ('to seize, grasp') and comparable to English 'leap' only coincidentally. The -क- extension expresses sudden, darting motion toward a target.

लपेटना.etymology: लपेटना (lapeṭnā) descends from Prakrit लप्पेटइ / लपेटइ (lappeṭai, 'wraps around, folds'), connected to Sanskrit लिप् / लपेट् ('to coat, cling, wind'). Its transitive stem लपेट- contrasts with the passive/intransitive लिपटना ('to be wrapped, cling'). It covers both wrapping gifts and coiling ropes.

लाजवाब.etymology: Indo-Persian compound from Arabic لا (lā, 'no, without') + جواب (jawāb, 'answer, peer, match').

लाना.etymology: Contracted compound of ले आना ('to take and come -> bring'), from लेना + आना.

लालटेन.etymology: Borrowed from English lantern via folk-phonetic adaptation लालटेन (influenced by लाल 'red, glowing').

लिए.etymology: Grammaticalised oblique perfective participle of लेना ('having taken -> for the sake of').

लिखना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit लिखति (likhati, 'scratches, draws, writes'), via Prakrit लिखइ (likhaï).

लिखवाना.etymology: Indirect causative in -वाना formed from लिखना ('to write').

लिखावट.etymology: Derived within Hindi from लिखाना / लिखना ('to write') + abstract feminine suffix -आवट (-āvaṭ).

लिनेन.etymology: लिनेन (linen) is borrowed from English 'linen', which comes from Old English 'līnen' ('made of flax'), from Latin 'līnum' ('flax'). लिपटना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit लिप्त (lipta, 'smeared, joined, clinging') + extension -ट, via Prakrit लिप्पडइ.

लिफ़ाफ़ा.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian لفافه (lifāfa) from Arabic لِفَافَة (lifāfa, 'wrapping, covering, envelope'), from root ل-ف-ف ('to wrap').

लेना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit लभते / नी (labhate, 'takes, receives'), via Prakrit लेइ (leï).

लैंप.etymology: Borrowed from English lamp, via Old French lampe from Greek λαμπάς (lampás, 'torch').

लॉबी.etymology: Borrowed from English lobby, from Medieval Latin lobia ('covered walk, foyer').

लोग.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit लोक (loka, 'world, realm, people, folk'), via Prakrit लोग (loga).

लोहा.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit लोह (loha, 'reddish metal, copper, iron'), via Prakrit लोह (loha).

लौ.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit लोचि / प्रभा or अलात, via Prakrit लोअ ('glow, flame tongue').

लौटना.etymology: Inherited from Prakrit लोट्टइ (loṭṭaï, 'turns back, rolls back, returns').

वक़्त.etymology: वक़्त (vaqt) entered Hindi via Classical Persian وقت (vaqt) from Arabic وقت (waqt, 'time, period, fixed moment'). Alongside Sanskrit-derived समय, it is one of the most frequent everyday words for time, occasion, or the right moment in spoken North Indian Hindi.

वकील.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic وَكِيل (wakīl, 'representative, legal agent, advocate'), via Classical Persian وکیل.

वजह.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian وجه (wajh) from Arabic وَجْه (wajh, 'face, aspect, manner, reason').

वरक़.etymology: वरक़ (varaq) entered Hindi via Classical Persian ورق (varaq) from Arabic ورق (waraq, 'leaf, foliage, sheet of paper or beaten metal'). In Jaipur's traditional craft culture—both miniature painting and artisanal mithai-making—वरक़ specifically denotes paper-thin beaten gold or silver leaf applied for luminous highlights.

वरना.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian ورنه (warna, contraction of و گر نه wa gar na, 'and if not').

वर्कशॉप.etymology: वर्कशॉप (varkshop) is borrowed from English 'workshop', a compound of 'work' and 'shop' dating from Early Modern English for a room where manual crafts or repairs are carried out. In Hindi it is commonly treated as feminine by analogy with native words like कार्यशाला and दुकान.

वह.etymology: Inherited from Prakrit ओह / वह (vaha, 'that one'), distal counterpart of एह ('this').

वहाँ.etymology: Distal counterpart of यहाँ ('here'), formed on the distal stem व- in Early Hindi.

वाक्य.etymology: Learned Sanskrit borrowing वाक्य (vākya, 'utterance, statement, sentence'), from वाच् ('speech, voice').

वादा.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic وَعْدَة (waʿda, 'promise, pledge'), via Classical Persian وعده (waʿda).

rootFamily.gloss: to fulfil; to carry through; to uphold (a role, promise, teamwork)

वापस.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian واپس (wāpas, 'back, behind, returning'), from وا ('back') + پس ('after, behind').

वायलिन.etymology: वायलिन (vāyalin) comes from English 'violin', borrowed from Italian 'violino', the diminutive of 'viola' (ultimately from Medieval Latin 'vitula', a stringed instrument). Introduced into India during the colonial era and widely integrated into both Western and Carnatic/Hindustani classical ensembles, it takes masculine gender in Hindi.

वाला.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit पालक (pālaka, 'keeper, guardian, holder'), via Prakrit वालअ (vālaa), grammaticalised into an all-purpose adjectival suffix.
