वाल्त्ज़.etymology: वाल्त्ज़ (vāltz) is borrowed via English 'waltz' from German 'Walzer' ('a revolving dance in triple time'), derived from 'walzen' ('to roll, turn, revolve'). In Hindi musical usage it refers both to the three-beat ballroom dance and to compositions written in waltz rhythm, taking masculine gender.

वाल्व.etymology: Borrowed from English valve, from Latin valva ('folding door leaf').

वास्तुकला.etymology: वास्तुकला (vāstukalā) is a Sanskritic compound (tatsama) formed from वास्तु (vāstu, 'dwelling site, building, structure', from वस् 'to dwell') and कला (kalā, 'art, craft'). Classical Indian treatises such as the Vāstu Śāstras used वास्तु for spatial design and building science, and modern Hindi coined वास्तुकला as the standard equivalent of 'architecture'.

वास्तुकार.etymology: Learned Sanskrit compound वास्तुकार (vāstukāra, 'builder, architect'), from वास्तु ('site, building') + कार ('maker').

वाह.etymology: Borrowed/shared across Indo-Iranian (Persian واه wāh / Sanskrit वाह), a natural exclamation of admiration.

rootFamily.gloss: oh!; hey!; wait a moment! (surprise or sudden realisation)

विधि.etymology: विधि (vidhi) is a learned borrowing (tatsama) from Sanskrit विधि (vidhi, 'rule, precept, manner, prescribed method'), formed from वि- + धा ('to lay down, ordain, arrange'). From ancient ritual and grammatical rules, its sense generalized in Hindi to any step-by-step method, legal procedure, or culinary recipe.

विनम्र.etymology: Learned Sanskrit borrowing (tatsama) विनम्र (vinamra, 'bowed, modest, courteous'), from वि- + नम्र ('bending, humble').

विभाग.etymology: Learned Sanskrit borrowing विभाग (vibhāga, 'division, section, department'), from वि- + भज्.

विरासत.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic وِرَاثَة (wirāṯa, 'inheritance, heritage'), via Classical Persian وراثت (wirāsat).

विश्वविद्यालय.etymology: विश्वविद्यालय (vishvavidyālaya) is a modern Sanskrit-based compound coined in the nineteenth/twentieth century to translate English 'university' (from Latin 'universitas'). It combines विश्व (viśva, 'all, universe') + विद्या (vidyā, 'knowledge, learning') + आलय (ālaya, 'abode, hall'). Because आलय is masculine, the whole compound takes masculine gender.

वे.etymology: Plural of वह ('that; he/she'), formed in Early Hindi on the distal stem व-.

वैसा.etymology: Inherited from Prakrit वइस (vaïsa, 'like that'), distal analogical formation alongside अइस ('like this') and जइस ('like which').

वैसे.etymology: Oblique/adverbial form of वैसा ('like that'), grammaticalised as a conversational topic-shifter ('incidentally, otherwise').

history.meaning: in that manner -> by the way

rootFamily.gloss: thus; like this; (with ही) just like that / casually

वॉटरप्रूफ़.etymology: वॉटरप्रूफ़ (voṭarprūf) is a direct borrowing from English 'waterproof', compounding 'water' and 'proof' (Old French 'preuve', 'tested, impervious'). Widely used in Indian stationery, packaging, and outdoor gear vocabulary, it serves as an invariable modifier.

व्यावसायिक.etymology: Learned Sanskrit vriddhi derivative व्यावसायिक (vyāvasāyika, 'relating to trade or business'), from व्यवसाय + -इक.

शटर.etymology: Borrowed from English shutter ('hinged or rolling metal cover that shuts a shopfront or window'), agent/instrument noun from shut (Old English scyttan, 'to bolt, bar, close') + -er.

history.meaning: movable security cover for a window or shopfront

शटर.notes: In Indian towns and bazaars, शटर उठाना ('pulling up the rolling iron shutter') and शटर गिराना ('pulling down the shutter') mark opening and closing a shop for the day.

शनिवार.etymology: शनिवार (shanivār) is a Sanskrit-derived compound (tatsama) from शनि (Śani, the planet Saturn and deity associated with it) and वार (vāra, 'day of the week, turn'). Following the classical planetary weekday system shared with Greco-Roman tradition, Saturn's day corresponds directly to English 'Saturday'.

शब्द.etymology: Learned borrowing from Sanskrit शब्द (śabda, 'sound, voice, word').

शर्ट.etymology: शर्ट (sharṭ) is borrowed from English 'shirt', descending from Old English 'scyrte' ('short garment, tunic', cognate with 'skirt' from Old Norse). It largely replaced or sits alongside कमीज़ (from Arabic/Portuguese) in modern Indian Hindi and routinely takes feminine gender (plural शर्टें).

शहतीर.etymology: शहतीर (shahtīr) is borrowed from Classical Persian شاهتیر (shāhtīr, 'main beam, ridge-pole'), a compound of شاه (shāh, 'king, chief, largest') and تیر (tīr, 'beam, shaft, arrow'). In traditional North Indian haveli carpentry and masonry, it denotes the primary heavy ceiling timber spanning a room or veranda.

शहद.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian شهد (šahd) from Arabic شَهْد (šahd, 'honeycomb, pure honey').

rootFamily.gloss: sweet; pleasant (of voice, music, or scent)

शहर.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian شهر (šahr, 'city, town'), from Middle Persian šahr ('land, realm, city').

शांत.etymology: Learned Sanskrit borrowing (tatsama) शान्त (śānta, 'calmed, tranquil, still'), past participle of शम् ('to grow calm').

rootFamily.gloss: peace of mind; cosy calm; tranquillity

शांति.etymology: Learned Sanskrit borrowing शान्ति (śānti, 'peace, calm, tranquillity'), from root शम् ('to grow calm').

rootFamily.gloss: peace of mind; cosy calm; tranquillity

शानदार.etymology: Indo-Persian compound from Arabic شان (šān, 'dignity, splendour') + Persian دار (-dār, 'possessing').

शाबाश.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian شاباش (šābāš, contraction of شاد باش šād bāš, 'be joyful! bravo!').

शाम.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian شام (šām, 'evening'), from Middle Persian šām.

rootFamily.gloss: evening (in polite greeting शुभ संध्या! 'Good evening!')

शामिल.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic شَامِل (šāmil, 'comprising, including, comprehensive'), via Classical Persian شامل.

rootFamily.gloss: with; together with (के साथ); together (एक साथ)

शायद.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian شاید (šāyad, 'it may be; perhaps'), 3rd sg. present of شایستن ('to be fitting, be possible').

शाही.etymology: शाही (shāhī) is borrowed from Classical Persian شاهی (shāhī, 'royal, kingly'), formed from شاه (shāh, 'king, sovereign', Old Persian 'xšāyaθiya-') plus the adjectival suffix -ई (-ī). In Rajasthani and North Indian cultural usage, it evokes regal elegance, grand hospitality, and fine craftsmanship.

rootFamily.gloss: big; large; elder; very (in expressions like बड़े शौक़ से)

शिक्षक.etymology: शिक्षक (shikshak) is a learned borrowing (tatsama) from Sanskrit शिक्षक (śikṣaka, 'teacher, instructor'), an agent noun from the desiderative root शिक्ष् (śikṣ, 'to wish to know, learn, teach', from शक् 'to be able'). In modern Hindi it functions as the primary formal and colloquial noun for a school or college teacher.

शिल्प.etymology: शिल्प (shilp) is a learned borrowing (tatsama) from Sanskrit शिल्प (śilpa, 'variegated art, skill, handicraft, mechanical art'). Across South Asian cultural history, it encompasses woodworking, pottery, textile printing, and stone carving, forming compounds such as हस्तशिल्प ('handicraft') and शिल्पकार ('artisan').

शीशा.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian شیشه (šīša, 'glass, bottle, mirror'), from Middle Persian šīšag.

शुक्र.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian شکر (šukr) from Arabic شُكْر (šukr, 'gratitude, thanks').

cognates.meaning: everyday 'thank you' from the same Arabic root

rootFamily.gloss: God; the Lord (भगवान का शुक्र है! 'Thank goodness!')

शुक्रवार.etymology: Learned Sanskrit compound शुक्रवार (śukravāra): शुक्र ('bright; the planet Venus') + वार ('day of the week').

शुक्रिया.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic شُكْرِيَّة (šukriyya) / Classical Persian شکریه ('gratitude, thanks'), from Arabic شُكْر ('thanks').

शुभ.etymology: Learned Sanskrit borrowing (tatsama) शुभ (śubha, 'bright, auspicious, fortunate, good').

rootFamily.gloss: evening (in polite greeting शुभ संध्या! 'Good evening!')

शुरू.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic شُرُوع (šurūʿ, 'beginning, commencement, entering upon'), via Classical Persian شروع.

शून्य.etymology: शून्य (shūnya) is a direct borrowing from Sanskrit शून्य (śūnya, 'empty, void, zero'), derived from शून (śūna, 'swollen, hollow', PIE *ḱewh₁- 'to swell, be hollow'). In ancient Indian mathematics, शून्य named the positional place-value symbol for zero. Rendered into Arabic as ṣifr, it subsequently gave rise via Medieval Latin to both English 'cipher' and 'zero'.

rootFamily.gloss: number (room number, phone number, shoe size)

शेफ़.etymology: शेफ़ (shef) is borrowed via English 'chef' from French 'chef (de cuisine)' ('head of the kitchen'), where 'chef' continues Latin 'caput' ('head'). Adopted into modern Indian hospitality and café vocabulary, it serves both as a formal culinary title and an affectionate compliment to a talented cook.

शेल्फ़.etymology: Borrowed from English shelf, from Middle Low German schelf.

शॉर्टकट.etymology: शॉर्टकट (shorṭkaṭ) is borrowed from English 'shortcut', a compound of 'short' and 'cut' ('a path cut across to shorten a journey'). Widely used in contemporary urban Hindi for both quicker street routes and faster methods of doing a task, it takes masculine gender.

शॉवर.etymology: Borrowed from English shower ('overhead perforated water spray for bathing', transferred in nineteenth-century English from shower 'brief fall of rain', Old English scūr, Proto-Germanic *skūraz).
शॉवर.notes: Written with the chandrakala vowel sign ॉ (ऑ) used specifically in Devanagari to represent open rounded English vowels.

शोर.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian شور (šōr, 'tumult, outcry, commotion; saltiness').

शौक़.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian شوق (šawq) from Arabic شَوْق (šawq, 'longing, eagerness, fondness').

rootFamily.gloss: mind; heart; mood / inclination (मन करना 'to feel like')

सँकरा.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit संकीर्ण / संकट (saṅkaṭa, 'crowded together, contracted, narrow'), via Prakrit संकड (saṅkaḍa).

सँभलना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit सम्भृ / सम्भलति (sambhalati, 'supports oneself, recovers balance'), via Prakrit संभलइ.

rootFamily.gloss: to handle; to look after; to hold steady

सँभालना.etymology: Transitive/causative in -आना from सँभलना ('to steady oneself'), from Sanskrit सम्भारयति.

rootFamily.gloss: to be careful; to steady oneself

संगीत.etymology: Learned Sanskrit borrowing सङ्गीत (saṅgīta, 'sung together; concert, music'), from सम्- ('together') + गीत ('sung').

rootFamily.gloss: to ring (a bell); to play (a musical instrument)

संगीतकार.etymology: संगीतकार (sangītkār) is a Sanskrit-based compound (tatsama) formed from संगीत (saṅgīta, 'symphony, vocal and instrumental music', from सम्- + गीत 'sung together') and कार (kāra, 'maker, doer'). In Hindi it refers generally to any musician, instrumentalist, or composer.

संतरा.etymology: Early borrowing from Portuguese Sintra (a town near Lisbon famed for sweet oranges introduced via sixteenth-century Lusitanian trade).

history.meaning: Portuguese town famed for sweet oranges

rootFamily.gloss: sweet; pleasant (of voice, music, or scent)

संदूक़ची.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian صندوقچه / Indo-Persian संदूक़ची, diminutive of Arabic صُنْدُوق (ṣundūq, 'box, chest').

संदेश.etymology: संदेश (sandesh) is a learned borrowing (tatsama) from Sanskrit सन्देश (sandeśa, 'message, news, command'), derived from सम्- + दिश् ('to point out, communicate, direct'). Classical Sanskrit poetry even featured the Sandeśakāvya ('messenger poem') genre; in modern Hindi it remains the standard word for a written or spoken message.

संध्या.etymology: Learned Sanskrit borrowing सन्ध्या (sandhyā, 'junction of day and night; twilight, evening'), from सम्- + ध्या.

संपत्ति.etymology: Learned Sanskrit borrowing सम्पत्ति (sampatti, 'prosperity, property, estate'), from सम्- + पद्.

संयोग.etymology: Learned Sanskrit borrowing संयोग (saṃyoga, 'conjunction, coincidence'), from सम्- + युज्.

सकना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit शक्नोति (śaknoti, 'is able, can'), via Prakrit सक्कइ (sakkaï).

rootFamily.gloss: is needed; is wanted; should (with infinitive)

सख़्त.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian سخت (saxt, 'hard, firm, stern'), from Middle Persian saxt.

सच.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit सत्य (satya, 'true; truth'), via Prakrit सच्च (sacca).

सचमुच.etymology: सचमुच (sachmuch) is an expressive echo-compound formed from सच (sach, 'true, truth', descending from Sanskrit सत्य via Prakrit सच्च) paired with the rhyming echo element मुच. Such jingle-compounds are highly productive in colloquial Hindi to add warmth, emphasis, or earnestness meaning 'really and truly'.

rootFamily.gloss: truth (सच में? 'Really?'; सच कहूँ तो 'To tell the truth')
completely; absolutely; (with नहीं) not at all

सच्चा.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit सत्यक (satyaka, 'true, faithful'), via Prakrit सच्चअ (saccaa).

rootFamily.gloss: truth (सच में? 'Really?'; सच कहूँ तो 'To tell the truth')

सजना.etymology: सजना (sajnā) derives from Sanskrit सज्जति (sajjati, 'is ready, equips oneself, adorns') or सज्ज (sajja, 'equipped, arrayed') via Prakrit सज्जइ (sajjai). In Hindi the geminate -ज्ज- simplified to -ज-, yielding the intransitive verb सजना ('to be adorned, look lovely') alongside the transitive सजाना ('to decorate').

cognates.meaning: to be decorated; to look graceful

सज्जन.etymology: Learned Sanskrit compound सज्जन (sajjana, 'good person, gentleman'), from सत् ('good, true') + जन ('person').

सटीक.etymology: सटीक (saṭīk) traces to Sanskrit सटीक (saṭīka, 'accompanied by a commentary, exact, authentic') or Prakrit सट्ठीक (saṭṭhīka, 'quite right, exact', from स- + ठीक 'right, proper'). In modern Hindi, it means 'spot-on, precise, accurate', especially regarding measurements, timing, or phrasing.

सड़क.etymology: Inherited Indo-Aryan noun सड़क (saṛak, 'beaten road, highway'), from Prakrit सडक्क.

सन.etymology: सन (san) descends from Sanskrit शण (śaṇa, 'hemp, Cannabis/Crotalaria juncea fibre') via Prakrit सण (saṇa). The palatal sibilant श- regularly became dental स- in Hindi, and retroflex -ण- flattened to -न-. Remarkably, English 'sunn (hemp)' was borrowed back from this very Indian word during colonial botanical trade.

सपना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit स्वप्न (svapna, 'sleep, dream'), via Prakrit सिविण / सपण, from PIE *swépnos.

सप्ताहांत.etymology: Modern Sanskritised compound सप्ताहान्त (saptāhānta): सप्ताह ('seven-day week') + अन्त ('end').

सफ़र.etymology: सफ़र (safar) entered Hindi via Classical Persian سفر (safar) from Arabic سفر (safar, 'journey, travel, departure'). Widely naturalized across North Indian speech, music, and literature, it stands alongside Sanskritic यात्रा as the most common everyday word for a trip or journey.

सफ़ेद.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian سفید (safēd, 'white, bright'), cognate with Sanskrit श्वेत (śveta) and English white.

सब.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit सर्व (sarva, 'all, whole, every'), via Prakrit सब्ब (sabba), from PIE *solh₂wós.

सबसे.etymology: Compound of सब ('all') + ablative-comparative postposition से ('than'), literally 'than all'.

सब्ज़ी.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian سبزی (sabzī, 'greenery, herbs, vegetables'), from سبز (sabz, 'green').

सभ्य.etymology: सभ्य (sabhya) is a learned borrowing (tatsama) from Sanskrit सभ्य (sabhya, 'fit for the assembly, well-bred, polite, civilized'), derived from सभा (sabhā, 'assembly, council, court'). Just as English 'civil' evolved from 'city' and 'courteous' from 'court', Sanskrit सभ्य shifted from 'belonging to the assembly' to 'courteous and civilized'.

history.meaning: fit for an assembly; well-mannered; polite

समंदर.etymology: समंदर (samandar) is a colloquial semi-tatsama development of Sanskrit समुद्र (samudra, 'gathering of waters, sea, ocean', from सम्- + उद्र 'water'), via Prakrit समुद्द / समुंदर. The intrusive nasal -अं- and epenthetic vowel -अ- broke up the final consonant cluster -द्र, yielding the warm spoken form समंदर alongside literary समुद्र.

समझना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit सम्बुध्यते (sambudhyate, 'awakens to, perceives, understands'), via Prakrit संबुज्झइ (sambujjhaï).

rootFamily.gloss: to explain; to help someone understand

समझाना.etymology: Causative in -आना formed from समझना ('to understand').

rootFamily.gloss: to understand; to realise; to figure out
to tell; to explain; to let someone know

समय.etymology: Learned borrowing from Sanskrit समय (samaya, 'appointed time, season, occasion'), from सम्- + इ ('to come together').

समय-सारणी.etymology: Learned Sanskrit compound समय ('time') + सारणी ('table, chart, list').

समानांतर.etymology: समानांतर (samānāntar) is a Sanskritic compound (tatsama) formed from समान (samāna, 'equal, same') + अन्तर (antara, 'interval, distance'). Literally meaning 'having an equal interval throughout', it was adopted in modern Hindi geometry, engineering, and everyday description to correspond directly to English 'parallel'.

सम्मान.etymology: Learned Sanskrit borrowing सम्मान (sammāna, 'high regard, honour, respect'), from सम्- + मान.

सम्मानित.etymology: सम्मानित (sammānit) is a learned borrowing (tatsama) from Sanskrit सम्मानित (sammānita, 'honoured, esteemed'), the past passive participle of the causative verb सम्-मानयति (from सम्- + मन् 'to think highly of, respect'). In Hindi it serves as a formal, warm adjective for guests of honour and distinguished elders.

सर.etymology: Borrowed from English sir ('respectful form of address to a man, guest, teacher, or senior'), shortened in Middle English from Old French sire ('lord, master'), an unstressed proclitic development of Vulgar Latin *seior < Classical Latin senior ('older, elder').

history.meaning: sir (polite address to a male guest, customer, or teacher)

सर.notes: Distinct from its Perso-Hindi homograph सर / सिर ('head'); often softened even further in polite Indian hospitality as सर जी.

सरकारी.etymology: सरकारी (sarkārī) is formed with the adjectival suffix -ई (-ī) from सरकार (sarkār, 'government, authority, estate'), borrowed from Classical Persian سرکار (sarkār, literally 'head of affairs', from سر 'head' + کار 'work, business'). In Indian administrative and everyday speech it translates 'governmental' or 'official'.

सरसराना.etymology: सरसराना (sarsarānā) is a reduplicated onomatopoeic verb built on the sound-imitative syllable सर्र / सर- (sar-, 'rustle, whoosh'), mimicking the soft hiss of wind through dry leaves, silk, or paper. Adding the verbalizing suffix -आना to a reduplicated sound stem is a classic Hindi pattern for continuous auditory verbs (compare खटखटाना and झिलमिलाना).

history.meaning: soft rustling sound of wind or leaves

सर्दी.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian سردی (sardī, 'coldness, winter'), from سرد (sard, 'cold').

सर्र.etymology: सर्र (sarr) is a native Hindi onomatopoeic exclamation imitating the crisp, swift rushing sound of wind, sliding paper, or sudden movement. Its geminate final -र्र conveys abruptness and speed, and it serves as the auditory root behind related verbs like सरसराना ('to rustle').

सलीक़ा.etymology: सलीक़ा (salīqā) entered Hindi via Classical Persian سلیقه (salīqa) from Arabic سليقة (salīqa, 'natural disposition, innate good taste, knack, refined manner'). In Hindi-Urdu it specialized toward neatness, good taste, and proper etiquette, and inflects like native -आ masculine nouns to give the everyday adverbial phrase सलीक़े से ('neatly').

सलीक़ेदार.etymology: सलीक़ेदार (salīqedār) is a Persian-style compound adjective formed in Hindustani from सलीक़े (oblique stem of सलीक़ा, 'neatness, tact', from Arabic سليقة) and the Persian possessive suffix -दार (-dār, 'having'). It describes people, arrangements, or plans marked by orderliness and grace.

सवा.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit सपाद (sapāda, 'with a quarter'), from स- ('with') + पाद ('foot, quarter').

rootFamily.gloss: a quarter to; minus a quarter (−¼)
half past; plus a half (with numbers 3 and above)

सही.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic صَحِيح (ṣaḥīḥ, 'sound, true, authentic, correct'), via Classical Persian صحیح (sahīh -> sahī).

सही-सलामत.etymology: Paired Arabo-Persian phrase combining सही (ṣaḥīḥ, 'sound') + सलामत (salāmat, 'safe, unharmed').

सा.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit सम (sama, 'like, equal, similar'), via Prakrit सअ / सा, reduced to an enclitic degree particle.

rootFamily.gloss: a little; some; a few (in plural)

साँचा.etymology: साँचा (sānchā) descends from Sanskrit सञ्चक (sañcaka, 'mould, stamp, impression') via Prakrit संचअ (sañcaa, 'mould'). The nasal+palatal cluster -ञ्च- simplified in Hindi to -च- with lengthening and nasalization of the preceding vowel, yielding साँच-. It denotes any hollow mould used in baking, brickmaking, or metalwork.

साँस.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit श्वास (śvāsa, 'breath, sigh, respiration'), via Prakrit सास (sāsa) with nasalisation.

सागवान.etymology: Inherited/regional Indo-Aryan timber name सागवान (sāgvān, Tectona grandis), connected to Sanskrit शाक (śāka, 'teak tree').

सागौन.etymology: सागौन (sāgaun) derives from Sanskrit शाक (śāka, 'the teak tree, Tectona grandis') and Prakrit साग / सागवण (sāgavaṇa, from शाकवन 'teak-wood'), also giving Marathi सागवान. Widely prized across India for furniture, ships, and architectural joinery, सागौन refers to seasoned teak timber.

साझेदारी.etymology: Hybrid Indo-Persian formation: Hindi साझा ('share, joint venture') + Persian -दारी (-dārī, 'holding').

rootFamily.gloss: with; together with (के साथ); together (एक साथ)

साढ़े.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit सार्ध (sārdha, 'with a half, plus one half'), from स- ('with') + अर्ध ('half').

सात.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit सप्त (sapta, 'seven'), via Prakrit सत्त (satta), from PIE *septḿ̥.

साथ.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit सार्थ (sārtha, 'company, caravan, accompanying'), via Prakrit सत्थ (sattha).

rootFamily.gloss: near (के पास); in one's possession ('to have')

साथ-साथ.etymology: साथ-साथ (sāth-sāth) is the distributive reduplication of साथ (sāth, 'company, accompaniment'), which descends from Sanskrit सार्थ (sārtha, 'caravan, company of travellers, companion') via Prakrit सत्थ (sattha). Repeating the word reinforces simultaneity or walking side by side.

rootFamily.gloss: with; together with (के साथ); together (एक साथ)
near (के पास); in one's possession ('to have')

साथी.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit सार्थिक (sārthika, 'fellow traveller, companion'), from सार्थ ('caravan, company').

rootFamily.gloss: with; together with (के साथ); together (एक साथ)

सादा.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian ساده (sāda, 'plain, smooth, unadorned'), from Middle Persian sādag.

rootFamily.gloss: light (in weight, flavour, sound, or brightness); gentle

साफ़.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic صَافٍ / صَافِي (ṣāfī, 'pure, clear, limpid, clean'), via Classical Persian صاف (sāf).

साफ़-साफ़.etymology: साफ़-साफ़ (sāf-sāf) is an intensive reduplication of the adjective साफ़ (sāf, 'clean, clear, distinct'), which entered Hindi via Persian صاف from Arabic صافٍ (ṣāfin, 'pure, clear, unclouded'). Repeating the adjective turns it into a crisp manner adverb meaning 'clearly, legibly, or candidly'.

साबुन.etymology: Entered Hindustani via Classical Persian صابون (sābūn) / Arabic صَابُون and reinforced by Portuguese sabão, all tracing back to Latin sāpō ('soap').

सामने.etymology: सामने (sāmne) descends from Sanskrit संमुखेन / संमुख (sammukha, 'facing, confronting', literally 'with face together', from सम्- + मुख 'face') via Prakrit संमुह / सामुहे (sammuha). The medial cluster simplified with lengthening of the first vowel and oblique -ए marking its adverbial/postpositional role.

rootFamily.gloss: ahead; forward; further on; in front (के आगे)

सामान.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian سامان (sāmān, 'equipment, household goods, order, luggage').

सारा.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit सर्व (sarva, 'all, whole, entire'), via Prakrit सब्ब / सार (sāra).

साल.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian سال (sāl, 'year'), from Middle Persian sāl.

सालगिरह.etymology: सालगिरह (sālgirah) is a Classical Persian compound سالگره (sālgereh), combining سال (sāl, 'year') and گره (gereh, 'knot'). It literally refers to the traditional custom of tying a knot on a cord each year to count a person's age or mark each passing year. In Hindi-Urdu it serves as the warm everyday word for an anniversary or birthday.

सालाना.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian سالانه (sālāna, 'yearly, annual'), from سال (sāl, 'year') + suffix -انه.

साहब.etymology: साहब (sāhab) entered Hindi via Classical Persian صاحب (ṣāḥib) from Arabic صاحب (ṣāḥib, 'companion, owner, master, sir'). In South Asia it evolved into a universal term of respectful address and a polite suffix added to names or titles such as डॉक्टर साहब and मोहन साहब.

सिक्का.etymology: सिक्का (sikkā) entered Hindi via Classical Persian سکه (sekka / sikka) from Arabic سكة (sikka, 'coining die, stamped coin'). The Arabic word originally meant the iron die used to stamp metal currency before shifting to the stamped coin itself. In Hindi it inflects regularly as a masculine -आ noun (सिक्के).

सिखाना.etymology: Causative in -आना from सीखना ('to learn'), inherited from Sanskrit शिक्षयति (śikṣayati, 'teaches, instructs') via Prakrit सिक्खावेइ.

सितारा.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian ستاره (sitāra, 'star'), from Middle Persian stārag, from PIE *h₂stḗr.

सिर.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit शिरस् (śiras, 'head, summit'), via Prakrit सिर (sira), from PIE *ḱérh₂s.

rootFamily.gloss: mouth; face; spout / opening of a vessel

सिरहाना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit शिरोधान (śirodhāna, 'head-rest, pillow-end of a bed'), from शिरस् ('head') + धान ('place, receptacle').

सिरा.etymology: सिरा (sirā) derives from Sanskrit शिरस् / शिरा (śiras, 'head, top, tip, extremity') via Prakrit सिरअ (siraa). As palatal श- shifted to dental स- in Hindi, सिर came to mean 'head' while the -आ extended form सिरा specialized for the tip, end, or extremity of a cord, cloth, or road.

सिर्फ़.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic صِرْف (ṣirf, 'pure, unmixed, mere, sheer'), via Classical Persian صرف (sirf, 'only').

सीट.etymology: सीट (sīṭ) is borrowed from English 'seat', which entered Middle English from Old Norse 'sæti' ('seat, sitting place', related to Old English 'sittan'). In Indian transport, theatre, and event contexts it is fully naturalized as a feminine noun taking the plural सीटें.

सीढ़ी.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit श्रेणी / श्रि ('series, ladder, flight of steps'), via Prakrit सिड्ढी (siḍḍhī).

rootFamily.gloss: floor / storey of a building; destination

सीधा.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit सिद्ध (siddha, 'accomplished, direct, straight'), via Prakrit सिद्ध (siddha).

rootFamily.gloss: to fold; to bend; to turn

सुंदर.etymology: Learned Sanskrit borrowing (tatsama) सुन्दर (sundara, 'beautiful, lovely, noble').

सुकून.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian سکون (sukūn) from Arabic سُكُون (sukūn, 'stillness, calm, serenity'), from root س-ك-ن ('to dwell, be still').

सुखाना.etymology: सुखाना (sukhānā) is the transitive causative verb derived from सूखना (sūkhnā, 'to become dry'), which descends from Sanskrit शुष्यति (śuṣyati, 'dries up', past participle शुष्क śuṣka) via Prakrit सुक्खइ (sukkhai). Adding the causative -आ- suffix regularly shortens the long stem vowel ऊ to उ, producing सुखाना.

सुधा.etymology: From Sanskrit सुधा (sudhā, 'ambrosia, nectar'), from सु- ('good') + धा.

सुनना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit शृणोति (śṛṇoti, 'hears, listens'), via Prakrit सुणइ (suṇaï), from PIE *ḱlew- ('to hear').

rootFamily.gloss: to speak; to say; to talk

सुनहरा.etymology: Derived from सोना ('gold', from Sanskrit सुवर्ण suvarṇa 'fair-coloured, gold') + adjectival suffix -हरा.

सुनाई.etymology: Action noun in -आई formed from सुनना ('to hear, listen'), inherited from Sanskrit शृणोति.

सुनाना.etymology: सुनाना (sunānā) is the regular causative verb formed from सुनना (sunnā, 'to hear, listen'), which descends from Sanskrit शृणोति (śṛṇoti, 'hears') via Prakrit सुणइ (suṇai). Meaning literally 'to cause someone to hear', it idiomatically covers telling stories, reading letters aloud, and performing music for an audience.

सुप्रभात.etymology: Learned Sanskrit compound सुप्रभात (suprabhāta): सु- ('good, auspicious') + प्रभात ('dawn, daybreak').

rootFamily.gloss: evening (in polite greeting शुभ संध्या! 'Good evening!')

सुबह.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian صبح (subh) from Arabic صُبْح (ṣubḥ, 'dawn, morning').

सुर.etymology: Tadbhava form inherited from Sanskrit स्वर (svara, 'musical note, tone, voice'), via Prakrit सुर (sura).

सुरक्षा.etymology: Learned Sanskrit compound सुरक्षा (surakṣā): सु- ('well, thorough') + रक्षा ('protection, guarding').

सुरक्षित.etymology: Learned Sanskrit borrowing (tatsama) सुरक्षित (surakṣita, 'well-guarded, safe'), from सु- ('well') + रक्षित ('protected').

rootFamily.gloss: to save; to protect; to spare

सुलह.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic صُلْح (ṣulḥ, 'peace, reconciliation, settlement'), via Classical Persian صلح (sulh).

सुहाना.etymology: Derived from सुहाना ('to be pleasing, suit'), inherited from Sanskrit शोभन (śobhana, 'pleasing, handsome') via Prakrit सोहण.

सूँघना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit शिङ्घति (śiṅghati, 'smells, sniffs'), via Prakrit सुंघइ (suṅghaï).

सूखा.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit शुष्क (śuṣka, 'dry, parched'), via Prakrit सुक्ख (sukkha).

सूचना.etymology: सूचना (sūchnā) is a learned borrowing (tatsama) from Sanskrit सूचना (sūcanā, 'indication, intimation, notice'), derived from the verb सूचयति (sūcayati, 'points out, reveals', from सूचि 'needle, pointer'). In modern Hindi journalism and administration it is the standard word for a bulletin, notice, or piece of information.

सूची.etymology: Learned borrowing from Sanskrit सूची (sūcī, 'needle, pointer; index, list').

सूटकेस.etymology: Borrowed from late nineteenth-century English suitcase ('flat rectangular hinged travelling case originally sized to hold a dress suit'), compound of suit (via Anglo-Norman suite < Vulgar Latin *sequita 'matched set') + case (via Anglo-Norman casse < Latin capsa 'box, receptacle').

morphemes.meaning: hinged box or container (< English case)

सूटकेस.notes: Masculine in Hindi (बड़ा सूटकेस); standard word for rigid or wheeled luggage alongside अटैची ('attaché / small suitcase').

सूना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit शून्य (śūnya, 'empty, void, zero'), via Prakrit सुण्ण (suṇṇa).

cognates.meaning: ultimately calqued from Sanskrit शून्य via Arabic صِفْر

सूप.etymology: Borrowed in its culinary sense from seventeenth-century English soup, itself borrowed from French soupe ('broth poured over slices of bread; soup'), from Late Latin suppa ('bread soaked in broth'), of West Germanic origin (cognate with English sop and supper).
सूप.notes: Masculine in Hindi (गरम टमाटर का सूप, 'hot tomato soup'); in Hindi सूप पिया जाता है ('soup is drunk' with पीना rather than eaten with खाना).

सूरज.etymology: सूरज (sūraj) is the inherited semi-tatsama / tadbhava development of Sanskrit सूर्य (sūrya, 'the sun', cognate with Greek 'hēlios' and Latin 'sōl') via Prakrit सूरिय / सूरज (sūriya / sūraja). Breaking the Sanskrit cluster -र्य- into -रज- yielded the warm everyday word सूरज, which sits alongside formal सूर्य in modern Hindi.

से.etymology: Inherited from Prakrit सहुं / सइं or Sanskrit समम् ('together with') blended with ablative तो.

rootFamily.gloss: to; for; definite direct-object marker; at (times of day)
until; up to; as far as; even

सेंटीमीटर.etymology: सेंटीमीटर (senṭīmīṭar) is borrowed via English 'centimetre' from French 'centimètre', coined in 1793 from Latin 'centum' ('hundred') and Greek 'métron' ('measure'). Adopted into Indian metric measurement, carpentry, and architecture, it takes masculine grammatical gender.

सेंट्रल.etymology: सेंट्रल (senṭral) is borrowed from English 'central', derived via Old French from Latin 'centrālis' ('in the centre', from 'centrum'). In Indian railway and civic naming (such as सेंट्रल स्टेशन or सेंट्रल पार्क), it functions as an established proper place-name component.

सेकंड.etymology: Borrowed from English second, from Medieval Latin secunda.

सेब.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian سیب (sēb, 'apple'), from Middle Persian sēb.

rootFamily.gloss: sweet; pleasant (of voice, music, or scent)

सेवा.etymology: Learned borrowing from Sanskrit सेवा (sevā, 'attendance, care, service'), from root सेव् ('to attend upon').

सैकड़ों.etymology: सैकड़ों (saikaṛon) is the oblique plural collective form of सैकड़ा (saikaṛā, 'a group of a hundred, century'), which derives from Sanskrit शतक (śataka, 'a hundred', from शत 'hundred') via Prakrit सअडा / सैकड़ा. Used before nouns without a postposition, सैकड़ों expresses an indefinitely large count of 'hundreds of'.

सोचना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit शोचति (śocati, 'ponders, reflects, grieves'), via Prakrit सोचइ.

rootFamily.gloss: to understand; to realise; to figure out

सोडा.etymology: Borrowed from English soda (soda water / carbonated water).

सोना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit स्वपिति (svapiti, 'sleeps'), via Prakrit सोवइ (sovaï), from PIE *swep- ('to sleep').

सोमवार.etymology: Learned Sanskrit compound सोमवार (somavāra, 'day of the Moon / Monday').

सोलह.etymology: सोलह (solah) descends from Sanskrit षोडश (ṣoḍaśa, 'sixteen', compound of षष् 'six' + दश 'ten') through Prakrit सोळह (soḷaha). As regular in Indo-Aryan numerals, Sanskrit -ड- shifted to -ल- and -दश weakened to -ह, giving modern Hindi सोलह.

सोलहवाँ.etymology: सोलहवाँ (solahvān) is formed by adding the regular Hindi ordinal suffix -वाँ (descending from Sanskrit -तम via Prakrit -अम / -वँ) to the cardinal numeral सोलह ('sixteen', Sanskrit षोडश). Like other -वाँ ordinals from पाँचवाँ onward, it inflects for gender and case: सोलहवाँ, सोलहवीं, सोलहवें.

सौ.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit शत (śata, 'hundred'), via Prakrit सअ (saa), from PIE *ḱm̥tóm.

स्कूल.etymology: Borrowed from English school, ultimately from Greek skholḗ.

स्क्रीन.etymology: Borrowed from English screen, from Middle French escren.

स्टेशन.etymology: Borrowed from English station, from Latin statiō ('standing place').

स्टैंड.etymology: स्टैंड (sṭainḍ) is borrowed from English 'stand' (from Old English 'standan', 'to stand'). In modern Hindi it is widely used for easels, display stands, cycle stands, and bus stops, behaving as a regular consonant-final masculine noun.

स्ट्रॉबेरी.etymology: Borrowed from English strawberry, continuing Old English strēawberige (compound of strēaw 'straw' + berige 'berry', named either from the straw mulch spread beneath the runners or the tiny straw-coloured achenes flecking its red skin).
स्ट्रॉबेरी.notes: Feminine in Hindi (मीठी स्ट्रॉबेरी) because of its final long -ई (-ī), and cultivated widely in Indian hill stations such as Mahabaleshwar and Nainital.

स्थानीय.etymology: स्थानीय (sthānīya) is a learned borrowing (tatsama) from Sanskrit स्थानीय (sthānīya, 'belonging to a place, local'), derived from स्थान (sthāna, 'place, station', from स्था 'to stand') with the adjectival suffix -ईय. It is the standard Hindi adjective translating 'local' in civic, cultural, and geographical contexts.

स्थिर.etymology: Learned Sanskrit borrowing स्थिर (sthira, 'firm, steady, motionless'), from स्था ('to stand'), PIE *stéh₂-ro-.

rootFamily.gloss: to stop; to wait; to stay overnight (at an inn)

स्याही.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian سیاهی (siyāhī, 'blackness; ink'), from سیاه (siyāh, 'black').

स्लेटी.etymology: Derived from English loanword स्लेट (slate) + Hindi colour-adjective suffix -ई.

स्वभाव.etymology: Learned Sanskrit compound स्वभाव (svabhāva): स्व- ('own') + भाव ('being, nature, disposition').

rootFamily.gloss: mind; heart; mood / inclination (मन करना 'to feel like')

स्वागत.etymology: Learned Sanskrit compound स्वागत (svāgata, 'well-arrived; welcome'), from सु- ('well') + आगत ('come, arrived').

स्वाद.etymology: Learned Sanskrit borrowing स्वाद (svāda, 'taste, relish, flavour'), from स्वद् ('to taste sweet'), PIE *swéh₂dus.

rootFamily.gloss: sweet; pleasant (of voice, music, or scent)

स्वादिष्ट.etymology: Learned Sanskrit borrowing (tatsama) स्वादिष्ट / स्वादिष्ठ (svādiṣṭha, 'sweetest, most savoury'), superlative of स्वादु ('sweet, tasty', cognate with English sweet).

rootFamily.gloss: sweet; pleasant (of voice, music, or scent)

स्वेटर.etymology: Borrowed from nineteenth-century English sweater ('knitted woollen pullover', originally worn by rowers and athletes during training to induce sweating), agent/garment noun from sweat (Old English swǣtan, from Proto-Indo-European *sweyd-, cognate with Sanskrit स्वेद sveda 'sweat') + -er.

cognates.meaning: sweat, warmth (distant Indo-European cognate of sweat via PIE *sweyd-)

स्वेटर.notes: Masculine in Hindi (ऊनी स्वेटर बुनना, 'to knit a woollen sweater') and the universal North Indian winter word for pullovers and hand-knitted jumpers.

हँसाना.etymology: Causative of हँसना ('to laugh'), from Sanskrit हासयति (hāsayati, 'causes to laugh').

हज़ार.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian هزار (hazār, 'thousand'), cognate with Sanskrit सहस्र (sahasra).

हटना.etymology: Inherited from Middle Indo-Aryan हट्टइ (haṭṭaï, 'draws back, retreats').

हटाना.etymology: Causative/transitive in -आना from हटना ('to step back, move aside'), from Middle Indo-Aryan हट्टइ.

rootFamily.gloss: to put; to place; to keep

हड़बड़ाना.etymology: हड़बड़ाना (haṛbaṛānā) is a denominative verb formed from the expressive reduplicated stem हड़-बड़ (haṛ-baṛ, 'commotion, hurry, confusion'), built on Middle Indo-Aryan sound-symbolic roots mimicking clattering haste (compare गड़बड़ and धड़धड़). The -आना ending creates an expressive intransitive verb of flustered rushing.

rootFamily.gloss: to feel nervous; to panic; to get flustered
fast; heavy (rain); strong/sharp (salt, spice, sun, sound)

हड़बड़ी.etymology: हड़बड़ी (haṛbaṛī) is the feminine noun derived from the expressive stem हड़-बड़ (haṛ-baṛ, 'flustered haste, clamour') with the abstract suffix -ई. Like its verb counterpart हड़बड़ाना, it conveys both physical hurry and anxious mental confusion.

हथेली.etymology: हथेली (hathelī) derives from Sanskrit हस्ततल (hastatala, 'surface/palm of the hand', from हस्त 'hand' + तल 'flat surface') via Prakrit हत्थल्ल / हत्थेलिआ (hatthalia). The cluster -स्त- simplified to -थ- and the diminutive feminine suffix -एली yielded modern Hindi हथेली.

हफ़्ता.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian هفته (hafta, 'seven-day week'), from هفت (haft, 'seven', cognate with Sanskrit सप्तन् saptan).

हम.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit अस्मे (asme, oblique plural of अहम्), via Prakrit अम्हे (amhe, 'we'), from PIE *ṇsmé.

rootFamily.gloss: one's own (my, your, his, her, our, their)

हमेशा.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian همیشه (hamēša, 'always, continually'), from Middle Persian hamēšag.

हर.etymology: Borrowed from Classical Persian هر (har, 'every, each'), from Old Persian haruva- (cognate with Sanskrit सर्व).

rootFamily.gloss: one each; one by one; every single

हरा.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit हरित (harita, 'green, verdant, yellowish-green'), via Prakrit हरिअ (haria).

rootFamily.gloss: small leaf; herb leaf; tea leaf

हल्का.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit लघुक (laghuka, 'light, swift, slight'), via Prakrit हलुअ (halua) with metathesis of l and h.

rootFamily.gloss: slow; low; soft/quiet (of voice or light)

हवा.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian هوا (hawā) from Arabic هَوَاء (hawāʾ, 'air, atmosphere, breeze').

हवेली.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian حویلی (hawēlī) from Arabic حَوَالَيْ (ḥawālay, 'surrounding enclosure, courtyard residence').

हस्तांतरण.etymology: Learned Sanskrit compound हस्तान्तरण (hastāntaraṇa, literally 'passing from one hand to another').

हस्ताक्षर.etymology: हस्ताक्षर (hastākshar) is a learned borrowing (tatsama) from Sanskrit हस्ताक्षर (hastākṣara, 'one's own handwriting, signature'), compounding हस्त (hasta, 'hand') and अक्षर (akṣara, 'letter, syllable'). Literally 'hand-letters', it became the standard formal Hindi word for a personal signature, sitting alongside the Persian-derived दस्तख़त.

हाँ.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit आम् (ām, 'yes, indeed'), with expressive initial h- and nasalisation in Prakrit आम / हँ -> हाँ.

हाज़िर.etymology: हाज़िर (hāzir) entered Hindi via Classical Persian حاضر (ḥāẓir) from Arabic حاضر (ḥāḍir, 'present, at hand, attending'), the active participle of حضر (ḥaḍara, 'to be present'). In Hindi-Urdu it is used both for physical attendance and politely when presenting tea, tools, or service.

rootFamily.gloss: right now; just now; still / yet

हाथ.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit हस्त (hasta, 'hand'), via Prakrit हत्थ (hattha) with compensatory vowel lengthening.

rootFamily.gloss: to shake; to move; to wiggle

हाथीदाँत.etymology: हाथीदाँत (hāthīdānt) is a native Hindi descriptive compound combining हाथी (hāthī, 'elephant', from Sanskrit हस्तिन्) and दाँत (dānt, 'tooth, tusk', from Sanskrit दन्त). Literally 'elephant tusk', it functions as a calque/equivalent of English 'ivory' for both the material and the warm creamy off-white shade.

हादसा.etymology: हादसा (hādsā) entered Hindi via Classical Persian حادثه (ḥādisa) from Arabic حادثة (ḥāditha, 'occurrence, event, accident'), the feminine active participle of حدث (ḥadatha, 'to happen, occur newly'). In Hindi it was integrated into the masculine -आ noun class (plural हादसे) and came to refer specifically to an unexpected mishap or accident.

हामी.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic حَامٍ (ḥāmin, 'supporter, defender'), via Persian حامی (hāmī), idiomatised in हामी भरना.

rootFamily.gloss: to accept; to agree; (हार मानना) to give up

हाय.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit हा (hā, 'alas! oh!'), extended to हाय in Middle and Modern Indo-Aryan.

rootFamily.gloss: oh!; hey!; wait a moment! (surprise or sudden realisation)
Ram (invoked in mild everyday exclamations like हाय राम!)

हार.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit हार (hāra, 'loss, deprivation'), from हृ; paired with जीत ('victory').

rootFamily.gloss: to lose; (हिम्मत हारना) to lose heart

हारना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit हारयति (hārayati, 'loses, forfeits'), via Prakrit हारइ.

rootFamily.gloss: defeat; giving up (हार मानना 'to give up, admit defeat')

हार्डवेयर.etymology: Borrowed from English hardware ('metal tools and plumbing fittings').

हाल.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian حال (hāl) from Arabic حَال (ḥāl, 'state, condition, present circumstance').

rootFamily.gloss: for now; at present; for the moment

हिम्मत.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic هِمَّة (himma, 'resolve, high spirit, courage'), via Classical Persian همت (himmat).

rootFamily.gloss: defeat; giving up (हार मानना 'to give up, admit defeat')

हिलना.etymology: हिलना (hilnā) descends from Sanskrit हिल्लति / हल्लति (hillati / hallati, 'rocks, swings, moves') via Prakrit हिल्लइ (hillai). The geminate -ल्ल- simplified to single -ल- in modern Hindi. It forms a clean intransitive-transitive pair with हिलाना ('to shake or wave something').

rootFamily.gloss: to shake; to move; to wiggle

हिलाना.etymology: Causative/transitive in -आना from हिलना ('to move, sway, shake'), from Prakrit हिल्लइ (hillaï).

हिसाब.etymology: Borrowed via Classical Persian حساب (hisāb) from Arabic حِسَاب (ḥisāb, 'reckoning, calculation, account').

हिस्सा.etymology: Borrowed from Arabic حِصَّة (ḥiṣṣa, 'share, portion, lot'), via Classical Persian حصه (hissa).

ही.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit हि (hi, 'indeed, surely, for'), preserved across Prakrit हि -> ही.

rootFamily.gloss: then (after अगर/जब); as for (topic/contrast); why don't you!

हीटर.etymology: Borrowed from English heater ('appliance that warms a room or water'), instrument noun formed from heat (Old English hǣtu 'warmth, heat', Proto-Germanic *haitį̄) + -er.

history.meaning: electric room heater or coil stove

हीटर.notes: Masculine in Hindi (कमरे में हीटर चलाना, 'to turn on the heater in the room'), essential during crisp North Indian winter nights.

हुक.etymology: हुक (huk) is borrowed from English 'hook', descending from Old English 'hōc' ('curved piece of metal, hook'). In Indian hardware, reception desks, and households it sits alongside खूँटी specifically for metal wall hooks and key pegs, taking masculine gender.

हे.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit हे (he, vocative interjection 'O!').

rootFamily.gloss: oh!; hey!; wait a moment! (surprise or sudden realisation)
God; the Lord (भगवान का शुक्र है! 'Thank goodness!')

हैंडल.etymology: Borrowed from English handle, from Old English handle.

rootFamily.gloss: to lift; to pick up; to wake up

हैटबॉक्स.etymology: हैटबॉक्स (haiṭboks) is borrowed from English 'hatbox', compounding 'hat' (Old English 'hætt') and 'box' (Late Latin 'buxis'). Adopted into travel and luggage vocabulary in Hindi as a single compound borrowing, it takes masculine grammatical gender.

history.meaning: fitted box for carrying a hat

हैलो.etymology: Borrowed from English hello (also spelled हेलो), which rose to global prominence in the late nineteenth century (championed by Thomas Edison for telephone switchboards) from earlier English hallo / hollo, an expressive hailing call used to draw attention across a distance.

history.meaning: call to attract attention -> standard telephone and social greeting
hello! (especially on answering the phone or getting someone's attention)

हैलो.notes: Universal across India when picking up a telephone call, while face-to-face greetings warmly pair or alternate it with नमस्ते.

हॉल.etymology: Borrowed from English hall ('large public auditorium, concert hall, or spacious central living room'), descending from Old English heall and Proto-Germanic *hallō ('covered lofty chamber, hall', from Proto-Indo-European *ḱel- 'to cover, shelter', cognate with Sanskrit शाला śālā 'hall, house').

history.meaning: great roofed chamber -> auditorium, entrance or living hall
concert or cinema auditorium; central drawing room of a flat

cognates.meaning: hall, large room (distant Indo-European cognate via PIE *ḱel-)

हॉल.notes: In Indian English and Hindi housing (e.g. '2 BHK' — bedroom, hall, kitchen), हॉल also means the main family living room, alongside public concert and cinema halls.

होटल.etymology: Borrowed from English hotel, adapted in the eighteenth century from French hôtel ('town mansion; travellers' inn'), which evolved through Old French ostel from Medieval Latin hospitāle ('guesthouse, hospice', neuter substantive of Classical Latin hospitālis 'hospitable, of a guest', from hospes 'guest, host').

history.meaning: establishment providing lodging and meals to travellers
hotel (and colloquially also a roadside restaurant or eatery)

rootFamily.gloss: hospital (older borrowing from the same Latin root hospitāle)
student hostel (parallel doublet from Old French ostel)

होटल.notes: Masculine in Hindi; note that in everyday Indian usage होटल can mean either a lodging hotel or a casual neighbourhood restaurant.

होना.etymology: Inherited from Sanskrit भवति (bhavati, 'is, becomes, happens'), via Prakrit होइ (hoï), from PIE *bʰuH- ('to become, be').

rootFamily.gloss: to stay; to live; progressive marker (रहा/रही/रहे)
to be made; to turn out; to become

हौज़.etymology: हौज़ (hauz) entered Hindi via Classical Persian حوض (ḥauẓ) from Arabic حوض (ḥawḍ, 'cistern, water basin, reservoir, pool'). Widely used in North Indian and Rajasthani haveli architecture for carved stone fountain basins and courtyard water tanks (including famous place names like दिल्ली का हौज़ ख़ास), it takes masculine gender.
